title: Todd Monken Finally Shares When Browns Will Learn Preseason Starting Quarterback
full_text:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken is keeping his quarterback plans very close to the chest.
But on Wednesday, the first-time head coach told reporters that he will inform Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders of which one of them is going to start Saturday’s preseason game against the Chicago Bears after practice.
Monken has already decided whether Watson or Sanders will start the preseason opener, but both quarterbacks will get the message from their head coach later Wednesday afternoon.
The preseason games will be significant for this competition. Throughout the first dozen training camp practices, Watson has more reps with the starting offense. But the 30-year-old veteran has also thrown more interceptions than Sanders, who has consistently developed over the course of the offseason.
Watson and Sanders will each start a preseason game for the Browns. It’s likely that a formal announcement of who won the competition could happen after Cleveland’s second preseason game.
Against the Bears, the starting offensive is likely to play the first drive. It’s possible that the starting quarterback could play the first half of each preseason game.
Monken’s decision will boil down to which quarterback he believes will give the Browns the best chance to win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.
Watson has more snaps with the starting offense so far because of Saturday’s switch in the rotation. Since spring practices, Monken has been alternating days between Watson and Sanders with the starters. But on Saturday, Watson was awarded a second-straight day of reps with the starting offense, snapping the cycle and giving him more reps than Sanders overall.
A big area of focus in this particular competition is which quarterback can efficiently run the entire operation. Monken’s offense puts a lot on the plate for quarterbacks, so Cleveland’s pre-snap operation needs to be flawless before the 60-year-old head coach names a starter.
Neither quarterback has run away with this competition, which makes the preseason even more intriguing for the Browns. There’s no telling how much Monken will honestly factor in preseason performance during the evaluation of these quarterbacks, but it’s certainly the next step in the process.
After this preseason opener in Chicago, Cleveland’s joint practice with the Buffalo Bills on Thursday August 20 will be the next big check-in on this competition. After that practice, the Browns will host the Bills for a preseason game. From there, it’s anyone’s guess as to when Monken could name his Week 1 starting quarterback.

title: Browns Host Another Free Agent Edge Rusher Knowing Defensive Line Is Thin
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns might have real depth issues on the defensive line heading into the preseason and are looking to add a player to help fill in that void.
With the injury bug making its way through training camp on defense for the Browns, they need to address the issue as soon as possible. One way the Browns are looking to address it is by adding a free agent edge rusher.
After Cleveland hosted Jadeveon Clowney a couple of weeks ago, it was clear that the Browns wanted to add a player to fix their depth issues. Now, free agent edge rusher Tyus Bowser is working out with the team on Wednesday.
Veteran edge Tyus Bowser, who last played for the Miami Dolphins in 2024, worked out today for the Cleveland Browns.
It’s clear that the Browns are interested in bringing in a veteran on the defensive line to fill in after recent injuries have limited their current players. Here’s what signing Bowser would mean in regard to Cleveland’s lack of depth.
There has been a plethora of training camp injuries that have led to the Browns defensive line being so thin, none that are threatening as of now, but it’s still an issue either way.
Over the last week of training camp, the Browns have had to mix some things up by upgrading some of their second and third team players to the first team defense. That was when it became glaringly obvious there was a depth issue.
Now, with Tyus Bowser visiting Cleveland and working out for the team, it seems like they’re more than willing to sign a player or two to help with that heading into the preseason. This will give their coaching staff a better idea of what they have to work with before the regular season.
Bowser hasn’t played a regular season game since the 2024 season when he was with the Miami Dolphins but has had a productive career even after being unsigned last season.
It’s been since 2021 that Bowser played a full season and hasn’t put up near the defensive numbers since his time with the Baltimore Ravens. In 2021, Bowser had 59 total tackles, 33 solo tackles, with seven sacks and two forced fumbles.
That was by far his best season of his eight-year career and had only mustered two sacks the following season before seeing a significant drop off in production and playing time.
Now at age 31, Bowser is still looking to make an impact in any given role with an NFL team, and his next may be the Cleveland Browns. If his workout goes well, he could wind up helping out on their thin defensive line that is still missing a few key players at training camp.
Bowser’s signing would allow for players like Adin Huntington and Elijah Chatman to continue seeing reps at defensive tackle while Mike Hall Jr. continues to work back from injury.
Maliek Collins is still on the PUP list, so this saga could continue into the regular season, but all eyes are on the preseason first. Cleveland’s first preseason game is this Saturday against the Chicago Bears, with kickoff scheduled for 1:00 p.m.

title: 7 Big Takeaways From Cleveland Browns' First Preseason Depth Chart
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 Preseason, and as expected, there were a few surprises.
As announced earlier by head coach Todd Monken, the quarterback position was going to show two co-starters, while a trio of rookies are slotted with the starting unit on offense.
Here are seven takeaways from the first installment of the Browns’ unofficial depth chart:
John Madden used to famously say, “if you have two quarterbacks, you have none.“
Nowhere has this proven to be more accurate than with these Browns, still undecided on who will be the starter come Week 1 of the regular season.
Head coach Todd Monken has promised Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders one start each in the preseason , but if Cleveland is really waiting until after August 22nd to make a call, how much preparation will the eventual starter get before the regular season opener, without having to look over his shoulder and being able to really focus on the task at hand?
The scales were always tipped towards the offense, after the team went offense-heavy in last April’s draft, including their top three picks. Now, said top three draftees are penciled in as starters -- Spencer Fano as left tackle, and KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston as wide receivers.
Fano’s inclusion among the starters is especially noteworthy, since it comes a few days after Monken shared that the team was considering staying with Dawand Jones, in case he wasn’t ready for the starting role. A training camp fight against Jared Verse helped change Monken’s mind about Fano’s readiness.
Even though Monken maintained from the very beginning that his preference was having Elgton Jenkins at guard, the team has him as the team’s starting center, with Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston battling it out for the right guard spot. Monken shared that Jenkins had the edge over Leveston thanks to experience, which would explain why he’s listed as the current starter, though there still might be some changes here.
Cleveland drafted two tight ends this year, and both of them are listed way on the deep end of the depth chart. It might be hard for the Browns to make room for both of them on the practice squad.
The starting foursome consisting of Verse and Alex Wright on the outside, paired with Mason Graham with Maliek Collins -- who’s on the PUP list -- on the inside, doesn’t really inspire awe. But things get more concerning once you get to the second and third stringers. Having the end positions manned by Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara and UDFAs Logan Fano and Khordae Sydnore, while the interior is handled by backups Mike Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Sam Kamara, Adin Huntington and UDFA Tyreak Sapp, just feels like a scream for help from the outside.
Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams were always going to be starters for Cleveland, and chances are they’ll be the two linebackers on the field when the Browns go to nickel alignment. But having Cleveland list Easton Mascarenas-Arnold as the third starter is a nice surprise, overtaking Nathaniel Watson, Winston Reid and rookie Justin Jefferson for that spot. That position battle has flown under the radar, understandably, but it does feel like a tight one.
With teams spending so much time in nickel and big nickel formations, it’s become increasingly popular to see depth charts listing five starting DBs instead of four.
Cleveland didn’t take this route, sticking with Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell at the corners, and Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman as safeties. This left second-round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren -- who’s expected to play a lot in three safety looks -- as a second stringer, along with presumptive nickel corner Myles Harden.
Like with the offensive backfield, expect the team to shed a lot of weight from their offseason 90-man roster here.

title: Jaydon Blue Has a Problem That Could Cost Him Cowboys RB2 Job
full_text:
A fifth-round pick out of Texas in 2025, Jaydon Blue hardly saw the field during his rookie season. Entering year two, however, he's been given every opportunity to secure the RB2 spot with the Dallas Cowboys.
By all accounts, he seems to be making a strong case for himself . Every practice seems to bring another Jaydon Blue highlight where he rips off a run for at least 40 yards. That explosion out of the backfield was the only thing missing from this offense last year, which is why so many eyes have been on Blue.
Unfortunately, his spot on the team might not be as secure as it seems. According to Cowboys beat reporter Nick Eatman, Blue has had serious issues with fumbles. Eatman said Blue has put the ball on the ground often, including multiple times in the joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams. That led to Eatman saying that Blue could be in danger of losing his spot, while adding that Dallas could be looking elsewhere for a No. 2 back behind Javonte Williams by the time the regular season rolls around.
"He's made some plays, but then again, you know, Bill Parcells, he said all the time, no running back's worth fumbles. Not any running back is worth a fumble. And so, you know, if he's going to lay it on the ground, you know, that was an issue he had in college," Eatman said while appearing on 105.3 The Fan .
"It happened in his practices and with the Rams a couple of times, you know, so he's...he's got to hang on to the ball. He's got to do all the little things. And I just think it's close between some of the other guys. I mean, (Israel) Abanikanda, to me, is as complete of a running back as they have. And I'm not sure that the No. 2 running back is even on the roster at this point."
Last year, Dallas had Miles Sanders as the No. 2 back but when he suffered a knee injury, it was Malik Davis who came out of nowhere to secure that spot. Could the same thing happen in 2026 with Israel Abanikanda?
A fifth-round pick out of Pitt in 2023, Abanikanda began his career with the New York Jets and had 70 yards on 22 rushing attempts as a rookie. He has yet to see the field in the regular season since then and has bounced around the league.
He signed with Dallas last November and was instantly seen as a solid fit for Klayton Adams' running scheme. Eatman's claim that he has been one of the best all-around backs is interesting and makes Abanikanda a name to watch this weekend as the Cowboys take on the Seattle Seahawks in the preseason opener. If he rises to the occasion, he has a chance to be this year's version of Malik Davis.

title: The Good & Not So Good From Dallas Cowboys Practice: Shavon Revel Jr. Shines Again
full_text:
After a solid outing in the joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams earlier this week, the Dallas Cowboys are looking to use that momentum headed into the preseason opener against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on Saturday.
The Cowboys got one of their final chances to do just that after wrapping up Thursday's training camp practice in Oxnard.
Dallas will likely go through walk-throughs on Friday before heading to Seattle, so here are the positives and negatives from the last true look fans got of the Cowboys ahead of the preseason.
Like they did in the joint practice with the Rams, the Cowboys defense had another strong day against the pass on Thursday, hauling in three interceptions.
This included picks from Markquese Bell, DJ Withers and Curtis Robinson, along with multiple pass breakups from other players.
Caleb Downs almost came down with an interception of his own on a Dak Prescott throw to the sideline but he couldn't reel in the ball while trying to get both feet inbounds.
Christian Parker's defense continues to have a strong training camp but will face its first real test against the Seahawks on Saturday.
While Prescott and Sam Howell's interceptions came from a deep pass and a tipped ball, respectively, Joe Milton III showed didn't exactly help his cause for the backup quarterback job.
He threw an interception right in the middle of the field to Curtis Robinson, almost as if he didn't see him there at the linebacker spot.
Milton has had his ups and downs during training camp but the interception marked another low point. He will have a chance to build momentum against the Seahawks.
What more can be said about Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. that hasn't already been said during training camp?
The second-year jump continues to look alive and well, as Revel had two impressive pass breakups during Thursday's practice, one against George Pickens and the other against Ryan Flournoy.
It appears Revel's pairing with Christian Parker will be taking his game to a new level in 2026.
Here's a look at his PBU against Pickens:
George Pickens wanted a flag on this Shavon Revel PBU. Didn’t get one. pic.twitter.com/BRY99xFXRQ
While the defense's pass coverage was no doubt a positive, the other side of that coin should focus on the offense's inconsistency.
Regardless of who the quarterback was, the Dallas defense was getting hands on the ball during multiple plays. Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel Jr., Dee Winters, Caleb Downs and James Houston all had PBUs.
This is great news for the Cowboys defense but the offense will need to sharpen things up as the clear stronger unit of the two.
Many of the team's young wide receivers are looking to break through and earn a 53-man roster spot despite the Cowboys already being deep at the position.
Traeshon Holden, Camden Brown and Anthony Smith all got busy during the scrimmage portion of practice. Brown even got some action with the starters and caught a short pass from Dak Prescott.
The preseason will be massive for all three of these players.
Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham continues to sit out with a groin injury.
He's working his way back in order to play against Seattle, but the fact he wasn't out there on Thursday creates some doubt about whether or not he will play against Seattle.
Regardless, the injury is not one that the team has any concern about.

title: Dallas Cowboys Injury Report For Final Practice Before NFL Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have had an eventful week, which was highlighted by a joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams and will wrap up with the team's first game of the NFL preseason.
But first, the team returned to the practice field in Oxnard on Thursday afternoon for the final session before heading to Seattle for the preseason opener against the Seahawks at Lumen Field on Saturday night.
While the Cowboys have been able to avoid any serious injuries throughout the first few weeks of camp, there are some notable players who have been banged up ahead of Saturday night's primetime game. Among those players is rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham , who has been one of the surprise standouts for the team in training camp .
Barham has missed the past few practice sessions after suffering a groin injury, but it is not believed to be major. According to Cowboys insider Todd Archer, Barham " is improving but not ready for full return ."
Along with Barham, cornerback Devin Moore and defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard are also dealing with groin injuries. Moore has been showing improvement and is working his way back into practice.
Another cornerback, Zion Childress, is dealing with a hamstring issue, while veteran wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling missed Thursday's session with a knee issue.
Marquez Valdes-Scantling (knee) is out today #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/qT0VALpWI2
The most concerning of the injuries is Valdes-Scantling. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer informed reporters before Thursday's session that the pass catcher would be sent for an MRI . MVS has been competing for the team's WR4 job.
We will have to see how long he remains sidelined, but missing extended time would be a major blow to his chances of carving on a role in the team's offense for 2026. Let's hope he can return sooner rather than later.
Dallas will travel to Seattle on Friday before suiting up in primetime on Saturday night. Kickoff between the Cowboys and Seahawks is set for 8:00 p.m. ET on the NFL Network.

title: Dallas Cowboys Reveal Preseason Plan For Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence
full_text:
The new-look Dallas Cowboys are days away from kicking off their three-game slate in the 2026 NFL preseason , with the opener set for Saturday, August 15, against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field.
Dallas enters the 2026 campaign with several new faces on the defensive side of the ball, including first-round picks Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence .
While the Cowboys made some important moves throughout the offseason, fans will have to wait until the regular season to see them in live game action. That's because head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed that a majority of the team's starters will not suit up in the preseason .
“We’re not going to play a lot of our starters during the preseason,” Schottenheimer said earlier this month. “There’s something to the young guys playing a little bit, and we do it in the first two games. I think that’s part of it. Usually, you don’t play many of those guys in the third preseason game, but it’s something that we’re very serious about.”
That means fans may have to wait to get a full look at Downs patrolling the secondary, but there still may be a slight sneak peek during the team's first two preseason games. Schottenheimer revealed those plans when speaking to the media ahead of the team's return to practice in Oxnard on Thursday afternoon.
Both Downs and Lawrence have been impressive during the first few weeks of training camp, so it would be nice to see how the rookies perform in their first taste of NFL action. But because the players are expected to be contributors this season, we may only get a glimpse.
According to Cowboys insider Tommy Yarrish, Schottenheimer expects the first-round picks to “play a little bit.” As for who else will get a look during the preseason as the team works its way down to a 53-man roster, that plan is still being developed.
After opening the preseason on Saturday, August 15, the Cowboys will travel to Phoenix for a showdown with the Arizona Cardinals the following week. Then, after a return to Texas, Dallas will cap off the preseason by hosting the Seattle Seahawks at AT&T Stadium.
Whatever plan the team puts into place turns out to be, let's just hope the Cowboys can enter the 2026 season with a healthy roster.

title: Dallas Cowboys Look To End Alarming Trend in NFL Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are just days away from kicking off their NFL preseason schedule , with a primetime Saturday showdown against the Seattle Seahawks set to get things underway. It will be our first real look at the revamped roster in a game situation, as fans eagerly wait to see whether the chatter about the new-look defense is legit .
Dallas has received a lot of hype throughout the preseason thanks to its offseason changes, headlined by the hiring of defensive coordinator Christian Parker , and now it's time to put everything on display.
While the Cowboys enter the preseason with more hype than a year ago, which was Brian Schottenheimer's first year as a head coach, the team will need to overcome some recent demons in Week 1 of the preseason.
As pointed out by Blogging the Boys , it has been nearly a decade since the Cowboys won their first game of the preseason. Since 2018, the Cowboys have not won a Week 1 preseason game, and it won't be any easier in 2026 against the reigning Super Bowl champions.
Dallas has also confirmed that starters will not play in the preseason, so that's another hurdle for the team to face.
Of course, the preseason isn't necessarily about winning and losing. It's about evaluating the roster, and the Cowboys have a lot of crucial decisions to make over the next few weeks as the team cuts down to its 53-man roster .
Finding the players who can help the most when the games matter next month is the main goal, but it'd be nice to see the Cowboys start the new season on a high note and gain some momentum under ahead of what will hopefully be a bounce-back season and return to the NFL Playoffs.

title: Javonte Williams' Confidence in Cowboys Triggers Unhinged Response From Commanders CB
full_text:
Javonte Williams might have inadvertently given the Dallas Cowboys' opponents some bulletin board material.
The star running back recently said the Cowboys were at the top of their division , a feeling that seems to be shared by many. We even dove into a prediction that they will take the NFC East crown by way of tiebreaker over the Philadelphia Eagles.
Still, opposing teams can be offended if they feel overlooked and that could very well be the case with Washington Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson. The veteran cornerback, who signed with the Commanders this offseason, took exception to Williams’ words and fired back with a strong take of his own.
“We’ll see: Sometimes the loudest man, is always the weakest man. You see, I ain’t speak on all that. You see, we’re going to chop wood and carry water. We’re going to put the work in behind the scenes, man, continue getting better and we’re gonna shine when the lights are bright,” Robertson said via Josina Anderson .
A fourth-round pick out of Louisiana Tech, Robertson spent four years with the Las Vegas Raiders before heading to the Detroit Lions the past two seasons. Williams, a second-round pick out of North Carolina in 2021, signed with the Cowboys in 2025 following a four-year stint with the Denver Broncos.
He had a breakout campaign with Dallas , rushing for 1,201 yards and 11 touchdowns. That led to Williams signing a three-year $24 million contract this offseason.
Both the Cowboys and Commanders enter the 2026 campaign with plenty to prove. The Cowboys, in their first season under head coach Brian Schottenheimer, went 7-9-1 and failed to make the playoffs for the second year in a row.
Washington had worse struggles, going 5-12. This was especially frustrating for them after they were 12-5 the prior year and made the NFC Championship Game in Dan Quinn’s first season as their head coach. Injuries to quarterback Jayden Daniels contributed to their struggles and they hope a return to health will allow them to play with more efficiency.
That said, both teams need to prove they can hang with the Philadelphia Eagles, who have won the NFC East the past two seasons and were the team to knock Washington out of the playoffs during their recent run.

title: Cowboys Predicted to Finish on Top of NFC East Despite Eagles Tie
full_text:
Hopes are high for the Dallas Cowboys following a busy offseason. The Cowboys were one of the worst defenses in the NFL a year ago and Jerry Jones vowed to get that fixed.
Jones backed up his words with actions as Dallas hired new defensive coordinator Christian Parker and then tweaked the roster to fit Parker’s vision.
We have yet to see the new-look defense in a regular season game but the early buzz during training camp has been very positive. That includes an impressive joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams where the Dallas defense made its fair share of plays against an explosive offense.
The potential is clearly there on defense and even if it takes them time to find their rhythm, they should be vastly improved on that side of the ball. That’s why Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton has the Cowboys going 10-7 in his latest prediction, which has them tied for first place in the NFC East .
”The Cowboys hired a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker. Dallas acquired edge-rusher Rashan Gary from the Green Bay Packers and drafted versatile defensive back Caleb Downs along with edge-rusher Malachi Lawrence in the first round,” Moton wrote.
“Cornerback Cobie Durant, a free-agent acquisition, is an underrated signing. If linebacker DeMarvion Overshown stays healthy, the Cowboys' defense will be one of the most improved units from the previous campaign.”
Moton adds that the help from the defense is all Dak Prescott and the talented Dallas offense need to take the division away from the Eagles.
The Eagles are the defending champs and have star players such as Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith returning. While that will help, they have a new play-caller on offense in Sean Mannion. Moton believes it will take time for him to get things figured out on offense, especially now that they don’t have A.J. Brown at wide receiver following an offseason trade.
It’s easy to think the loss of Brown will be devastating for the offense, but that might not be the case. Brown hasn’t been happy in the Philly offense for a couple of years now and his frustrations have often been a distraction.
It might take a few weeks for rookie Makai Lemon to truly hit his stride, but the culture could be improved in Philadelphia. That’s why looking past the Eagles, even with so many predictions favoring the Cowboys, would be a huge mistake.

title: Dallas Cowboys 'Magician' Christian Parker Continues Drawing Rave Reviews
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys training camp is in full swing, with the team set to hit the field for its first game of the NFL preseason in a matter of days. On Saturday, August 15, the Cowboys will face the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field.
Leading up to the preseason opener, there has been plenty of excitement surrounding the team, led by the revamped roster under defensive coordinator Christian Parker .
Parker has made a strong impression on those taking in the action in Oxnard and has immediately earned the respect of the team's young and veteran players. Earlier this week, during a joint scrimmage, Parker's defense put on a show against the Los Angeles Rams , and it's clear that players are buying into his scheme.
Cowboys pass rusher Rashan Gary , who the team acquired at the start of the new league year in a trade with the Green Bay Packers , recently appeared on The Rich Eisen Show , where he became the latest member of the team to hype up Parker and his football IQ.
"What can he not do? ... He's a magician at what he does." — @RashanAGary on how good Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is 🏈 (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/SCmnZMWpUz
Gary is familiar with Parker , who was on the Packers' staff during his first year in the league, so he comes with a better understanding of what Parker brings to the table than others on the Cowboys' roster.
"Man, what can he not do? He understands the back end.He understands the fronts. He understands how offense wants to, you know, attack our defenses," Gary said.
"And on top of that, he understands how to maximize his players, and that's in terms of, you know, freeing up more one-on-ones or find an opportunity to get, you know, a running, I mean, a linebacker on a running back, you know, mixing up the coverage to play with, you know, quarterback mindset. Don't want to say too much, but he's a magician in what he does."
We will get a better look at how the Cowboys' defense is coming together when they take the field for the preseason opener, but it will still likely be a more vanilla approach to the defensive gameplan. After all, Parker doesn't want to reveal all of his cards ahead of the regular-season opener against the division rival New York Giants. But with what everyone has seen so far, the team is heading in the right direction.

title: How a Maxx Crosby-Cowboys Trade Could Come to Fruition
full_text:
During the offseason, trade rumors circulated around the Dallas Cowboys as they reportedly had their sights set on Las Vegas Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby.
Dallas made a competitive offer , but were outbid by the Baltimore Ravens who agreed to send two first-round picks to Vegas in exchange for Crosby. The trade was nullified when Crosby failed his physical due to a knee injury, but the Cowboys already moved on and added Rashan Gary.
Las Vegas decided to patch things up with Crosby, who has since been cleared and is practicing. While they say they want Crosby to be part of their future, the speculation continues regarding his future. One analyst who still thinks Crosby could be traded is Mike Florio, although he doesn't think a trade will happen before the season.
Of course, in this scenario, the Cowboys would need to be a competent team in need of one playmaker to push them over the top. If they're not contending, such a move would make very little sense,
Florio believes the Raiders will go into the 2026 season with Crosby, but says they're a team to keep an eye on during the year. He believes they could decide to send Crosby to a contender if they struggle to start the season .
"Not necessarily before the season, but once the season starts, if the Raiders struggle. Because they've already stretched the rubber band to the point of trading him. And that was at a time when people were concerned about the health of his knee. He's cleared. He's back. Now, whether he's got five more years in that knee is a different issue. But, if they aren't playing well and they understand that Maxx Crosby isn't going to be part of the long-term solution and they could get value for him."
Florio said he's keeping an eye on the Tuesday after Week 9, which is the NFL trade deadline. That's where he sees the Cowboys making a move, especially after they expressed a desire to give up future assets to win now .
"I can see a team like the Cowboys. They've already talked about giving up future assets to improve their defense. And there was talk that they were thinking about making a play for Maxx Crosby back in March when the Ravens did. It would not surprise me if the Cowboys contend, the Raiders don't, Crosby gets traded to Dallas."
Crosby was in the news for another reason lately, as he and quarterback Kirk Cousins got into a "scuffle" during Raiders practice .
Cousins took exception to Crosby's physical play, which led to an altercation. While it was reported that no punches were thrown, both players were held out of practice for one day. Crosby plays with a relentless motor, which is part of what helps him succeed on game day, but in this instance, it drew the ire of the team's veteran quarterback.

title: Former NFL QB Says Cowboys’ D-Line Is Going to ‘Eat’ This Year
full_text:
Christian Parker is one of the biggest names in coaching right now. Whether he proves to be successful is still a question, but all eyes are on the Dallas Cowboys first-year defensive coordinator.
Parker takes over a defense that was atrocious in 2025 under Matt Eberflus, and will face plenty of pressure to improve that unit quickly in 2026. The Cowboys have an elite offense, with all 11 starters returning. The belief is that they will be a contender, as long as Parker makes them relevant on defense.
On Tuesday, Parker's star got quite the boost as his defense held its own against the Los Angeles Rams . It's a stretch to say they shut the high-flying Los Angeles offense down, which was never going to happen during a joint practice . Neither team had schemed anything up, so the players were very vanilla. What was important, however, is that the Cowboys weren't embarrassed. That wasn't the case in 2025, as the Rams made it look as though they were practicing against air.
That practice has once again given hope to Dallas, but others are seeing plenty of positives as well. That includes former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel, who said this defensive line is going to "eat" this year. Daniel claims the combination of the recently extended Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark is the best one-two punch on the interior that the Cowboys have had. He added that Parker will run a multiple defense in the same way his mentor Vic Fangio did, which will allow them to generate pressure without blitzing.
"And that is what a Vic Fangio defense does. They absolutely eat on that defensive line. Even going back to the 49ers years, they've always had beasts on that D-line," Daniel said on ESPN's NFL Live . "It's a system that's pretty simple at its core. But the first thing that Fangio would tell you is they do not want to blitz. And if you have a defensive lineman or defensive line in general that can get pressure on a quarterback without blitzing, it leaves more people in coverage, right?"
The one question Daniel seemed to have about this defense was just how fast Parker could get his scheme installed and allow the defense to find its rhythm.
That's a fair question not only because Parker is entering his first year as a defensive play-caller, but more than half of the defensive starters for the Cowboys will be new this season. Thankfully, their offense is good enough to win games even without an elite defense, but if they want to make a true run in the playoffs, this defense has to be firing on all cylinders.

title: Broncos at Falcons: How To Watch, TV Channel, Live Stream, Time
full_text:
At long last, the Denver Broncos are poised to take the field again on Friday night in Atlanta, Georgia, in the team's preseason opener.
The Atlanta Falcons will host the Broncos, with the plan to start Tua Tagovailoa at quarterback. I don't imagine Tua will take too many snaps against the Broncos' first-team defense — a unit that has led the NFL in sacks in back-to-back seasons.
We'll get to a few players to watch as well, but first, here's how to make sure you can catch the Broncos' preseason debut on Friday night.
We've had two-plus weeks of training camp to see how the Broncos' key position battles have shaped up . Based on what we've seen, here are a handful of players to watch .
Head coach Sean Payton tried walking back his comments from the offseason about there being an open competition for the No. 1 quarterback job, but there's clearly a battle going on. Ehlinger has acquitted himself well thus far, while Stidham has seemed to be pressing at times, like he's feeling the pressure.
Stidham will get the first half in Atlanta, while Ehlinger will get the second. These preseason games will go a long way toward the coaches' decision on this position, and the first audition is Friday night.
Coleman's place on the roster is secure, but it will be great to finally see him in action in an actual game. He's looked as advertised in camp, showcasing his three-down skill set as a complete back.
Will Coleman get a chance as a kick returner? I'm curious to see, simply because he was utilized that way last Saturday in the Broncos' planned scrimmage.
Bryant and Franklin are both locks for the roster — barring an unforeseen trade — but this first preseason game will be the first opportunity to create some clarity on the depth chart. Bryant has been the star of camp thus far, but can he translate it to the preseason games themselves?
Franklin's seat at the table has been diminished this summer, though his number of targets improved with Jaylen Waddle laid up for the past week-plus. Can Franklin remind the coaches why he started last season as the starter opposite Courtland Sutton?
Butler has also been one of camp's standouts. However, he's had a couple of down days, and the Broncos' receiver room is stacked. He'll need to show out in the preseason to have a chance at even the practice squad, with how deep the room is.
These two rookie linebackers have built up a head of steam in camp of late. Now it's time to translate that momentum into the preseason.
The Broncos have two linebacker roster spots up for grabs, and odds are, only one of these two have a chance at one. Murdock, as a seventh-round pick, has the advantage over the undrafted York.
Neither of these two rookies has impressed in camp up to this point. The Broncos have four veterans they trust at the top of the depth chart, but they drafted these two for a reason.
Joly's roster outlook is better than Bentley's, only because the Broncos would be unlikely to re-sign Joly after waiving him. Some other team would likely claim him.
If Joly wants to avoid that potential conundrum, he's got to start showing something in the preseason. Bentley's brief is to show enough for Denver to justify keeping a practice squad spot for him.

title: What Broncos' Latest Signing Really Says About the Center Crisis
full_text:
This week was a great reminder that, in the NFL, it's not what coaches say, but what they do.
After third-teamer-turned-first-teamer Michael Deiter was carted off the practice field on Tuesday , Sean Payton played down the seriousness of the Denver Broncos' center situation, only to sign a veteran two days later.
“We’ll work through it," Payton said. "We have guys that are flexible. We’ll be fine.”
Cut to Thursday, and the Broncos signed veteran center Lecitus Smith after placing Deiter on injured reserve, as first reported by 9NEWS ' Mike Klis , which gives them a little buffer with starter Luke Wattenberg and backup Alex Forsyth still sidelined with injuries . Smith is unlikely to play in the Broncos' preseason opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Friday, though, considering the timetable.
The demand to get some center help was intensified this week when Deiter went down with a season-ending quad injury . With the injuries to Wattenberg and Forsyth ahead of him, Deiter had been running with the first-team offense.
Following Deiter's injury, the Broncos had no choice but to turn to backup left guard Calvin Throckmorton as the first-team center . That's who fans can likely expect to see with the Broncos' ones and twos against the Falcons, while undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega runs with the threes.
The quad injury is a big bummer for Deiter, but it could be a great opportunity for Smith. Drafted in the sixth round by the Arizona Cardinals in 2022, Smith brings 19 NFL games and four career starts to the table in Denver.
At 28 years old, Smith has spent this offseason languishing as an unsigned veteran. Smith spent last season bouncing back and forth between the Green Bay Packers' practice squad and active roster. After the season ended, though, he was not re-signed.
Beyond the Cardinals and Packers, Smith has also spent time with the Houston Texans, Philadelphia Eagles, New England Patriots, and Pittsburgh Steelers, since entering the league in 2022. He's had a rough go of it, spending most of the past three seasons as a bubble player in the offseason and a practice squad player during the season.
At 6-foot-3 and 314 pounds, Smith's scouting report coming out of Virginia Tech praised his measurables, but questioned whether he had the technical refinement to become a starter-level center in the NFL.
"An athletic, three-year starter at guard with a decent frame, Smith lacks the desired measurables for the position. He is capable of working as a move blocker and out in space. However, he really struggles with hand placement and staying under control at the point of attack and on work-up blocks," NFL Media 's Lance Zierlein wrote .
"His lack of consistency as a run blocker is balanced by surprising technique and success in pass protection. Some of Smith's issues are correctable through coaching and discipline, but he might not rise above the level of average backup with the ability to step in and start from time to time."
Smith has been give the opportunity to start games with the Cardinals, Patriots, and Packers, but he's yet to show enough to retain such a role. In Denver, he'll at least get the chance to make the practice squad, but there could be an opportunity for more if the injury bug continues to ravage the team's center position.
The Broncos enter their first preseason game with a worst-case scenario at center. None of the three guys they entered camp with are healthy. The Broncos will get by this week, but if they're going to play Bo Nix in Game 2, they'll need health on their side at center.
Nix will not play in Atlanta, and while Sean Payton claims the decision was made a month ago , something tells me that the increasingly alarming situation at center may have factored in much more than the head coach is willing to admit. Whatever the impetus for the decision, it was the right one, regardless.
Hopefully, the Broncos have reason to believe that Wattenberg and/or Forsyth will be back on the field next week, though Payton is always mum on injuries and timetables. Wattenberg went down on Day 3 of camp , the first padded practice, while Forsyth followed later that week. It's been more than a week since either practiced with the team.
On the bright side, the past week-plus of camp has given Ortega a much bigger seat at the table than he would have otherwise gotten as an undrafted rookie. If he plays his cards right in the preseason, there's a chance he could win a job — if not on the 53-man roster, then perhaps on the practice squad.
We'll find out on Monday which way the arrow is pointing on that subject, but if it's still slow going on the health front, Smith could go from the couch to snapping to Nix within a matter of days.
Throckmorton's emergency contribution is admirable, but center is not his forte. And with Nix coming back from a serious ankle injury, the Broncos need better options at center.

title: Broncos Earn 'Elite Contender' Status in New NFL Power Rankings
full_text:
The Denver Broncos aren't phoning it in at training camp.
Sean Payton may be focusing on "load management" with certain tenured veterans and players coming off injuries, but that has not distracted from the Broncos' commitment to having a strong training camp. It's been a physical and competitive camp thus far, with emotions running high at times, and a heavy (and I mean heavy ) emphasis on the run game.
Payton is no fool. He saw the 2026 schedule and knew that the camp recipe would call for a lot of spice if the Broncos are to emerge from the kitchen with the Golden Spoon.
Given how tough the first eight weeks are, the Broncos are working hard to be ready to rock and roll, even if it has come at the expense of a maddeningly consistent rash of soft-tissue injuries and two season-enders to a pair of depth players.
Fortunately, the Broncos have avoided any major injuries to any starters or key players. And quarterback Bo Nix, though he won't play in the preseason opener vs. the Atlanta Falcons, has looked great in camp and fully recovered from his fractured ankle.
With the preseason set to begin in earnest this weekend, Nick Shook dropped the latest NFL power rankings, with the Broncos checking in at... No. 2 overall, behind only the Los Angeles Rams.
"After falling painfully short of the Super Bowl last season, the Broncos return one of the most complete rosters in the NFL with hope spilling out of their saddlebags. There's good reason for the optimism: Their core contributors return on both defense and offense, and they've added a new weapon in explosive receiver Jaylen Waddle. Theoretically, the team that finished 14-3 last season should be even better ," Shook wrote .
The alacrity with which the Broncos' 2025 season came to a screeching halt last season was jarring. The campaign may have officially ended in the AFC championship game, but it was over a week earlier after the euphoric overtime win over the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round of the playoffs.
Nix injured his ankle on the third-to-last play of the game, though fans didn't learn about it until 45 minutes or so after the final gun. That 45 minutes was blissful for Broncos Country, jubilant over the notion of this Nix-led team being set to host the AFC title game the next week.
Then Sean Payton stepped back to the podium and delivered the shocking news nobody west of the Mississippi wanted to hear: Nix was done for what remained of the season. The Broncos tried to rally around Jarrett Stidham, but the wind had been taken from the team's sails with the reality of Nix's injury, and the backup quarterback did not prove to be equal to his opportunity in the AFC championship game.
Knowing they were that close to the Super Bowl, the Broncos opted to batten down the roster's hatches, striving to retain as many of their free agents as possible, which they did. The Broncos will return 90% or so of their 2025 snaps this season, and with only a few strategic offseason additions, like Waddle and the club's draft class, the club hit training camp with continuity very much on their side.
"The Broncos have enjoyed an ideally quiet camp, are led by a veteran coach with a history of high-level success, welcomed their quarterback back into the fold after his injury-related exit in January and are hoping J.K. Dobbins can fulfill his sky-high promises (including completing a full season)," Shook wrote. "They also have five 2025 playoff qualifiers on their schedule in the first six weeks of the season. Right now, they're one of the elite contenders. They'll hope the same is true by the time winter arrives."
I'm not sure what qualifies as an "ideally quiet camp," but I would challenge Shook's assertion, based solely on the fact that, since the pads went on (Day 3), the Broncos have dealt with at least one injury per day .
Mostly of the soft-tissue variety, Payton has vowed to get to the bottom of it, but the notable absence of key players and starters, like Waddle, Marvin Mims Jr., Nik Bonitto (returned to practice days ago), Luke Wattenberg, Alex Forsyth, Devon Key, and others, has been conspicuous.
Again, though, the silver lining has been that nothing serious has befallen any of the players mentioned above. Backup defensive tackle Matt Henningsen (Achilles) and third-string center Michael Deiter (quad) have been lost for the season in camp, but the Broncos have seemingly dodged the worst possibilities in camp.
Dobbins even missed a day , creating more skepticism over the oft-injured running back's " pinky promise " to stay healthy for the full 17 games this season. He was back at practice the next day, though limited to individual drills, and was a full participant in Wednesday's session to prepare for the Falcons on Friday night.
The Broncos are well aware of how tough their initial schedule is. That has informed their physical, competitive training camp.
Hopefully, the collective callus the Broncos have built up during camp will serve them well when the regular season arrives, and they face the likes of the Kansas City Chiefs (twice), Jacksonville Jaguars, Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Chargers, and Seattle Seahawks all within the first eight weeks.
Weather that storm, though, and the Broncos will be sailing the smooth seas of the NFL's easiest second-half schedule . That is the mission, though the Broncos can only take it one game at a time come September.
As the highest-ranked AFC team in these power rankings, it's clear that Denver has finally earned the respect of the national media. Being categorized as an "elite contender" by Shook reflects how far the Broncos have come over the past two years.
Everyone knows that if Nix doesn't go down, the Broncos would have been in the Super Bowl to face the Seahawks. Suffice it to say, the 2026 Broncos are looking to make up for lost time.

title: Broncos at Falcons: 5 Burning Questions That Need Answers
full_text:
After a long offseason, the Denver Broncos finally return to the field on Friday night in their preseason debut against the Atlanta Falcons .
Training camp has seen some surprises , with a few players sidelined with minor injuries (plus two season-enders) and several incumbents showing improvement.
The first preseason game will give Broncos fans a better idea about how the roster is taking shape and which players will fill certain roles. Players can only face their teammates in practice so many times, so the preseason game against the Falcons will reveal how the Broncos fare against another team.
We've learned a lot about the Broncos since camp started, but the preseason opener could answer several lingering questions. There may be more to ask, of course, but these five questions might be the most notable, given the current circumstances.
There may not be a more important question to answer than who replaces John Franklin-Myers in the starting lineup on the interior defensive line. Zach Allen and D.J. Jones are locked-in starters, but the question is who fills the third spot.
Some might think it's Malcolm Roach, not only based on camp but also the Broncos' first unofficial depth chart . However, Roach is better suited to rotate in with Jones on passing downs.
Eyioma Uwazurike brings the most experience and might be a favorite , but others will get their chance to show what they can do.
Plenty of attention will be on 2025 third-round pick Sai'vion Jones to see what strides he has made since last season. We'll also find out whether 2026 third-round rookie Tyler Oyendim can make a case to crack the starting lineup.
Throughout training camp, the 2025 first-round pick has been utilized in different spots in the defensive backfield. But where does he eventually settle in, and at what spot? Barron is currently listed as the backup to Riley Moss at the No. 2 boundary cornerback and the No. 2 nickel behind Ja'Quan McMillian.
At this point, Moss has all but locked up the No. 2 cornerback spot, but the preseason games are the chance for Barron to demonstrate that he deserves increased snaps. There's no question that the second-year player needs to step forward.
While it's too soon to give up on Barron, he does need to show in the preseason games that he's ready to take a bigger load, even if he isn't a starter to open the season.
The Broncos have lost their top three centers to injury during training camp. Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth are said to have minor injuries, though it's unlikely they will see the field in the preseason opener after missing all of this week's practices.
Meanwhile, backup center Michael Deiter suffered a season-ending quad injury on Tuesday . With Deiter out, that leaves the Broncos extremely thin at center.
Calvin Throckmorton took first-team snaps at center during practice, but it wouldn't be a surprise if the Broncos add another center at some point this summer to at least have another healthy player out there. Undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega has gone from playing guard to center in the wake of all the injuries at the position.
Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad are set as the starting linebackers, but we don't yet know who will become the third man in that rotation. The rest of the players are lacking NFL defensive experience.
However, the Broncos have seen good things from Jordan Turner, Karene Reid, Red Murdock, and Taurean York, so all of these players will have a chance to show they can be relied upon in the linebacker rotation.
Levelle Bailey will also get a look, though time may be running out as he now enters his third year with the Broncos. The preseason is a good time for Bailey to show that he warrants a spot on the 53-man roster or practice squad.
We've recently highlighted how undrafted rookies have a knack for making the Broncos' 53-man roster . The first preseason game is a time when fans are especially interested in seeing what these unheralded rookies have to offer.
York, of course, is in the mix for a linebacker spot, but there have been other undrafted rookies who have made their mark at other positions. There's even a competition for the long snapper job, with Luke Basso competing with the veteran specialist Mitchell Fraboni.
The undrafted rookies are certain to see a lot of snaps in the preseason opener, meaning it's their first chance in a game situation to make a strong impression.

title: 10 Broncos With the Most to Prove in Preseason Opener vs. Falcons
full_text:
With the preseason opener approaching on Friday, the Denver Broncos are set to travel to take on the Atlanta Falcons .
With nearly three weeks of training camp in the books, the Broncos have a better idea of how the position battles are shaping up across the roster. But camp is only part of the equation; the preseason games account for the rest.
Preseason action is about roster evaluation, and today, we're highlighting 10 Broncos with the most to prove on Friday night at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA.
Robinson has had a great camp, giving the Broncos' tackles consistent fits, especially with his first step. We need to see consistent run defense from Robinson, as well as his pass rush prowess, carry over from practices to games.
Barron has been one of the more disappointing players in camp, and it seems he is no longer competing for the No. 2 boundary cornerback spot with Riley Moss. This first preseason game will be a big test to see whether Barron can improve his play or at least be a gamer if he can’t perform well in practices.
Malcolm Roach is currently in the top spot to take the John Franklin-Myers starting job, but Uwazurike is right alongside him. Uwazurike has been tough to block in practices, and it’ll be nice to see that translate to the game.
If Uwazurike plays in Atlanta and puts a good game together, it could get him closer to beating out Roach for the starting job opposite Zach Allen.
Sean Payton talked about needing a linebacker to step up in that third spot, and there is a good chance Reid could be the one. Reid shocked many by making the roster last season as an undrafted rookie.
Ideally, Reid takes a jump in his development, and he can put himself squarely in that spot, though the competition is stiff.
The Broncos' safety depth has struggled in camp so far and has been at fault for multiple big passing plays given up to the offense. Denver allowed P.J. Locke to walk, with eyes on Key stepping in as the third safety.
It isn’t clear whether Key has contributed to the issues with the safety depth in camp, but there's a reason the Broncos worked out veteran safety Taylor Rapp on Wednesday. This game is going to be a big test for Key.
The fan hero of the 2025 campaign had a rough season, though he turned in an admirable effort going from the backup right tackle to starting at left guard. Palczewski is a valuable depth piece, but how valuable?
Palczewski's practices have been inconsistent at left guard and right tackle, so on the heels of signing his two-year extension, he needs to start showing up in these preseason games.
There has been a lot of praise for Coleman as a ball-carrier in camp. He doesn’t look like a rookie out there.
Now, practices are a bit easier for backs to stand out, even against a defense as tough as Denver's, so this game is going to be the real test for the rookie. However, there is no reason to doubt that Coleman will struggle in the games given his play style.
Another back, but for a different reason. There has been praise for the growth Harvey has shown on passing downs, both as a receiver and blocker, and a game will be a great test for him.
His blocking is critical, and if it improves and he shows it in a game, it could cement him as the RB2 with a third-down back role.
Bryant is easily the star of training camp so far , as he consistently makes big plays and has been reliable. Training camp is just a stepping stone, and any player who has strong practices has to prove he can carry that over to games.
Bryant should be fun to watch in this one.
There is a fan hype around Joly, but the word out of camp isn’t overly promising. He has looked raw and has struggled in camp practices, which is something to monitor, especially with how poorly built the Broncos' tight end room is.
Considering the competition for the last two tight end spots on the roster, Joly can begin to separate by standing out in the preseason games. We shall see.

title: Breaking Down Broncos' Workout of Veteran S Taylor Rapp
full_text:
The Denver Broncos held a workout on Wednesday with veteran free-agent safety Taylor Rapp, according to media reports .
It's unclear whether Rapp was offered a contract following his visit while the Broncos prepare for Friday's preseason opener against the Falcons.
A second-round draft pick in 2019, Rapp has recorded 488 total tackles, 31 pass deflections, 12 interceptions, and two forced fumbles across 93 career appearances — 57 with the Los Angeles Rams and 36 with the Buffalo Bills, who released him in March. He also started 72 games.
The 28-year-old has not played a full regular season since the 2021 campaign due to a variety of injuries, most recently a knee issue that helped catalyze his departure from Buffalo.
Rapp was a decorated collegian at Washington, earning Pac-12 Defensive Freshman of the Year honors in 2016 as well as first-team All-Pac-12 selections in 2017 and 2018.
"Versatile three-year starter who combines tenacity with football intelligence to play at a consistently high level," reads his pre-draft scouting report by NFL Media 's Lance Zierlein . "Rapp isn't big, but he's well-built and durability hasn't been a concern despite his physical nature as a striker.
"He played all over the field this year and might be best suited in a mix between down safety and two-high looks with the ability to cover tight ends. His coverage talent is average, but his run support effort and open-field tackling are clearly defined strengths that make him a relatively safe selection."
While it's not unusual for teams to churn their rosters during training camp — Denver recently executed a pair of transactions — this might be read as a bit of an indictment on the incumbent safety corps, especially the backups.
The Broncos are set atop the depth chart with Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones, but they may not like what they see from the likes of Tycen Anderson, Miles Scott, JL Skinner, and Parker Robertson.
There aren't any glaring injuries that would've prompted Rapp's visit, suggesting the club believes it can improve its talent level at the position. (This, however, assumes Rapp is eventually signed.)
Perhaps the Broncos are merely doing due diligence; perhaps they're waiting until after Friday's preseason opener to re-assess the situation.
The aforementioned reserves will have an extended chance to acquit themselves with the starters only prepared to play about 15 snaps. If they don't, Rapp could be the next newest Bronco.

title: Broncos Camp Day 11: Good J.K. Dobbins News | Takeaways | Winners and Losers
full_text:
Denver Broncos training camp marched ahead on Wednesday.
With the first preseason game coming up on Friday vs. the Atlanta Falcons , Day 11 of Broncos camp was unique. The Broncos' practice format was an opponent-prep session with no pads.
It was also a shorter practice; just 90 minutes long, give or take. What did we learn?
Let's get to the key storylines from Day 11, what takeaways may be had, and the winners and losers.
After Wednesday's practice, head coach Sean Payton announced that Nix will not play on Friday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. However, Payton said that most starters will play "around 15 snaps" vs. the Falcons.
"Expecting our starters to play around 15 plays," Payton said after Wednesday's practice . "Bo won't play. He'll play next week."
Payton made it clear that Denver plans for Nix to get some preseason exposure, but the team is going to wait until Game 2 to debut its young franchise quarterback. Nix will also play in Game 3.
With Nix sitting out, the plan is for Stidham to play the first half and Ehlinger to play the second. Although Payton recently tried to walk back his offseason "we see a competition" comments about the No. 2 quarterback, this job is very much up for grabs.
Stidham has been the understood backup for the past three years — and he's paid like it. But after his performance in the AFC championship game, perhaps, the Broncos want to see if Ehlinger could be a better option.
Ehlinger has had a great camp, but it will take a lot to unseat Stidham as the QB2. The preseason games will play a major role in the Broncos' decision here.
Running back J.K. Dobbins practiced on Day 11, making it two days in a row after he got dinged up in Monday's session. The Broncos need him healthy in order for their revamped ground game to reach its full potential this season, so don't expect to see the veteran back in Atlanta.
Working on the side field during practice on Wednesday were wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr., centers Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth, offensive lineman Alex Palczewski, linebacker Jordan Turner, and rush linebacker Dasan McCullough, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel . Palczewski's presence on the side field is new; he practiced in full on Day 10.
Adkins got hurt last Friday, but recently returned to practice after missing a couple of days, so he may have reaggravated his injury. Turner was just activated off the Non-Football Injury list on Day 9 , so missing more live reps isn't good for his roster outlook.
Not seen at practice were tight end Caleb Lohner, wide receiver Michael Bandy, and center Michael Deiter. We learned from Payton after practice that Deiter suffered a serious quad injury on Tuesday that will end his season.
With all three of Denver's top centers injured, Calvin Throckmorton has run with the first-team, despite being listed as the No. 2 left guard on the first unofficial depth chart .
The Broncos worked out the veteran safety on Wednesday, per Gabriel , which comes with some curious implications for how the depth competition is shaping up at the position. Beyond Talanoa Hufanga, Brandon Jones, and Devon Key, the Broncos have been hoping to see great competition at safety.
If the Broncos keep four safeties, there's only one open roster spot. Key is an assumed lock because of his special teams prowess (first-team All-Pro last year), and he's also getting the first bite at the apple in replacing P.J. Locke as the No. 3 safety.
If the Broncos sign Rapp, it will be a poor reflection of how the Broncos see the depth safeties. However, with all three preseason games left to be played, there's plenty of time yet for one or two of these safeties to make a case for themselves.
Again, it was a lighter practice, so there wasn't as much to see from an individual performance perspective, but Dobbins makes the winner's column for practicing two days in a row.
Key makes it for returning to practice after missing many days with a soft-tissue injury.
Deiter's injury puts him on this list. He's the second player injured in camp whose season is already over.
Palczewski and Adkins make the list for not practicing in full. It'll be interesting to see if they travel with the team to Atlanta, as Payton said the Broncos plan to leave the injured players behind.
Skinner, Anderson, Scott, and Robertson make the list simply because of the implications of Rapp working out. It's a little unfair to paint them all with such broad strokes, but if the Broncos sign a safety, it means they're not happy with what they're seeing on the depth side.

title: Sean Payton Made the Right Call on Bo Nix Ahead of Broncos' Preseason Opener
full_text:
With the preseason opener coming on Friday, the Denver Broncos have made their decision.
Third-year quarterback Bo Nix won't play in Game 1 on the road vs. the Atlanta Falcons , Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced on Wednesday.
"Expecting our starters to play around 15 plays," Payton said after Wednesday's practice. "Bo won't play. He'll play next week."
The Broncos are acting accordingly with their young franchise quarterback. All of this team's 2026 ambitions are tied to Nix being on the field.
With Nix returning from a fractured ankle that required corrective surgery in January and a clean-up procedure in the spring, there's no reason to play him in the first preseason game. That's doubly true when you consider the artificial surface of Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Better safe than sorry.
Keep in mind, this isn't a reflection of Nix's performance in training camp thus far or of his overall health/recovery. He's been a full participant at camp with zero limits or strictures on his participation. Through 11 practices, he's looked as mobile and athletic as ever, like he's as good as new.
Nix's throwing motion looks more polished , and his deep-ball accuracy has been impressive. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said recently that Nix's deep accuracy has been " off the charts " in camp.
Nix looks more comfortable, more poised, and maybe even a bit more vocal. These practices have been physical and competitive, and the first-team offense and defense have butted heads at times.
Now in his third year in Payton's system, Nix recently told Kay Adams of the Up & Adams Show that he and the offense feel more on the level with the Broncos' elite defense, which has raised the competitive bar. These practices have been intense.
Another big reason not to play Nix in Game 1 is the absence of a healthy center. Starter Luke Wattenberg has been out since suffering an injury on Day 3 of camp, while Alex Forsyth has missed the past three days.
Even third-team center Michael Deiter went down on Tuesday, forcing the Broncos to turn to Calvin Throckmorton to snap with the starters. Payton announced on Wednesday that Deiter suffered a major quad injury that will require surgery, which means he's likely headed for injured reserve.
The Broncos are concerningly thin at center with Wattenberg and Forsyth still sidelined. I wonder if it we were in the regular season whether Wattenberg would be able to push through the injury report to play on game day, but with no such pressure existing in August, the Broncos aren't rushing their starter back onto the field.
As for Nix, if this were a regular-season game, he would be playing. But it's an exhibition contest, and the Broncos made this decision weeks ago.
"He wants to play. He'll play the next two weeks," Payton said of Nix. "I think that was probably something that was already decided like a month ago. But if we were playing a game, I would say he would play—you'd have to ask him—but I would say 100%."
In all honesty, I think most Broncos fans would be fine if Nix didn't step on the field of play until Week 1 of the regular season. But he's champing at the bit to play, and Payton believes in playing his starters in the preseason to help build a football callus and re-acclimate them to NFL game speed, but there's always a fine line.
Nix obviously wants to play in the preseason, but with Game 2 (Green Bay Packers) and Game 3 (Minnesota Vikings) being at Empower Field at Mile High on a playing surface he and the Broncos know well, the team is going to bide its time.
“I think preseason’s always a great time to get back out there and get your feet wet a little bit and see defenses in a live situation before the first game," Nix said on Monday, Day 9 of Broncos camp.
By this point, all the players on the Broncos' roster are dying to go against an outside opponent. That's especially true this summer, since Payton opted to skip the opportunity to hold a joint practice with any of Denver's preseason opponents.
Fans will have to wait at least another week before seeing Nix suit up again. When he returns to the field at Mile High, it'll be the first time since he suffered that heartbreaking fractured ankle on the third-to-last play of the divisional round of the playoffs in January.
Nix led the Broncos to a 33-30 overtime win, then had to watch from the booth the next week when the New England Patriots came to town for the AFC championship game. We all know how that game turned out.
Suffice it to say, Nix is hungry. He's looking to make up for lost time after leading his team to the doorstep of the Super Bowl. But good things come to those who wait.

title: Sean Payton 'Feels Bad For' Michael Deiter After Major Injury
full_text:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced backup center Michael Deiter, who was carted off the practice field on Tuesday, suffered a quad injury that will end his 2026 season before it even began.
Deiter will undergo corrective surgery and likely head to the injured reserve list.
"Feel bad for him," Payton told reporters following Wednesday's practice.
A former Dolphins third-round pick, Deiter is in his second season with the Broncos after joining the club's practice squad in January and subsequently landing a futures deal . The soon-to-be 30-year-old found his way to the Mile High City following stops in Miami, Houston, and Washington.
Deiter had been temporarily handling first-string center responsibilities with starter Luke Wattenberg and direct backup Alex Forsyth both battling injuries . Neither Wattenberg nor Forsyth participated in drills on Wednesday.
Veteran guard-by-trade Calvin Throckmorton was forced into the pivot with the aforementioned sidelined. It's possible, if not probable, that Throckmorton remains there for Friday's preseason opener at Atlanta before giving way to undrafted rookie C Gavin Ortega.
“We’ll work through it. We have guys that are flexible. We’ll be fine," Payton said Tuesday.
With Denver's starters set to play only 15 snaps against the Falcons, it's unlikely that All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz will be asked to man the center position in what's ultimately a meaningless game.
However, should this issue linger into the regular season, Meinerz acknowledged he's willing to pinch-hit if needed. Moreover, he stressed the importance of the starting front five (read: Wattenberg) getting back on the field together as soon as possible to form necessary chemistry — especially when the proverbial bullets start flying for real.
“We’re able to get into the level 400 of our offense a lot quicker because we already have a base foundation and fundamentals of how we want to do things," Meinerz told reporters Tuesday. "Now we’re looking at efficiencies, now we’re looking at not only winning the block, but being dominant with that block and understanding that there’s an emphasis in the rushing game this year for us. So just constantly grinding in our individual period to make sure that those reps are feeling good, ‘Hey, are my hands good here? Hey, was my hat... Did I give you enough help here?’ There’s always constant little feedback here, and I think what’s most fun is how much smaller the communication’s going to get on the line of scrimmage because when an offensive line’s able to communicate so little, there’s a lot less tells for the defense to be able to pick up on.”

title: Broncos' Release First Unofficial Depth Chart—Analyzing the Clues
full_text:
Let the overreactions begin! The Denver Broncos' first unofficial depth chart is here.
The Broncos are set to face the Atlanta Falcons in their first preseason game of the year on Friday, giving us our first look at the unofficial depth chart.
With two weeks or so of training camp in the books, let's take a look at the Broncos' first depth chart, with an emphasis on unofficial , and see if we can uncover any clues relative to the roster battles taking place this summer.
Analysis : Nothing has changed here, for now. Ehlinger has turned in an impressive camp performance, though, while Stidham seems to be pressing. This depth chart could change, depending on how these preseason games unfold.
Analysis : This is our first big reminder not to read deeply into this unofficial depth chart. As per Sean Payton's tradition, the rookie, Coleman, starts at the bottom of the depth chart, but based on what we've seen in camp, he's the No. 3 running back behind Dobbins and Harvey.
Analysis : That's that. Just one player listed and we all know who it is.
Analysis : Again, we have the rookies at the bottom. It's a matter of course with Payton, though in this case, it also happens to be an accurate reflection of where things stand. It'l be a surprise if the fifth-rounder Joly doesn't make the 53-man roster, but he has a long way to go in his development as an NFL-caliber tight end.
Analysis : Key, Manjack, and Duplessis are undrafted rookies, while Butler is a 30-year-old veteran in his second NFL season, officially. Butler, a two-time UFL Offensive Player of the Year, is interesting, based on how he's performed in camp, but nobody, and I mean nobody, has looked better than "Patty Ice" in camp thus far .
Analysis : The X and Z in Payton's offense is often nominal. He interchanges much, but as it stands, Mims tops the depth chart over Franklin, which is interesting, considering how Franklin was Denver's No. 2 receiver last year. Rowan recently returned to the Broncos after spending much of his rookie year on the practice squad, while Ross and Katsis are undrafted rookies who've shined thus far in camp.
Analysis : This is another example of the relative meaninglessness of the X, Z, and slot. Waddle is the 1a or 1b receiver in the ultimate pecking order, and will be moved around the formation at all the different spots. For now, though, only Waddle and Humphrey are listed in the slot.
Analysis : This one is based on NFL experience, once you get past Bolles. Peart is a veteran, while Crum is in Year 3. Peart missed most of last season after tearing his ACL in Week 6, so Crum served as the primary swing tackle. Miller is an undrafted rookie.
Analysis : Powers is the starter, while Throckmorton is a tenured vet. Ortega is an undrafted rookie. Both Throckmorton and Ortega have been called to play center snaps this week with all the injuries the Broncos have dealt with at the position.
Analysis : All three men are currently injured. Wattenberg has missed the past week, going down on the first day of pads, while Forsyth has missed the past couple of days. Deiter was running as the first-team center on Day 9 and Day 10 before going down himself on Tuesday, and being carted off. It's unlikely that any of these three will play in Atlanta.
Analysis : This is interesting. We all know the All-Pro, Meinerz, but Casey is a fourth-round rookie who's spent his entire career playing on the left side of the line. Casey's future is at left guard; another reminder not to read into these depth charts.
Analysis : McGlinchey is the locked-in starter, while Palczewski is still the primary backup at right tackle. However, after filling in for Powers at left guard for much of last season, Palczewski has right-to-left-side and inside/outside versatility. When Powers has been given any rest days or reps in camp this summer, Palczewski has gotten some first-team reps at left guard, and at right tackle in place of McGlinchey.
Analysis : It's interesting to see Jackson listed ahead of Jones here, but again, this unofficial depth chart doesn't carry much meaning. Jones is a 2025 third-rounder while Jackson is in his third year with the Broncos.
Analysis : There's a conspicuous name missing from the nose tackle depth chart, but we'll address that with the next position. Miller and Williams are the last two guys in the D-line room, so they'll need to shine in the preseason to stand a chance at making the roster.
Analysis : This may be the first depth chart to provide any true inkling into what the coaches are thinking. With John Franklin-Myers gone, Roach is in the driver's seat to win that starting job, instead of living as the backup nose tackle behind Jones. And Uwazurike is giving Roach a run for his money in camp. Onyedim is a rookie third-rounder who is a lock for the roster.
Analysis : Bonitto is a Pro Bowler, but Elliss has been one of the defensive stars of camp. I'm really looking forward to seeing Elliss in action this year. Robinson has also had a great camp as a 2025 fourth-rounder, while Walker is trying to make up for lost time after missing his entire rookie season with an injury.
Analysis : Cooper is the starter, while Tillman will be hard to beat out for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Sanders, a 2023 third-rounder, will certainly try, but unless the Broncos keep five outside linebackers this year, it'll be tough for him to make the roster. McCullough is an undrafted rookie who's dealt with an injury that has sidelined him for nearly a week.
Analysis : These linebacker spots are interchangeable. Singleton is the starter, while Reid made the roster last year as an undrafted rookie. Turner just got activated from the Non-Football Injury list, and has some catching up to do.
Analysis : Strnad returns as a starter, with Bailey doing everything he can to win one of the two linebacker roster spots. Murdock is a seventh-rounder and York is undrafted. Both are rookies and have impressed thus far in camp.
Analysis : Surtain needs no explanation. Abrams-Draine has had a great camp in Year 3, while Fresch was signed from the UFL in June, though he's dealt with an injury in camp that cost him a couple of days. Hallman was signed late last week after the Broncos waived the injured Jaden Robinson.
Analysis : Moss has been a super-stud in camp, leaving absolutely no daylight for Barron to win the No. 2 cornerback job. Barron, a 2025 first-rounder, has played a lot of nickel and dime in camp. Austin is an undrafted rookie who's shown some fight in camp.
Analysis : McMillian will remain at the top here, with Barron as the first defensive back onto the field in most sub-packages. The Broncos like Taylor, but they're super strong at nickel corner.
Analysis : Behind Hufanga, this depth chart is still up for grabs, though Skinner has the edge due to his sixth-round draft pedigree (2023) and special teams acumen. Anderson was a free-agent signing, who also brings some third-phase production to the table, while Robertson is an undrafted rookie.
Analysis : Jones is the starter, while Key is also a lock for the roster as a first-team All-Pro special teams ace. Scott is a seventh-round rookie battling with Skinner, Anderson, and Robertson for the fourth, and likely final, safety spot on the roster.
Analysis : No explanation needed.
Analysis : Again, self-explanatory.
Analysis : Who will serve as Mims's kickoff partner? Don't discount Coleman as a contender, even though he's unlisted here. Coleman returned some kicks during the Broncos' planned scrimmage on Day 8. Katis was signed for his returner upside.
Analysis : Mims is a two-time All-Pro returner, but if he's going to feature more in the offense, the Broncos need another good option. Bandy is at least reliable (though he muffed a punt last year), while Ross is a rookie with some juice. Katsis is unlisted here but may also be in the running.
