title: Mario Edwards’ Contract Could Subtly Change Texans’ 53-Man Roster
full_text:
The Houston Texans, since the start of training camp, have brought back two familiar faces on their defensive line heading into the 2026 season.
One of those was, of course, their former No. 1 overall pick, Jadeveon Clowney , who made his return to Houston after seven seasons on a one-year, $5.5 million deal and enters as a potentially pivotal piece in this already-stellar defensive end unit.
But the Texans, before they decided to bring in Clowney, also added another defensive lineman: Mario Edwards Jr. , who has played in Houston the past two seasons, yet was released earlier this year via a failed physical designation.
The Texans brought him back in, though, which was viewed as a nice depth move for their defensive tackle room when the news first surfaced within the first week of camp. And in the days to follow, it still is.
However, Edwards' reported contract might also offer some underlying hints of what to expect for Houston's defensive line, and as a result, their 53-man roster, that might've gone overlooked before.
According to NFL insider Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 , the Texans signed Edwards to a one-year, $1.4 million deal. $1.3 million of that contract is fully guaranteed, while the remaining $187,000 is a signing bonus––which is also guaranteed money.
#Texans one-year deal for Mario Edwards Jr.: fully guaranteed $1.487 million, salary $1.3 million (fully guaranteed), $187,500 signing bonus @KPRC2
So the Texans are paying a small, but fully guaranteed contract out to Edwards just a month away from cutdown day. It's even a bit of a different structure than a deal like Clowney just signed, which could reach up to $8 million across one year via incentives, and had a base value of $5.5 million.
If anything, that structure for Edwards shows the vision that the Texans and their decision-makers have for him on this defense in 2026: he's going to be a depth piece on this defensive line, whose snap count is to be determined, but he will be a piece of the 53-man roster.
If the Texans didn't see a clear route for Edwards to make the 53-man roster, his deal wouldn't be quite as surefire with guarantees. Houston had him as a rotational player last year, and even post-injury, feels he can sustain that same level of production.
Could Houston decide to cut Edwards before the season and take that $1.4 million cap hit if they didn't want him? Sure, it’s only a $1.4 million cap hit to do so. But why sign him to the deal so close to the season in the first place? That's practically flushing money down the drain.
That makes keeping him on the Week 1 roster, and as a frequent piece of this defensive line, the more likely outcome, barring any sudden surprises.
With Edwards close to being locked in as a piece of this 53-man roster, adding him to this defensive line starts to really round out what you can expect on both the interior and the edge for this unit as a whole heading into Week 1.
As for the Texans' defensive tackle room, seven players are currently signed on: Edwards, Sheldon Rankins, Kayden McDonald, Tommy Togiai, Naquan Jones, Kyonte Hamilton, and Dominic Bailey.
Logan Hall is technically listed as a defensive end, but it seems like Houston wants to run him inside more often than he'll be playing off the edge. So adding him takes that total to eight.
The first four of those players are due to make the roster. Including Hall raises the number to five. Add in the Texans' top three edge rushers and likely one of Dylan Horton and Dominique Robinson , and that's nine players on the defensive line for the 53-man roster.
So adding Edwards, by consequence, makes the squeeze to make the roster much tighter for the likes of Naquan Jones, Kyonte Hamilton, and Dominic Bailey; three guys who aren't as locked into their respective roster spots. It does the same to the defensive end room, but to a lesser extent.
That's because five rotation-level defensive tackles could be more than enough for Houston to enter the season with, and thus, leave the other three as cuts or practice squad players. Jones feels like the closest player to make it past the cut, but six defensive tackles on the roster would be a lot on a team that also has tough calls to make at wide receiver, tight end, and linebacker.
There's lots of time, and preseason games to be played, before the Texans' roster decisions become final. Injuries can happen, and the stock of several players will go both up and down, that might just leave Houston carrying six defensive tackles into the Buffalo Bills game in Week 1 .
But if all holds to form, don't be surprised if Edwards' signing, and more specifically, his contract details, were a sign of things to come.

title: 5 Texans Players I'm Most Excited to See in Chargers Preseason Matchup
full_text:
The Houston Texans are kicking off their first preseason game of three on Thursday night, facing the Los Angeles Chargers.
For the Texans, it's their first real look at what this 90-man roster looks like in a live, in-game setting after a long offseason with multiple changes in all three phases.
Several of Houston's notable starters won't be playing in this one, but what that allows for is some roster bubble guys or otherwise unproven players to get some real shine, and as a result, move their stock to find a roster spot or a big role on the depth chart up or down.
With that in mind, I'll be keeping a close eye on these five Texans players throughout the night, because a big day from them could end up paying major dividends moving forward:
﻿ The Texans' sixth-round rookie wide receiver has been a pleasant surprise ever since he's been on the field in OTAs. That momentum that he's built up within this position group has only carried him into a positive training camp thus far, and could have a chance to roll into a productive preseason debut on Thursday.
If Bond has a big day in a game where he could see a lot of snaps among this deep group of receivers on the 90-man roster, expect talks surrounding him climbing up the depth chart to get even louder as the Texans get closer to Week 1 of the regular season.
The Texans' tight end room has been one that's largely undecided throughout the offseason and into the first two weeks of camp. One name who's been fighting for a roster spot within that unit is Brevin Jordan, who might've been fifth on a six-man depth chart coming into camp, but has been one of the early risers in practice who's now a more likely bet to make the 53-man roster .
If he's able to show out in this preseason outing––one where Dalton Schultz might not play in, and Brevin Jordan could be injured––that's big for his stock moving forward, and might just be what puts him on the inside of the 53-man cut for the time being.
If the Texans decide to give their first-round rookie run in their preseason debut, there's no doubt that all eyes will be on Rutledge to come out of the gates with a statement performance. He's made waves in camp in being one of the more fierce competitors of anyone on the field, getting into frequent spats, and even having risen to the top of Houston's early depth chart at center.
Rutledge's transition from guard to center won't be perfect. As a rookie, and considering he hasn't played the position a whole lot, there's going to be bumps along the way. But preseason will be a great way for the Texans to give him some much-needed live reps at the position. And if he looks like he's ahead of schedule, that's even better.
The Texans' linebacker room might have become even more unpredictable since the start of training camp following their recent injury to Jake Hansen . His return is to be determined, but in the timeframe that he's out in preseason, the door is now open for another player further down the depth chart to step up.
Enter Jamal Hill, who was ranked towards the bottom of Houston's first preseason depth chart at linebacker, is trying to take a big leap entering his fourth season with the Texans, and will likely get a ton of reps this game. If he does, and he converts on them, his chances to make the roster might be just a bit better than they look right now.
Right next to Bond as possibly the biggest standout at Texans training camp, UDFA cornerback Collin Wright has made some noise as a defender who can get his hands on the football, and has stood out in practice virtually every day to guys like DeMeco Ryans and Derek Stingley.
That attention could become even greater for Wright if he stands out in this preseason game. If he gets a couple of PBUs or even an interception, he'll have a really serious case to be one of the few, if not the only, undrafted rookies to make this year's 53-man roster. So the stakes he faces against this Chargers team are massive.

title: Where to Watch, Stream Texans' First Preseason Game vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans are taking on their first of three preseason games on Thursday night , facing off against the Los Angeles Chargers in Reliant Stadium, also for the first game in their newly re-named stadium, formerly known as NRG Stadium dating back to 2014.
It marks the long-awaited return of the Texans back on an NFL field, which has been over seven months since we've last seen Houston competing in a live game. Now, the team is back, has a fresh season to take on, and will be trying to reach even higher than the heights they went to last year.
Here's a look at where and when you can watch the Texans' action against the Chargers on Thursday night:
Date: Aug. 13 Time: 7 p.m. CT Location: Reliant Stadium | Houston, TX
TV channel (national): N/A TV channel (local): ABC 13 (Houston), CBS LA (Los Angeles) Streaming: NFL+ | Fubo | ESPN+ Unlimited
It's two of three Texans games that are taking place on a Thursday, which includes next week's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20th.
Their third and final preseason game, against the Carolina Panthers on the road, will be on a Friday, August 28th. Both of Houston's next preseason games will also have a joint practice against that team during the days before ; a little different than the preparation against Los Angeles this week.
But of course, this being the first preseason game of the year, the first NFL football game on-screen in several months, and the implications these snaps have on the turnout of each team's 90-man roster, this matchup will have some more eyes on it than you might think. For the Texans, it could be the start of a potentially historic 25th-anniversary season.
Let's sort through what will be worth keeping a watch on for the Texans as their preseason officially gets underway.
- Who plays and who doesn't: DeMeco Ryans made it clear earlier in the week that a select few players would not play in Thursday's game. Who's going to be sidelined, and who's going to get a taste of the action? - What the offensive line looks like: How the Texans' offensive line performs is going to be a considerable talking point surrounding this team until the playoffs. Preseason will be no different. However, rather than just discussing how the line is holding up, who's getting the most reps there will also be worth jotting down. - The rookies' first preseason game: What often goes overlooked in any first preseason game is it's impact on rookies. This is their first experience in an NFL game, albeit an exhibition, and for a few, could be the start of a long, successful career. For Houston, how guys like Keylan Rutledge, Marlin Klein, and even guys like Lewis Bond and UDFA Collin Wright perform will be interesting.

title: 3 Biggest Things to Watch in Texans' Preseason Opener vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans kick off their first of three preseason games before the 2026 campaign at home on Thursday night against the Los Angeles Chargers.
It's a long-awaited return to the field for the Texans, as this will be the team's first time back in a live NFL game since their playoff exit against the New England Patriots back in January. And now, they get to start fresh in what could be an even better season from the one they're fresh off.
In their first preseason game against the Chargers, though, there will be a few storylines to keep an eye on as it relates to the Texans; some that can offer hints as to how the depth chart and 53-man roster could look come time for Week 1 after two weeks of training camp are now in the books .
Here are three of the biggest factors to be watchful of for the Texans in their Thursday night game against the Chargers:
The Texans' offensive line will look a little bit different heading into Week 1 of the regular season compared to how they wound up at the tail end of last year. And as preseason begins, we'll be able to land a first look at how we could expect this depth chart to be looking at the start of the 2026 campaign.
How will the Texans determine their first five starters? Will they hold out some of their expected starters to keep them fresh for closer to the season? How will rookies like Keylan Rutledge and Febechi Nwaiwu perform , and how much will Houston decide to play them? If the Texans are primarily running second and third-team offensive lines, who's lining up where and getting the most reps?
There's a ton of questions to be had for the Texans on their offensive line heading into the season, which is why it’s my number one factor to keep watch of as Houston begins preseason.
The first two weeks of the Texans' training camp has seen a couple of frequent highlight playmakers emerge as those who could make a run to the 53-man roster before Week 1 kicks off: wide receiver Lewis Bond and Collin Wright have probably been the two surprise performers hearing their names the most since Houston's been back on the field.
But now is the next step in their process to make noise on the 53-man roster: a live game against another team where both of them will be likely to get a high amount of snaps, given the circumstances.
It's a largely different scenario from what either of them has faced throughout their first steps in the league in practice and camp sessions. But a big performance from either would make their stock look even better heading into the season.
A huge question mark that's been in play throughout the Texans' first two weeks of camp: who will come out as the team's starting punter to start the season? And so far, there still hasn't been an exact verdict.
Kai Kroeger currently stands as the only punter on the roster after UDFA Jack Stonehouse was cut , but that doesn't mean Houston won't go out and sign another name to the 90-man roster for these next two preseason games, in the event that Kroeger struggles here against the Chargers.
That's what makes this game so important for Kroeger to take advantage of. If he can put together a big performance with consistent, positive punts when he's on the field, that can bolster his chances to make the 53-man roster in a big way. If he falls short, the conversation can easily shift in another direction.

title: Texans' Jadeveon Clowney Can Prove He's NFL's Biggest Bargain
full_text:
The Houston Texans are a little over a week removed from bringing in a big upgrade to their defensive line in Jadeveon Clowney .
The Texans had a ton of questions surrounding how they were going to attack their DE3 spot heading into the season. Clowney, a tested veteran who's been in the building once before, made a ton of sense to fill that spot, and now answers a ton of those lingering concerns Houston had off the edge .
And in order to do so, Clowney, who's now entering his 13th year in the NFL, took a pretty significant pay cut from what he'd typically be worth as a free agent––one that might end up making his contract one of the best in the league this season.
According to NFL insider Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 , the Texans will be paying Clowney a one-year, $8 million max value deal, with a base value of $5.5 million. Clowney will also have $4.5 million guaranteed on the contract.
#Texans three-time Pro Bowl edge Jadeveon Clowney one-year, $8 million max value deal: $2 million signing bonus, $2.5 million base salary (fully guaranteed), $58,823 per game active roster bonus, up to $1 million, $4.5 million total guaranteed, base value of $5.5 million, plus…
It's an extremely reasonable, borderline bargain deal for one of the better veteran edge rushers in the NFL. And when looking at what some of the top edge rushers on the market are making on their respective deals, the value looks even better for Houston.
An AAV of $5.5 million for Clowney barely lands within the top 60 of the NFL's highest-paid pass rushers in terms of cash.
According to Spotrac , $5.5 million in total cash is the same as New York Giants' defensive end/linebacker Chauncey Goldston. For reference, he played 10 games during the 2025 season to put together 1.0 sack and one start, playing in primarily special teams snaps.
As for Clowney, he proved he's still capable of playing well in the back-nine of his career in a rotational role with the Dallas Cowboys. And, as long as his production doesn't fall off a cliff in 2026, it will show that his contract is an extremely great deal for the Texans.
In 2025, Clowney played in 13 games with Dallas to put together 41 tackles, 12 TFLs, and 8.5 sacks, which makes for his third time in the past five seasons that he's had eight or more sacks in a year.
Even in what will be his age-33 season, Clowney is able to be respectable, high-end edge rusher who not only sets the edge and is a strong piece defending the run, has developed into a nice pass-rusher as well. His sack numbers have remained high, and could remain around the same in Houston.
But that impact for Clowney might be able to become further heightened on a defensive line like Houston's when he's paired with guys like Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter on the edge with him.
Clowney's individual numbers could see a slight dip, and his snap count could see the same effect, but he allows the Texans to rotate between all three of their high-end edge rushers and create what might just be the best three-man group off the edge in the entire league.
Clowney can play alongside either Anderson and Hunter when the other player is off the field, and really make this defensive line a tough task to stop on every down.
No matter if it’s a pairing of Anderson-Hunter, Hunter-Clowney, or Anderson-Clowney, this edge rush is a problem and offered a fit for Clowney that was hard to replicate with other teams––especially so when factoring in his history being the top draft pick to Houston in 2014.
For many teams, Clowney could be as high up the depth chart as their DE1, and in the process, have a near-double-digit sack season, while playing for a higher contract than what the Texans are paying him.
But Clowney chose to prioritize his role and his place on a winning team to make his fit in Houston come to fruition. And if those efforts from the Texans' former No. 1 pick make it result in a Super Bowl , there's going to be little debate that his $5.5 million contract is one of the best deals in the entire NFL.

title: Texans Sign Rookie Kicker Chris Freeman: Why Houston Added Him
full_text:
The Houston Texans are making a signing at kicker.
According to the Houston Chronicle 's Jonathan M. Alexander, the Texans are bringing in rookie kicker Chris Freeman to their 90-man roster.
The #Texans have signed rookie kicker Chris Freeman, while waiving WR Montrell Washington. This will allow Houston to give K Ka'imi Fairbairn a break.
In a corresponding move, the Texans also released recently-signed wide receiver Montrell Washington, therefore slimming Houston's deep receiver room by one, and allowing them to bring in a second kicker to their 90-man roster .
Freeman will, of course, be joining the Texans' veteran Ka'imi Fairbairn, as the second kicker in Houston, who is the longest-tenured player on the roster, being onboard dating back to 2017.
The Texans aren't signing Freeman as any type of competition for Fairbairn. If he were, Houston wouldn't have signed Fairbairn to a lucrative two-year extension earlier this offseason.
Instead, Freeman is in Houston as a bit of a tryout for himself, but also to give the Texans' veteran kicker a break during the preseason games ahead.
DeMeco Ryans already made it clear earlier this week that a select few players around the roster would be held out of Thursday's preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers; a strategy many teams implement in the first, or sometimes, all of their preliminary showings to keep them rested for the regular season.
For Fairbairn, it seems as if the Texans are trending towards holding him out of those preseason games. But, as every football team does, Houston will need a kicker for their first game of the year on Thursday––even if they don't intend to sign him to the 53-man roster.
So the Texans went out and brought in Freeman, who comes off of four years playing college ball between the UConn Huskies and the Indiana Hoosiers, and now looks to make the jump to the NFL.
During the last season that Freeman played in UConn, Freeman had 23 field goal makes on 26 attempts. He made all of his 52 field goal attempts throughout the year, and two of his three misses were from 40-49 yards. He was 9-11 from that range.
It was his best season by far at the college level, and a big jump from his previous year with the Huskies, where he made less than 80% of his field goals. Now, he's making 88.5% of them and didn't miss a field goal for a second straight season.
So he's found the opportunity in the NFL after showcasing a ton of his skillset in the past couple of seasons. But the Texans, in all likelihood, won't bring Freeman aboard onto their 53-man roster. They'll have Fairbairn onboard to handle their kicking duties , as he's done for the past several seasons.
At the very least, though, Freeman will be able to get his film in front of NFL personnel, and the hope is that his showing leads to either a practice squad addition in Houston, elsewhere, or even a 53-man roster signing around the league where a team is in need of a kicker.
His first showcase will, most likely, come on Thursday against the Chargers, kicking off at 7 p.m. CT.

title: 5 Surprises Spotted in Texans' First Preseason Depth Chart
full_text:
The Houston Texans released their first unofficial depth chart heading into preseason later this week, giving us a peek into who on the 90-man roster places where , and what their role could be shaping up to look like.
Of course, there were several spots on that depth chart that weren't surprising by any means. Truly, a lot of the Texans' starters, especially on defense, are looking to be the same as they were from when they ended last season.
However, that doesn't mean there weren't a few surprises of note in that depth chart release either. A few players wound up ranking just a little higher (or lower) than many might've expected entering the first week of preseason action.
Let's sort through five of those more surprising listings on Houston's depth chart:
The Texans' preseason star rookie in the receiving room, sixth-rounder Lewis Bond , still might have work to do before he's deemed a true difference-maker, or even a roster lock, based on his standing in the depth chart. He's still listed as a third-stringer, and not within the top-six slots in the room.
There's certainly still time for Bond to make a bigger dent in the wide receiver room. Especially with preseason around the corner, some extended reps, and big plays, his way could slot him in at that WR6 spot––which should be his goal. Until then, the veteran, Justin Watson, may have the edge.
Another rookie who hasn't risen too far up the depth chart: second-round tight end Marlin Klein is fifth in the pecking order at his position, following up each of Foster Moreau, Cade Stover, and Brevin Jordan, in that order.
And it's not exactly too unexpected to not come along as quickly as some other first-year guys, like Keylan Rutledge. And even if he is tight end five, that won't prevent him from making the roster as a day-two rookie. But if his standing is a sign of anything, his rise in the depth chart might be a more gradual process .
Even after the Texans decided to guarantee more of Jarrett Patterson's contract ahead of their first preseason game, that didn't stop them from putting him a bit lower on the totem pole in the offensive line room. He ranked third at right guard behind Ed Ingram and rookie Febechi Nwaiwu.
And that's far from a sign that Patterson isn't in line to make the roster. The numbers on his contract–– which make it appear more likely he'll make the cut ––matter more than a preseason depth chart. If anything, his placement at right guard just showcases Patterson's versatility as someone who can play both guard spots and center.
The Texans solved their third defensive end questions by signing Jadeveon Clowney earlier this month. But with Clowney now locking that spot up , the fourth defensive end spot becomes the latest position battle that's up for grabs on Houston's front seven.
Based on the first depth chart listing, though, those rights are in Dylan Horton's hands, who was right there with Dominique Robinson getting the most looks for that DE3 spot before Clowney came on. Keep watch of Robinson and Solomon Byrd, though, who are the next two in line as a third-string defensive end.
The Texans' linebacker position still feels extremely wide open, with a verdict to be determined in the next couple of weeks, rather than being one that's been sorted out by the first preseason games. However, there is one player who might be falling behind in the race at the position, and that's fourth-year linebacker Jamal Hill, who fell into fourth-string on Houston's depth chart.
This could very well be considered a make-or-break camp and preseason for Hill. He's by no means a roster lock, and is in a linebacker room that's some of the most wide-open it's been since his arrival three years ago. He entered late July as someone who could be one of the biggest risers, or one of the biggest fallers, and seems to be leaning towards the latter side of that right now.

title: 6 Texans Roster Battles That Could Be Decided in Preseason
full_text:
The Houston Texans' preseason debut is right around the corner. And as the Texans begin their first of three exhibitions before the regular season, there are still several position battles around the roster that are yet to be determined.
These preseason games on the horizon–– kicking off with the LA Chargers on Thursday ––can be a big help for the Texans to sort out those position battles. If one player shows out in those in-game reps, or continues to have the hot hand from camp, or if another disappoints, that could be the turning point in a select few undetermined position battles.
With that in mind, let's unpack six position battles on the Texans' depth chart that could be up in the air as preseason gets underway.
The Texans' wide receiver room is largely sorted out heading into the season––except for the back-end of their depth chart, and whether the team decides to roster six or seven wideouts on the opening-day unit.
Lewis Bond has made a ton of traction to become a part of the 53-man roster since OTAs. Justin Watson could still be due for a role after returning from an Achilles injury, and even someone like Jared Wayne has been making plays in camp as of late that make him a dark horse to watch.
The Texans' tight end room, which is as deep as it's been since DeMeco Ryans arrived as head coach, still has yet to seen a verdict surface as to who's the top backup to Dalton Schultz, and really, who are the two, and maybe even three players who will be lining up behind that TE2 past the 53-man cut.
Since the start of camp, Cade Stover might be the player seeing his stock climb the most, and Brevin Jordan has seen his stock drop the most . He’s injured, which certainly doesn't help. Expect preseason to be a big aid in determining which tight end is due for a big role in this offense, and who's not.
The Texans' right tackle spot is yet to be determined, and really, might've shifted in a different direction compared to what the expectation looked like earlier this offseason. Trent Brown and Braden Smith are about neck-and-neck in their race to start.
The case for both is easy. For Brown, he's been someone the Texans have been confident in since he was starting last season, and he hasn't lost a game as a starter in Houston . For Smith, he's being paid $20 million and was one of the team's most expensive free agent signings this offseason. Will all of that be to sit on the bench?
For a long time, the Texans' defensive line was expected to have a DE3 battle ongoing around this part of camp. But Jadeveon Clowney has since answered those questions pretty confidently. Now, the debate resides in who will be the first guy getting snaps behind their top three names in Clowney, Danielle Hunter, and Will Anderson.
Dylan Horton and Dominique Robinson will be the two players getting the most looks their way, as they were for the Texans' DE3 job earlier this camp. But others like Ali Gaye and Solomon Byrd will be worth keeping an eye on as well.
The Texans' linebacker room still looks pretty wide open heading into preseason, and that became even more so after Houston saw Jake Hansen go down with an ankle injury and then placed their replacement signing, Sione Takitaki, on the reserve/injured list shortly after bringing him in. Who the LB3 and LB4 will be in Week 1 is still to be determined.
As per the Texans' unofficial depth chart, the two leaders to get the most snaps at the position behind Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o are Wade Woodaz and Marte Mapu. But if that depth chart is a sign of anything to expect, multiple other names in the room can change that and their stock in the preseason games ahead.
The Texans' top three cornerbacks feel easy to pick out: Derek Stingley, Kamari Lassiter, and Jaylin Smith, the team's third-round pick for a year ago. But the top name to appear on the depth chart after those three might be tougher to predict based on the start we've seen to training camp.
The biggest riser throughout the Texans' entire camp so far might just be UDFA cornerback Collin Wright , who's continuously made plays in practice that’ve really put him in the hunt for this CB4 spot. Don't forget about veteran Tremon Smith either, who filled in for Jaylin Smith on defense for a large part of last year and remained a key piece on special teams.

title: Keylan Rutledge Fights Will Anderson at Texans Camp, DeMeco Ryans Reacts
full_text:
The Houston Texans' first-round pick from this year's draft, offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge, just keeps on getting into fights at training camp .
After a little over a week had taken place in Texans camp, Rutledge had gotten into–– by my count–– four fights with opposing defenders after a play. And on Tuesday during practice, the rookie offensive lineman got into another skirmish.
This time, though, it was with somebody that not many offensive linemen––whether they're on Houston or an opposing team––don’t tend to mess with much: Texans All-Pro defensive end Will Anderson Jr.
Keylan Rutledge and Will Anderson Jr. just got into it. That’s rare for Anderson.
It was a fight that, while nothing totally malicious between Rutledge and Anderson, was able to get the attention of Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans after practice had finished.
And really, while Ryans isn't going to be one who is onboard with physically fighting, he seemed to be a bit of a supporter of the aggression his rookie showcased in that type of moment:
"Better be careful there messing with Will Anderson," Ryans said on Tuesday. "I love it. I love the scrappiness of Keylan. His mindset is what I love. He's not backing down from anybody; as he shouldn't. I expect that from every player on our team."
"We know we're not physically fighting. But there's always chippiness in our game. It's a tough, physical, violent game that we play, and there's going to be some chippiness that goes on. We just have to make sure that we're smart, especially in-game, to make sure we're not that second guy to cause the team to hurt us."
For chippy moments like that in which Rutledge showcases that relentless attitude, it's a perfect reminder of just why the Texans were interested in investing such a high draft pick into his skillset, and perhaps even more so, his mindset.
He's a tough-minded, S.W.A.R.M. player that the Texans and DeMeco Ryans loved to have on any side of the ball, but especially on this new-look offensive line that's looking to take some big steps forward in 2026.
Rutledge has shown some great progress in his development as a pro, especially in his change from guard to center, to warrant the confidence that he can be a long-term piece on the offensive line . As a result, he might have the inside track to being named a starter on this front in Week 1, and has the standing on Houston's unofficial depth chart.
But mentally, the rookie has all of the traits the Texans love as well, which have, and will continue to, only begin to get more clear with time.
And just maybe, a few teammates may get into a spat with Rutledge in training camp as a result, even if it's against somebody who has the status like Anderson Jr. does, who's not exactly one to get into a shouting match too often.

title: Colts' Cam Bynum Seizing Green Dot Opportunity With CJ Allen Out
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts entered training camp expecting rookie linebacker CJ Allen to have a real chance at becoming the voice of Lou Anarumo’s defense. Two weeks later, veteran free safety Cam Bynum may be taking control of that responsibility.
Bynum is currently wearing the green dot for Indianapolis, giving him the in-helmet communication with Anarumo and the responsibility of relaying calls to the rest of the defense.
The move makes plenty of sense. Anarumo has used a safety in this role before, including Vonn Bell in Cincinnati, and explained that having a veteran defensive back handle the communication can take pressure off a young linebacker.
It also helps that Bynum has proven he can handle just about everything Indianapolis has asked from him. He led the Colts with four interceptions last season and has continued making plays throughout camp.
Bynum reinforced that during Tuesday’s joint practice with the New England Patriots, intercepting Drake Maye in the end zone to finish a two-minute drill. At this point, Bynum has a legitimate case as the best defender on this roster.
“If it’s a deep ball and I gotta run back to the huddle, that’s probably the most challenging thing,” Bynum said. “But it’s a fun thing to be able to be looked at by (DC Lou Anarumo), for him to trust me. … I know I can do it.”
There should not be much concern about whether Bynum can handle the responsibility. The bigger question is whether Allen can do enough once healthy to take it back.
Anarumo has been clear that Allen has not lost the green dot because of poor performance. When asked how the rookie had operated with the role, Anarumo said, “Really good, no issues at all.”
“We didn’t take it away from him,” Anarumo said. “It’s just that I feel like Cam needs to get practice at it just in case.”
The problem for Allen is that those missed practice reps are beginning to add up .
Indianapolis’ second-round pick has missed six of the team’s first ten training camp practices. A calf issue kept him out of the first two before a hamstring injury forced him to miss four consecutive sessions, including Tuesday’s joint practice against New England.
In Allen’s absence, the Colts have continued rotating linebackers such as Akeem Davis-Gaither, Bryce Boettcher, Austin Ajiake and Jaylon Carlies through first-team work. Meanwhile, Bynum has received valuable time communicating the entire defense.
Allen still has every opportunity to establish himself once he returns. He wore the green dot at Georgia, immediately handled the responsibility when he first returned to Colts practice and has given Anarumo no reason to question whether he can eventually handle the job.
But training camp reps are valuable, especially for a 21-year-old rookie preparing to command an NFL defense. Every practice Allen misses gives Bynum another opportunity to make the role his own.
The Colts may eventually decide Allen is still the best long-term option to wear the green dot. For now, Bynum is proving there may be no reason to rush that decision.
Allen can still become one of the most important pieces of this defense . But until he gets back on the field, Bynum’s grip on the green dot only gets stronger.

title: Indianapolis Colts Rookie Report Entering Preseason Play
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts ' 2026 NFL Draft class has been slowly but surely acclimating to the next level.
The Colts are counting on their rookie class to contribute in year one , and training camp has been a great first look at the feasibility of said ask. This past week saw the Colts put on pads for the first time since the 2025 regular season concluded, and we got to see just how pro-ready their 2026 draft class is.
From developmental pieces to first-year starters and/or contributors, this class has it all.
Follow along as I break down each of the Colts' rookies' training camp showings through two weeks of practice, just in time for their first taste of NFL football against the New England Patriots to kick off preseason play.
The Colts' top draft pick (53rd overall) of their most recent class has been sidelined for the majority of training camp thus far, missing six of the team's ten practices.
CJ Allen was held out of the team's first two training camp practices as he worked back from a minor calf injury, but was soon sidelined again after injuring his hamstring. Allen has missed four consecutive practices, including a joint practice against the New England Patriots , as he deals with his nagging hamstring injury.
He could certainly be activated in time for the Colts' first preseason game against the Patriots, which takes place later this evening, but Allen missing as much valuable time as he has is concerning for someone who is expected to be defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo's green dot as a rookie .
The Colts' rookie safety has been given a massive opportunity during his first NFL training camp.
A.J. Haulcy has been battling with second-year safety Hunter Wohler for the Colts' starting role at strong safety. However, Wohler has only recently returned to the gridiron after being sidelined for several consecutive practices with a hamstring injury, which has opened the door for Haulcy to slide in as the Colts' de facto starting safety alongside veteran Cam Bynum.
Haulcy has had a quietly promising training camp and notched his first interception against Daniel Jones in the Colts' last practice before they departed for their week in Massachusetts. His first preseason showing will be a great next step in determining just how impactful he can be in year one, on top of being the first opportunity to prove himself as the best man for the starting job in question.
The Colts have been high on rookie guard Jalen Farmer since they drafted him early in the fourth round (113th overall).
Farmer has exclusively worked with the Colts' second-team offense throughout training camp. He had tons of offseason hype that suggested he'd be a contender for a starting job on the right side of the offensive line, but as training camp's end sits on the horizon, Farmer appears destined to be the next successful draft-and-stash player developed by OL Coach Tony Sparano Jr.
The Colts' other rookie linebacker has not only been a full participant in each of their ten training camp practices thus far, but has also taken the majority of the first-team reps among all rostered linebackers.
Bryce Boettcher has been viewed as a potential day-one starter since he was drafted, and especially after his strong spring showing, and it's now looking like he'll be more than just a sub-package defender who contributes on special teams as a rookie.
I thought George Gumbs Jr. was destined for a practice squad designation after his raw prospect profile suggested he'd benefit from a pseudo-redshirt rookie season , but a quietly strong training camp has claimed otherwise .
Tonight's preseason opener against the New England Patriots will be a necessary next step in determining whether Gumbs Jr.'s training camp performance is any indication of his impact in year one.
Caden Curry is an Indianapolis-area (Greenwood, IN) native, and although his return home is a fun story, his training camp showing has suggested that he'll benefit from practice squad duties in year one. Curry's productivity at Ohio State has yet to translate to the next level, but he still has enough intangibles to continue betting on for the long haul.
The Colts' lone addition to the running back room this offseason came via a seventh-round pick, but Seth McGowan has played nothing like a near-undrafted rookie player.
McGowan has taken full advantage of second-year running back DJ Giddens' extended absence from the gridiron and now looks to be the de facto RB2 heading into the 2026 regular season. He has since shown that he can be a solid passcatcher out of the backfield after his first week of training camp suggested otherwise, and now he can solidify himself as the Colts' best backup option in preseason play.
The Indianapolis Colts desperately need help in their wide receiver room, and although seventh-round rookie Deion Burks has flashed at times throughout training camp, it's hard to see a world where he's a key contributor on gamedays during the regular season.
Burks has been a regular rotator for the Colts' punt returner role, but outside of some scattered strong catch-and-runs with the reserve teams, he's yet to emerge as a potential year-one contributor on offense.

title: Colts Bout With Patriots Is Anthony Richardson Sr.'s Most Important Game
full_text:
The story of Anthony Richardson Sr.'s three years with the Indianapolis Colts can be summed up in one word: sad.
Later tonight, the Colts will kick off their 2026 preseason at Gillette Stadium against the New England Patriots. While there is a plethora of players to watch , perhaps none will draw more attention than Richardson.
According to Shane Steichen, he'll start the game and play the first two halfs, with Riley Leonard finishing up the last portion. These two, of course, are competing for the backup QB job behind Daniel Jones.
While it's just a preseason game, it's perhaps the most important game of Richardson's career heading into year four after three seasons of utter disappointment.
In this piece, I'll detail just why this game holds so much weight for the embattled former fourth-overall pick.
Make no mistake, Richardson is still seeking a trade partner. However, nothing has materialized since it was requested back in February.
That means that he's still fighting for the QB2 role with Leonard. Since Richardson didn't put together an ideal training camp, he'll need to look much better against New England to have a chance of beating out Leonard.
We got a brief glimpse of Richardson's preseason performance last year, and the highlight was a brutal one.
In Week 1 of the 2025 preseason, Richardson faced the Baltimore Ravens, and let's just say it didn't end well.
In the first quarter, Richardson failed to identify the free runner, David Ojabo. This resulted in Richardson getting destroyed. This led to an injury to his throwing hand.
Anthony Richardson injured on this David Ojabo sack pic.twitter.com/BmiLEdpBuL
These are the mistakes that Richardson can't afford to make. There were so many wrinkles to this play.
Not only did Richardson not identify the unblocked defender, but he also avoided both of his hot reads while staring toward the wrong side of the field.
Richardson doesn't necessarily need to light the world on fire tonight, but he needs to be efficient, accurate, and intelligent under center. These are the basic requirements of an NFL quarterback, which he hasn't shown to this point.
If Richardson looks good and in control of Steichen's offense, he'll make a case to battle out Leonard to backup Jones.
Not only will this help solidify himself one play away from getting on the field should something happen to Jones, but it will also rise his stock across the league.
Since Richardson's trade request is still active, and Indianapolis hasn't negated it, that means this game, and the rest of the preseason, could be an audition to land in a new destination.
The fact that no deal has happened in six months for a Richardson trade shows what the NFL thinks of the field general: they aren't willing to do business with Indianapolis until he shows something more.
Is there a wild chance that Indianapolis opts to keep Richardson should he show out against New England? Of course, anything is possible in the NFL.
However, the far more likely scenario is that Indianapolis hopes he plays well to recoup some capital after mortgaging their future on him with a fourth-overall selection.
If Richardson goes out there and shows poise, accuracy, and an ability to take care of the football, we could see a deal done after so many months of waiting.
If Richardson looks like he has in the past, or worse, it could lead to outcomes that the former Florida Gator wants to avoid.
Some of those include being relegated to QB3, or worse, becoming a cut candidate ahead of Indianapolis trimming the roster down to 53 names.
I think the outcome that he gets cut only happens if he looks absolutely horrendous. The unfortunate reality is, he has been that way multiple times throughout his career.
Hopefully, Richardson has a good game, but it can't be ruled out that he'll spiral out of control since he's done it before.
It could be seen as a hot take, but it's really not out of the question to call this preseason game the most important of Richardson's career.
While it's not against New England's elite competition, it's still a huge sample that Richardson needs to make tasty.
Everyone's eyes will be glued to what he does on the field tonight, and that includes any NFL teams that could be in the market to add another quarterback.
The future of the NFL's most athletic quarterback is on the line in what's considered an otherwise low-level game.
Let's see if he can dial back the mistakes, disappointment, and wild inefficiency in a game that could decide his professional football career.

title: Winners From Colts Joint Practice vs. Patriots: Tyler Warren Remains Top Target
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts had their first opportunity to showcase their new-look roster against an opposing NFL team ahead of the regular season on Tuesday.
The Colts traveled to Foxborough, Massachusetts, for some scrimmaging against the New England Patriots before they kick off preseason play on Thursday , and by all accounts, it was a lively affair.
While Colts On SI did not make the trek for this week's festivities, we, of course, followed along from afar. With help from both the Colts and Patriots beat reporters who are boots on the ground this week, I'm covering which Colts stood out in their first joint practice of the preseason.
For starters, the Colts had some much-needed reinforcements return to the gridiron for their joint practice against the New England Patriots.
WR Josh Downs (groin), CB Justin Walley, S Hunter Wohler (hamstring), and WR Laquon Treadwell (hamstring) all returned to practice. At the same time, WR Alec Pierce continued making progress in his recovery from left ankle surgery.
Pierce had his cleats on for the first time this offseason, and while he ultimately remained sidelined for ramp-up individual work, this was a great first step back.
General manager Chris Ballard said there has been no setback in Pierce’s recovery and clarified that Pierce did not receive a second PRP injection following surgery, despite a recent report claiming that he did.
It wasn't all promising on the injury news front, however. Rookie linebacker CJ Allen missed his fourth consecutive practice with a nagging hamstring injury, while cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. was sidelined for the first time all camp due to back pain and irritation.
The Colts' second-year tight end continues to prove that he's the offense's most reliable passcatcher.
Tyler Warren was an active contributor across both 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 play against the New England Patriots on Tuesday, hauling in multiple receptions throughout the day and peaking during the scrimmage's simulated two-minute warning period.
“He’s just a tremendous player. He's got a natural feel, a natural knack for the game on how to get open, how to run routes, and he makes plays. He's got strong hands, big body, big target for Daniel (Jones) to throw to," Colts head coach Shane Steichen said about Tyler Warren's presence in the Colts' offense.
The Colts' longtime defensive tackle has been known for plugging up the middle of the trenches, and that was on full display during their joint practice against the New England Patriots on Tuesday. Stewart was credited with blowing up numerous rushes up the pipe and was viewed as one of the biggest winners on both sides.
"That Grover Stewart, whoa," ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss said about the longtime defensive tackle's showing on Tuesday . "He might have been the best player on the field yesterday."
Head coach Shane Steichen's Colts offense struggled in the first half of practice, but found their footing late as they cruise-controlled to success against the New England Patriots' defense.
All three quarterbacks -- Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson, and Riley Leonard -- each had promising showings in 7-on-7 play in the red zone, but it was Jones who emerged during the scrimmage's simulated two-minute warning session to conclude practice.
Jones was finding Tyler Warren early and often during the simulated drive in question, before he connected with Josh Downs for a buzzer-beating touchdown to end the session.
Furthermore, their rushing attack saw each of its active running backs -- Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan, and Ulysses Bentley IV -- find paydirt throughout the day.
On the flip side, 2025 MVP runner-up quarterback Drake Maye reportedly got the best of the Colts' passing defense for much of the day, but safety Cam Bynum made sure to have the last laugh after baiting Maye into a throw he shouldn't have made during the Patriots' starting offense's two-minute drive.
It wasn't a performance that suggested a Super Bowl run is on the menu, but at least the Colts showed up when it mattered most and got some much-needed positive injury updates ahead of their preseason opener on Thursday .

title: 5 Colts Looking to Show Up Big in Preseason Clash With Patriots
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts begin their 2026 preseason tomorrow against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts.
There will be plenty of position battles to be on the lookout for, but also individual players who have a lot at stake in this preseason opener.
For this piece, we'll take a look at the top five players to watch closely on Thursday with a pivotal season just around the corner.
CJ Allen has missed a majority of training camp with a hamstring issue, which has opened the door for other linebackers to run with the first team.
A name we've heard plenty of from Colts training camp has been rookie Bryce Boettcher. Despite being a fourth-round selection (135th overall), he's shown out in a big way.
Allen figures to return to action, but Boettcher has clearly drawn the interest of defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo.
#Colts LB Bryce Boettcher on getting first-team reps: “I don’t really know if I expected it or not. I just kind of expected that the best player who shows the best effort and plays the fastest should play. They’ve given me a good opportunity to showcase my ability so far. …” pic.twitter.com/pJTyrskITh
If he can deliver an impressive performance against the Patriots, it will help him carry that momentum and improve his chances of being a factor in Indy's linebacker rotation.
Arguably, the biggest question mark for the Colts defense is the edge rusher position opposite Laiatu Latu.
Currently, the position battle to watch is between Jaylahn Tuimoloau and veteran Arden Key.
However, Tuimoloau is coming off a less-than-ideal rookie year, which makes this preseason tilt a big one for the former Ohio State Buckeye.
There's a real shot that Indianapolis ends up approaching this defensive end position with a rotation between Tuimoloau and Key.
However, if Tuimoloau can put things together with his valuable reps on Thursday, he could give himself a leg up in the race for playing time.
The Colts want to win and will give more starter reps to the better player. But I'd put good money on the fact that the franchise wants to see their 2025 second-round investment take a big leap forward.
Safety Hunter Wohler has dealt with a hamstring issue just like Allen, which has kept him out of a load of training camp practices this year.
Luckily, Wohler returned for the Tuesday joint practice against the Patriots. After such a fantastic 2025 training camp and preseason, Wohler fell to a season-ending Lisfranc injury.
Up to that point, he was tearing it up, which wasn't expected since he was Indy's final selection of the 2025 NFL Draft with the 232nd pick.
Wohler has displayed excellent football instincts, pursuit angles, and an ability to take the football away in past practices.
Even with the assumption that third-rounder A.J. Haulcy will start at strong safety, this is a huge game for Wohler on Thursday to cement himself a spot in Anarumo's rotation.
Anarumo's defense is predicated on cornerback and safety efficiency, and Wohler will have the chance to show that he's ready to be a factor in the game plan.
I could have just as easily placed Nick Westbrook-Ikhine into this category, as he and Ashton Dulin are battling it out for the WR3 spot behind Alec Pierce and Josh Downs.
But Dulin has been with Indianapolis for seven years, and this is arguably the best chance he'll get to become more to the team than just a special teams ace.
Given that Pierce won't be playing on Thursday, Dulin will be featured in Shane Steichen's offense, giving him ample opportunity to shine.
Dulin is an explosive pass-catcher who hasn't been able to get into the prominent receiver rotation throughout his career.
This preseason is massive for the veteran, and that all begins on Thursday with the opener against New England.
Anthony Richardson Sr. is at the end of his road with the Colts. The former fourth-overall selection has been named the starter against the Patriots, giving him a platform to make up for what's been an otherwise disappointing offseason.
#Colts head coach Shane Steichen shared Anthony Richardson will start at QB against the Patriots, with Riley Leonard playing the second half. He also said Daniel Jones will not be playing in any preseason game. pic.twitter.com/eDEM6RyUG3
Richardson is listed as a co-QB2 on Indy's unofficial depth chart with Leonard, but the fact that he couldn't outright win the backup position is not a good sign.
It's not an exaggeration to say that Richardson's time with Indianapolis has been a complete disaster.
He's on tap to get plenty of snaps in the preseason, but as the undisputed starter for the debut against the Patriots, he'll need to have a great showing.
This is still a competition for the backup position. If Richardson can put things together in the first half against New England, it will give him a much-needed piece of momentum.
On the other hand, if he plays wild and can't operate the offense well, it will put him in a brutal spot and give Leonard a clearer path to backup Daniel Jones.

title: 3 Colts' Position Battles to Watch in Preseason Opener vs. Patriots
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts finally face off against someone other than their teammates as they begin their preseason slate against the New England Patriots on Thursday night.
The Colts and Patriots participated in a joint practice on Tuesday against the reigning AFC Champions. Head coach Shane Steichen was pleased with his team's performance, which saw the Colts end practice on a high note on both sides of the ball.
"It was great. Obviously, competitive," Steichen said. "Obviously, they played in the Super Bowl last year, so it was good to get that competition. ... A lot of back and forth. Ended it with the two-minute drive there at the end. Ones got some reps, Twos got some reps. Really pleased with the first offense going there, and same thing with the defense, Cam Bynum getting a pick there to end it. So, it was awesome.”
While Steichen admitted that most of the starters will not play in the preseason opener, the competition at multiple spots across the roster will be in full swing. Here are the top position battles to keep an eye on for the Colts in Foxborough.
Steichen revealed on Tuesday that Daniel Jones will not play in the preseason as the Colts focus on keeping him healthy and ready for the regular season. That means there will be ample snaps available for Anthony Richardson Sr. and Riley Leonard over the next few weeks.
Steichen announced that Richardson will start against the Patriots on Thursday and play the entire first half. Leonard will get his crack at it in the second half. The two will flip roles next week against the Atlanta Falcons, with Leonard getting the start.
The competition between Richardson and Leonard has been tight through the first two weeks of camp, with both quarterbacks experiencing ups and downs. While Leonard has started to gain a slight advantage, a strong performance from Richardson, in which he shows consistency and command of the offense, could tighten things up quickly.
The battle for WR3 behind Alec Pierce and Josh Downs has been an intriguing competition. Ashton Dulin started training camp as the overwhelming favorite to win the job. He has developed a rapport with Jones and has been on the receiving end of multiple touchdowns.
While Dulin is still the favorite – the veteran is only taking reps with the starters and none on special teams – Nick Westbrook-Ikhine has made the battle a little more interesting over the past week. Westbrook-Ikhine has the size to be a red zone target for Jones and the speed to take the top off any defense. The former Indiana Hoosier has made highlight plays on multiple occasions.
The wide receiver spot could be one of the only positions we see potential starters playing on Thursday. If Dulin does not play, the battle could be all but decided. However, if Dulin and Westbrook-Ikhine are both out there, it likely signals the competition is closer than we thought.
The kicking competition is one of the most important battles across the roster. Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader will each get a chance to kick on Thursday as special teams coordinator Brian Mason wants to ensure both kickers have as many opportunities as possible.
"All the kicks that we've charted or filmed, there's highs and lows to both guys," Mason explained. "I think it's been overall a solid work. Grupe overall is kicking 85 percent and Shrader's kicking 83 percent. The bigger differentiation is going to be when they go live. Shrader hasn't been kicking as consistently as Grupe when we've been going live. Obviously, everybody has seen those live kicks and kind of discussed or known that, and Grupe’s kicking 91 percent before (Saturday) when we've gone live. But we kind of look at the big picture overall.
"We're not judging who's the best kicker in the first two weeks. We're judging who is the best kicker to make us through the regular season that gives us the best chance to score points and win games."
Expect Grupe and Shrader to get close to the same number of attempts on Thursday night. Grupe holds the lead in the competition for now, but all it takes is a slight slump by either kicker to really impact the outcome of the battle.

title: Colts Get Much-Needed Reinforcements Back From Injury
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts finally received some positive news on the injury front Tuesday.
WR Josh Downs, CB Justin Walley, S Hunter Wohler and WR Laquon Treadwell all returned to practice, while WR Alec Pierce continued making progress in his recovery from left ankle surgery.
Indianapolis isn't entering this season with enough proven depth to comfortably absorb long-term injuries at important positions like years in the past. That is especially true at wide receiver, where Pierce has yet to return to full practice.
That makes Downs’ return from a groin injury even more significant. He missed practices over the weekend, but head coach Shane Steichen previously indicated the injury was not serious, and getting him back on the field Tuesday is an encouraging development.
Downs is too valuable to this offense for a relatively minor injury in August to turn into something that follows him into the regular season. Getting him back on the field is encouraging, but making sure the groin issue does not become a recurring problem matters even more.
Treadwell also returned from a hamstring injury Tuesday, giving Indianapolis another receiver back in the rotation.
The Colts WR room depth has already been tested throughout camp, making every healthy return at the position that much more valuable.
Walley’s return may be just as important for a defense that needs its young secondary pieces available.
The second-year cornerback missed his entire rookie season after suffering a torn ACL during a joint practice with the Baltimore Ravens last August. Walley had been one of Indianapolis’ biggest training camp standouts before the injury ended his season before he could play a regular-season snap.
Now, his second NFL training camp has already been interrupted by a hamstring injury.
Walley returned Tuesday and participated in team work, which is a positive step. However, his biggest challenge this season may be proving he can stay healthy enough to consistently show the talent Indianapolis saw from him last summer.
Two training camps have now been interrupted by injuries before Walley has played his first NFL snap.
Wohler finds himself in a similar situation after his rookie season was wiped out by a Lisfranc injury. He returned from a hamstring issue Tuesday and also participated in team drills.
For a defense lacking overwhelming depth across the board, getting both young defensive backs healthy could become increasingly important as Week 1 approaches.
Pierce may still be the injury situation worth watching closest.
The veteran receiver was on the field Tuesday doing individual work with a trainer and wearing cleats as he continues rehabbing from left ankle surgery.
General manager Chris Ballard said there has been no setback in Pierce’s recovery and clarified that Pierce did not receive a second PRP injection following surgery. Ballard also said Pierce is making “great progress” as he continues working his way back.
There is still no firm timeline for when Pierce will return to full practice, but the expectation remains that he will be available for the regular-season opener against Baltimore.
That makes every step forward between now and Week 1 worth monitoring.
The Colts are starting to get healthier, but this is not a roster that can afford for several important players to battle lingering injuries throughout the season. Getting Downs, Walley, Wohler and Treadwell back Tuesday was a strong start, while Pierce’s continued progress may be the most important development of them all.

title: Will Alec Pierce's Ankle be the Colts' Ultimate Undoing?
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts ' Alec Pierce has been sidelined since his last snap in Week 18 of the 2025 regular season, and he's had two important things happen in the subsequent offseason, both of which came in March: signing the richest deal for a free agent wide receiver in NFL history and undergoing ankle surgery.
The homegrown wide receiver certainly deserved a big payday after breaking out with over 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and leading the NFL in yards per catch (21.3) for the second year in a row.
However, despite being regarded as a necessary move that demanded a patient rehab process, concern for Pierce's eventual return has been mounting as of late.
Alec Pierce fought through pain in his ankle during his breakout campaign and decided to address the issue in the offseason before things worsened.
“It had been bothering me since the end of like the 2024 season, so just was dealing with that and kind of finding ways (to play)," Pierce explained to local reporters back in June. "But it definitely got a little bit worse as the season went, and probably the last month (of the season) I'd say was kind of struggling, affected practice, had taken some days off and stuff."
Pierce netted a monster four-year, $114 million deal in free agency earlier this offseason, and a few weeks later, had his aforementioned 'clean-up' procedure done on his ankle.
His return timeline was an estimated four-to-six months from late March, and while it's not a shock that Pierce has missed the Colts' first nine training camp practices after missing the entire offseason, it's still a bit concerning.
"Talking with the doctor, I think we determined that surgery was the smartest play for the long term," Pierce said. "They kind of were saying I was going to have to do it at some point. And then, when I asked them what the time frame was, he said, like, four to six months. It was like late March, so then I was like, 'Okay, four months gets me basically to camp.'"
"So, just hearing that time frame, then it was a quick turnaround, right?" he continued. "Because they were like, 'Okay, if we're going to do this, we've got to do this now.' ... Then I started talking about the risks (of waiting) and stuff like that. And I think we just determined that it was smart to take care of it now with the risks ... of having a worse injury happen during the season."
The Colts were aware of Pierce's situation going into contract talks and have been bracing for a speedy recovery ever since.
General manager Chris Ballard kicked off training camp by saying Pierce was "probably a week or two away," which has only aged poorly. The Colts are two weeks deep into training camp, and have their first preseason game on Thursday, yet Pierce remains sidelined.
Pierce received a platelet-rich plasma treatment in January to try to address his ankle pain, but when it proved to be nothing more than a quick fix, he turned to surgery. The Athletic's James Boyd reported that Pierce has received a second PRP injection , this one coming sometime after he inked his new deal.
"Pierce did not have a setback, the source said. He received the second PRP shot in late June to alleviate soreness and speed up his rehab, which the source emphasized is “not abnormal,'" Boyd said.
Ultimately, missing the preseason altogether has always been in the cards for Alec Pierce; however, the Colts truly cannot afford to lose him for any amount of time during the regular season, and especially early on, but they've made their bed, and now they must sleep in it.
The Indianapolis Colts are entering a make-or-break season that largely hinges on head coach Shane Steichen's offense returning to early-season form from a year ago, but their star wide receiver's rehab from an offseason surgery has kept him sidelined for the entirety of training camp thus far, which has produced a scary reality of what the wide receiver room would look like without him .
The Colts desperately need Pierce to return to the gridiron as soon as possible, but they also don't want to rush him.
"I think obviously we want the date to be as early as possible, but kind of got to let your body guide yourself and see how you feel because what I'm learning with the rehab is the more you overdo it, the more sore you get," Pierce admitted. "(It) can sometimes be counterproductive. So, I'm learning when to push through the pain and soreness and when to back off."
Reaggravating the issue in the preseason would be detrimental for all parties involved, and that simply can't be an option if the Colts want to exit their early regular-season gauntlet on a high note.
Ballard traded away longtime wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to afford Pierce earlier this offseason, and now they're betting on Pierce to replace Pittman Jr.'s production while Josh Downs and Tyler Warren do their thing, with special teams ace Ashton Dulin and friends picking up the scraps.
The Colts are hopeful that Pierce returns to practice before Week 1 arrives on September 13, but it's still concerning despite their understandable amount of patience shown.

title: Colts' Anthony Richardson, Riley Leonard Reveal Mindset on QB2 Battle
full_text:
One of the most talked-about position battles throughout Indianapolis Colts training camp is for a spot the Colts hope will never have to see the field.
With Daniel Jones fully entrenched as the starting quarterback, the competition has been for QB2 between Anthony Richardson Sr. and Riley Leonard. Richardson and Leonard have been splitting reps with the second-team offense through the first two weeks of camp. Neither has been able to separate themselves at this point in the competition.
Head coach Shane Steichen made it clear on Sunday what the deciding factor would be in who wins the battle.
"The guy that’s going to be most consistent is going to win that job," Steichen stated. "Those guys are battling. It’s back and forth right now. Obviously we will grade the tape, go through it and get better every day.”
Consistency has been something both quarterbacks have struggled with over the last couple of weeks. It has been an up-and-down training camp for both Richardson and Leonard. While both quarterbacks have flashed at times, they have made more mistakes than either would like to admit.
For Richardson, who requested a trade from the Colts back in February, his focus has been on improving his consistency on a down-by-down basis throughout the offseason.
"That’s something I've been trying to work on throughout the whole offseason," Richardson explained. "Just discipline, consistency, studying the playbook, coming out here making sure my footwork and everything is on point, coming out here trying to command the offense, just taking it day-by-day. Some days aren't my best days. Some days aren't the worst. So, I just got to keep pushing and like you said, just be consistent whenever I can."
Although Richardson requested a trade this spring, nothing has materialized for the former No.4 overall pick. There is a very real possibility that Richardson remains with the team in 2026, the final year of his rookie deal. Whether that is in the QB2 role or not will be determined by his ability to eliminate the peaks and valleys in his play that have plagued him throughout his career.
Meanwhile, Leonard's focus has been taking the next step in his pre-snap process. So much of what a quarterback does happens before the ball is even snapped.
Jones has excelled in this area during his time in Indy, as Steichen has consistently credited the veteran with making the right checks at the line of scrimmage to get the Colts into the right play. Leonard has attached himself to Jones' hip since he was drafted in the spring of 2025 and wants to emulate how the latter processes what the defense is doing before the ball is snapped.
"Something I've taken a step further in is understanding what the defense is doing a lot a lot better. Obviously, when you get to know the offense for a whole year, you don't have to think about the little things. ... Now I'm able to save (time) and really figure out what the defense is doing and get my eyes up. So mentally, I mean, this game and quarterback is all about pre-snap decisions, and I think I've done a great job of kind of understanding, maybe not exactly where the ball should go, but knowing where it shouldn't go.”
The competition between Richardson and Leonard remains tight as we head into the Colts' first preseason matchup with the New England Patriots. Steichen revealed after practice Sunday that both quarterbacks would split the reps during Thursday night's game, as Jones is not expected to play.
It will be interesting to see who Steichen starts at quarterback, as the decision could give us an early indication of which quarterback the Colts feel is ahead in the QB2 battle.
After a slow start, Leonard has settled in and is performing better in practice as of late. He has been more accurate with the football and has been receiving more reps with the second-team offense than Richardson. However, the second-year player has looked a bit slow in his decision-making and has taken too many would-be sacks.
Despite the slow start, Leonard sees progress in his game as camp has gone along.
"It's been a good couple days for me," Leonard said. "Obviously, when you're playing the quarterback position, sometimes it takes a while to get going. Sometimes you start off great. ... Tomorrow could be terrible. But I think today went pretty good, and I feel comfortable back there in the pocket, getting to know the new centers that I'm operating with and the receivers out here."
Richardson continues to show the flashes of why he was so enticing as a prospect while his mistakes have been damning. The athleticism and rocket arm are on full display, yet bouts of inaccuracy have made his performances erratic. Richardson has also struggled with multiple fumbled snaps both in shotgun and under center.
These are areas Richardson must clean up or risk falling too far behind in the competition.
"I was trying to find a few different things to do with my hands so I could see if I could catch the snap a little differently," Richardson remarked. "I started putting my hands out a little bit more, and it's been helping me. But it's just a little adjustment, got shoulder pads and stuff on now, bullets flying, people running fast around me. So, I feel like I figured out the problem.”
While the Colts are hoping for a full season from Jones, he has only accomplished that feat once in his seven-year career. Jones' injury history suggests the Colts will more than likely have to turn the offense over to Leonard or Richardson at some point this season.
The job is there for the taking. The Colts are just waiting for Leonard or Richardson to seize it.
