title: Biggest Takeaways From Colts' First Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts released their first unofficial depth chart Monday, and a few things immediately stand out. From a depleted wide receiver room to two major position battles, the preseason suddenly has plenty to sort out.
The wide receiver room may be the Colts’ biggest concern on offense right now. Alec Pierce continues working his way back from ankle surgery, while Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell have also missed practice time with injuries.
Ashton Dulin is currently listed as the third starting receiver ahead of Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and several inexperienced options make up much of the depth behind the starters.
Tyler Warren sits atop a six-man group featuring Mo Alie-Cox, Drew Ogletree, Will Mallory, Carson Towt and Pharaoh Brown. Carrying a crowded tight end room has been common throughout Shane Steichen’s tenure, but it could be even more important this season considering the uncertainty at receiver.
Warren is coming off an excellent rookie season, while Alie-Cox and Ogletree give Indianapolis experienced options behind him. The depth also gives Steichen plenty of flexibility to lean into heavier personnel if the wide receiver room remains thin.
Tanor Bortolini continues to establish himself at center. The third-year lineman sits firmly atop the depth chart and has developed into one of the strongest young pieces on the offensive line.
At running back, DJ Giddens is listed behind Jonathan Taylor with rookie Seth McGowan third. McGowan has been a bright spot while Giddens has dealt with a hamstring injury, making the seventh-round rookie worth watching this preseason.
Linebacker might be one of the weakest rooms on the roster. Rookie CJ Allen and Akeem Davis-Gaither are listed as starters, while Bryce Boettcher surprisingly sits third at WILL despite significant first-team work since the spring.
If rookies Allen and Boettcher can make an immediate impact, the outlook could change quickly.
The secondary has a much higher ceiling. Defensive backs Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward Sr., Justin Walley and Camryn Bynum headline a group capable of being elite if they stay healthy.
Rookie AJ Haulcy only adds to the excitement. He is listed as the starting strong safety ahead of Hunter Wohler and intercepted Daniel Jones during Sunday’s practice.
Backup quarterback and kicker remain the two biggest unresolved battles on the depth chart. Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson Sr. are co-listed behind Daniel Jones, while Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader remain co-listed at kicker.
Jones will sit Thursday against New England, giving Leonard and Richardson a chance to separate themselves. The same goes for Grupe and Shrader, with preseason performance likely to play a major role in deciding the job.
The depth chart is unofficial, but it gives Indianapolis a clear set of storylines to watch. Receiver health, the crowded tight end room and several young players could make this roster look much different by Week 1.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Jaguars Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times and TV Channels to Watch Liam Coen's Squad
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The preseason will officially kick off for the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday vs. the New Orleans Saints, starting a critical three-week period for Liam Coen's squad.
So, how can you keep up with the Jaguars during the start of the preseason? We break down all three weeks for you below.
The Jaguars will not be expected to play their starters in the preseason opener after the two sides held a joint practice on Thursday. This meant a ton of work for the starters and key backups, most of whom will now be sat for Saturday's preseason opener.
“Yeah, with limited overall reps throughout, even throughout a training camp, is, look, we're going to keep it fairly simple in terms of the formations, the motions, the coverages, the calls. I just want to see a clean operation. I mean, that, and then just go play," Coen said on Thursday about his expectations for the Jaguars' backups in the game on Saturday.
"Like, let's see who is going to be the guy that's going to go make plays when it's not perfect, right? We're not getting a ton of reps that maybe this play and, well, can you, can they fix it? Can they fix any problems on Saturday that maybe we haven't shown them? Who can do that operation? And then who's going to win some one-on-one matchups? Whether it's one-on-one pass pro, whether it's I'm covering the guy one-on-one, or whether I got to defeat a one-on-one matchup at receiver. Like, who's going to go do that?”
This is the fifth preseason matchup between the teams and the second consecutive year the Jaguars have visited the Saints in the preseason. In 2025, the meeting ended in a 17 -17 tie.
The Jaguars faced the Panthers in the regular-season last year in Week 1, which led to the Jaguars starting the Coen era off with a 1-0 record. The Panthers are returning most of their key pieces from that game, especially so with head coach Dave Canales and quarterback Bryce Young. The two teams last met in the preseason in 2017, though they used to play annually in the preseason when both teams joined the NFL in 1995.
Like the Jaguars did with the Saints, they will hold a joint practice session with the Panthers two days before they kick off next week for the second week of the preseason.
"Because you're in a little bit more of a controlled setting that you can get the guys you want specific reps and not have to worry about as much that you're putting a guy in a full-contact situation in preseason games that don't count against our schedule record," Coen said this offseason when explaining why he favored joint practices.
This one will be filled with storylines. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their base didn't exactly take it well when Coen left their coordinator role to take the Jaguars' job, and now some of that bad blood can be exercised over the course of two joint practices and then a preseason finale. As Coen said in March, it only makes sense for the Jaguars and Buccaneers to hold practices together, something they last did in 2024.

title: 10 Winners, 5 Losers From Mid-Point of Jaguars Training Camp
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Training camp is at the mid-way point, the preseason is here, and the Jacksonville Jaguars are just a month away from kicking off in Week 1 against the Cleveland Browns.
With so many practice days under the Jaguars' belts so far, here is a look at each of the risers and fallers from training camp thus far, starting with a few key names.
If there has been a leading receiver from training camp so far, it has been Parker Washington. It doesn't seem like the fourth-year wide receiver has anything else to prove to earn a new contract from the team before he becomes a free agent in March, because he has checked every single box in this year's training camp. He is my current pick to lead the Jaguars this year in receiving yards.
"Parker's never changed. He's always been the same guy. The stuff I saw just social media-wise, him coming in, working, that's always been him," Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange said about Washington, his college teammate, earlier this week. "He is the star player that he is because of the work that he puts in. No surprise by me. I've been seeing it for the past however many years, but yeah, it's just on this stage now, so nothing different.”
Travis Hunter has been nothing short of terrific for the Jaguars in training camp. He has taken a full workload in every practice since the Jaguars kicked things off on Day 1 of camp, he has spent extensive time at both cornerback and wide receiver, and he has made the kind of plays on both side of the ball that have made it clear how special of a player he is and always has been.
“Done a really good job. I think he's taken a big jump. I think he's spent a lot of good time with Mat [Defensive Pass Game Coordinator Mathieu Araujo] even off the field, learning the system. Just a little bit more fluid for him, easier for him to communicate. I think he knows it a little bit better," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said this week. "Obviously, we talked about his body physically. He's a different guy right now physically, which is great but I think he's done a great job balancing both. Which in camp, it's a lot, they are long days, and you're on both sides. And he's done a really good job compartmentalizing when he's with us."
Jaguars running back LeQuint Allen was talked up by the Jaguars all offseason when it came to his potential as a pass-catcher , and he has since seen the Jaguars involve him more in the passing game in training camp as a result. He is going to play a ton of third downs for the Jaguars this year, so he might as well get the ball thrown his way.
I thought Danny Striggow was a lock to win the DE3 job for the Jaguars in training camp, but so far it has seemed like that role belongs to B.J. Green. The second-year defensive end has gotten first-team defensive reps this summer and has been able to dominate the offensive linemen across from him in both the pass and running game more often than not. He looks like he is about to play a ton for the Jaguars this season.
Matt Dickerson was the backup to Arik Armstead on the Jaguars' first unofficial depth chart of the season, a sign of the faith the Jaguars have in the veteran backup. Dickerson did good things for the Jaguars' defensive tackle rotation a year ago and he has gotten plenty of snaps with the first-team defense in training camp as a result. He looks like he will make the 53-man roster.
Perhaps no cornerback has made more plays in training camp than Jarrian Jones. Perhaps no defensive back has lined up in more spots, either, with Jones taking snaps outside, in the slot, and at safety. He has hauled in several interceptions over the course of training camp and it feels like he has earned himself a starting gig in Week 1.
“I love Jarrian, man. Love coaching him. He's a really sharp football player. He constantly is working at it away from the field," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said last week.
"And that's helped him kind of branch out and play different spots. You see, like, he's in there as a nickel, in there as a dime, and in there as a corner, and I've said to you before, like, he's even taken reps in here in some settings as a safety. So, he's a really sharp football guy, and he's constantly working at his craft. I think him working with Mat [Defensive Pass Game Coordinator Mathieu Araujo], just watching that, his process has been a lot of fun to watch.”
Branson Combs was one of the best stories of the offseason, and he has carried it over into training camp. He spent most of last year on the practice squad after signing as an undrafted free agent, but he looks like a lock for the training camp this year. There is a good argument to make that he has been the most impressive coverage linebacker on the practice field this season.
Jabbar Muhammad is another former undrafted free agent who went from being a stellar offseason story to a likely contributor. He is one of the five best cornerbacks on the roster and will likely be needed to be leaned on by the defense sooner rather than later, which is quite the rise for a player who spent his entire first year on the practice squad.
"I think he's got a good chip on his shoulder too. He's really taken in all the teaching that Mat is bringing to him. There are some things that, fundamentally, I think he's really gotten better at," Campanile said about Muhammad.
"And that doesn't happen unless you're totally bought in and you're doing it every day. It's a muscle memory game. And Jabbar, probably as much as anybody on our defense has developed, from where he was at this time last year in camp to where he is now. He's just done a lot of really good things. He's been a good football player for us, so to your point, another guy who's in UDFA, who's shown up for us."
With all of the injuries on the offensive line, Chuma Edoga could go from odd man out to a spot on the 53-man roster. It looked shaky for his chances to make the roster after the Jaguars added a top-100 guard in Emmanuel Pregnon in April, but recent injuries along the offensive line could force the Jaguars' hand when it comes to keeping Edoga, who has managed to stay mostly healthy over the course of the summer.
After starting training camp in limited fashion, Chris Rodriguez Jr. has seen his reps increase with seemingly each practice over the last few weeks. His physical nature and ability to get consistent yards after contact have shown up time and time again, with Coen even noting it had done so in joint practices against the Saints.
"I think he had a couple nice downhill runs today that you like to see. I thought he had a nice pickup and blitz protection as well today. It's day by day. He's getting better and better. I've been pleased with his progress," Coen said on Thursday from New Orleans.
Wyatt Milum has been able to stay healthy, which is more than most Jaguars offensive linemen have been able to say. But it sure feels like the second-year offensive lineman has had some rough moments at both right guard and right tackle, and it is easy to say that he has so far failed to run away with a starting job despite having plenty of chances.
Whether Milum starts in Week 1 likely depends on who the Jaguars have available to them health-wise, which is likely not what anyone wanted to hear about Milum entering the former third-round pick's second season.
If I did this article a week ago, Jalen McLeod would probably be in the winner's column. But the past week has since seen McLeod miss practice time due to an unspecified injury, and McLeod is one of the last players who can miss any time with injury. He missed basically his entire rookie season due to injuries, and he needs to get healthy to prove to the Jaguars that he is here to remain on the 53-man roster.

title: 1 Thing We Have Learned From Each Jaguars Position Group at Training Camp
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There are only a few weeks left in the Jacksonville Jaguars' 2026 training camp, and things are starting to come together.
We have talked about what we've learned from camp so far in terms of lessons and surprises, but what is one thing we can truly take away from every position group in camp so far? We break it down below.
Trevor Lawrence has not been on fire every single day of Jaguars training camp, but has taken a few leaps in some key areas. One such area is his general down-to-down accuracy and consistency, which has at times in his career been up-and-down and one of the bigger inconsistencies in his overall game. In this year's camp so far, though, Hunter has shown improved accuracy downfield and in the red-zone, missing fewer passes high or overthrown than he has in past training camps.
The Jaguars spent plenty of chances this offseason talking about a potentially expanded role for second-year running back LeQuint Allen, who was stellar as a pass-blocker last season. Allen was one of college football's most productive pass-catching running backs while at Syracuse, and he has gotten more looks in the passing game in training camp this year than he did at this time a year ago. Just how much more of a passing game load he gets remains to be seen, but it does seem like the uptick is about to be very real.
Brian Thomas Jr. was the MVP of the Jaguars' offseason program after stellar showings in OTAs and minicamp, and he has carried it over to what has so far amounted to the best training camp of his career. Thomas struggled at this same time last year, and all he has done so far is prove that his improvement is as real as every one could have hoped it would be.
The fact that the depth will be tested is another clear lesson from the offensive line, but the last two weeks have also made it clear who the Jaguars envision taking over the most important position on the line with Anton Harrison at left tackle. Harrison taking over the left tackle role was more of an idea than anything else before this summer, but it has felt very real in camp.
If there is one thing rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher has shown so far, it is that he is the real deal as a run-blocker. The Texas A&M product has had several standout days in camp as a blocker, with members of the roster and staff remarking at different times this summer how impressed they have been by the No. 56 pick when it comes to blocking defensive ends in the running game.
One of the best defensive line combinations the Jaguars put on the field last year had Josh Hines-Allen and Dennis Gardeck on the outside, while Arik Armstead and Travon Walker rushed from the inside. This allowed Walker and Hines-Allen to line up on the same side of the field, which proved to be a tough test for every unit the two faced with that package. Everything thus far has indicated that Walker will once again get a chance to win inside on third-downs this year, perhaps more than he ever has before.
The Jaguars made two notable additions to the defensive tackle room this offseason with veteran defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro and third-round defensive tackle Albert Regis, but patience might be needed for both when it comes to making a true impact on the Jaguars' defense moving forward. Orhorhoro was placed behind veteran defensive tackle Matt Dickerson on the Jaguars' first unofficial depth chart, while Jaguars head coach Liam Coen made it clear this week that Regis still has a ways to go in his early development.
The battle to replace Devin Lloyd at linebacker is hot-and-heavy between Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs, and it has not let up at really any point in the process. It feels like Miller is the favorite since he has gotten more reps with the startiing defense in recent practices, but overall the Jaguars have seen both linebackers make their fair share of plays. It feels far too early to proclaim a winner one way or another at this spot, and this battle could even rage into Week 1.
The Jaguars have not been afraid to let Travis Hunter take over a top spot at cornerback since training camp begun, with Hunter frequently taking reps on the outside with the No. 1 defense. There has been a mix of Jarrian Jones, Montaric Brown, and Jourdan Lewis sharing the field with him at different times, but it has felt like the one constant has been Hunter commanding a big role and making plays. When he is on offense, it is noticed.
Caleb Ransaw was truly a wait-and-see player entering training camp. The Jaguars clearly had hopes that he would develop into a contributor when they took him in the third round a year ago, but he missed his entire rookie year and entered training camp as a question mark. Through the first few weeks of camp, however, it is clear that Ransaw is going to play a role considering how often the Jaguars have toyed with multiple safeties. He might be the No. 3 safety like Antonio Johnson was last year, but that is still a significant role.
All signs point to another good year from Cam Little, who said earlier this week that he wants to focus on his consistency from 50+ this season. He got red hit over the second-half of the 2025 season and he has had an even better training camp this year than he had in his first two years. He boomed a massive kick last preseason, and he looks like he could easily do it again.

title: Travis Hunter Is Quickly Emerging as the Jaguars’ Answer to Their Biggest Need
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Ever since the Jacksonville Jaguars traded Jalen Ramsey in 2019, the team has been searcing for the long-coveted shutdown cornerback. Now, it is looking like Travis Hunter is ready to finally fill a need that the Jaguars have been desperate to fill.
The Jaguars have spent high draft picks on other cornerbacks (CJ Henderson in 2020, Tyson Campbell in 2021) and spent money on the position (Shaquill Griffin in 2021). They have also had players develop into strong starters like Montaric Brown and Jarrian Jones. But no matter the path, they have not had a true No. 1 corner who could put his name up there with the best in the league.
Hunter, though, has always been thought of as a potential answer to that prayer. Through the first few weeks of training camp, all signs have so far pointed to Hunter fulfilling that role entering his second season.
Hunter impressed at cornerback as a rookie, but due to the construction of last year's roster his role was more focused on receiver than cornerback. He spent twice as many snaps on offense as he did on defense, and it was clear the Jaguars' early plan was for Hunter to play both ways but do a lot of his damage at receiver.
Things have of course changed since then. After Hunter's injury before Week 9 last year, the Jaguars traded for and gave a contract extension to Jakobi Meyers. They also saw Parker Washington break out over the second-half of the year, with Washington finishing the season as one of the hottest receivers in football. At the same time, the Jaguars saw Campbell get traded to Cleveland, and his replacement Greg Newsome left in free agency in March.
That means Hunter is now seemingly destined to step into a top cornerback role for a Jaguars' defense that arguably lost last year's Wild Card matchup with the Buffalo Bills due to miscues in a secondary that did not have Hunter.
Hunter has played on both sides of the ball in every practice for the Jaguars this training camp, but he has ultimately spent more snaps in team drills on defense. He will play both ways once Week 1 comes along, but the construction of the roster has always hinted to a larger role at cornerback this year, and the Jaguars' actions have said the same thing.
Hunter has impressed, too. The second-year Hunter has recorded two interceptions so far in training camp, showing off the play-making ability at cornerback that could help shift games if it carries over into the regular season.
“He has elite ball skills. The thing about Travis, obviously, you can see even in some of these practices, he can go up and tear the ball out of the air," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Wednesday.
"So that's advantageous for us, obviously defensively, and he's aggressive. He goes after the ball like a receiver, so that's what's exciting about him. And you saw a little bit of that in practice the other day. I thought he made a heck of a play, honestly, coming out of nowhere and tearing the ball out of this guy.”
YOINK ‼️ @TravisHunterJr | @Dream_Finders pic.twitter.com/Bg5NkCzIGe
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has liked what he has seen from Hunter on the defensive side as well. Coen knows he will have Hunter at his disposal on offense, but that vantage point has also given him a chance to see just how valuable Hunter can be for the Jaguars' defense.
“The play they made the other day and Trevor [QB Trevor Lawrence] scrambled and threw it in the middle. The play was dead. He was sacked, but Travis just came out of nowhere and makes the play, like I can't coach it," Coen said earlier this week.
"And so, I think the length, the anticipation on defense, we got him today on the one, but when you have length and anticipation and have a good feel for routes, I think that the play making, getting your hands on balls or just denying the ball with good coverage. That's a win in itself that I think goes a little bit unnoticed from corners. It's like, yeah, when they don't get a lot of work, it's probably because they're doing their job and doing it at a high level, so I've been pleased with him.”
The NFL made it clear coming into camp that the league at large sees Hunter as a player with elite potential at cornerback. The more he plays there, the more it looks like he is a safe bet to meet that potential.

title: The 5 Biggest Surprises From Jaguars' Training Camp So Far: Anton Harrison's Role
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Training camp is always a time for surprises. We all spend so many offseason months trying to picture what a team will look like come Week 1, and then training camp manages to throw a wrench in many plans.
This year's camp has been no different for the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are set to hold a joint practice with the New Orleans Saints on Thursday for their 11th official practice of training camp. A number of situations have played out much differently than we anticipated over the first few weeks of camp, and here are the five biggest.
Anton Harrison came into camp as the Jaguars' most important offensive lineman (alongside Cole Van Lanen), so it is hardly a surprise that he has been one of the standout performers of the summer so far. But what has been a surprise is to see Harrison take the vast majority of his camp reps at left tackle instead of right tackle, with the last two weeks serving as the longest amount of time Harrison has spent on the left side since getting drafted in the first-round of the 2023 NFL Draft.
Harrison spent the first couple of days of camp at right tackle but has spent most of camp switched to the blindside as the Jaguars wait-and-see with Van Lanen's recovery. It wouldn't make much sense for the Jaguars to devote this much time to Harrison on the left side if he wasn't going to take some serious snaps there this season, a shift from pre-camp expectations that had Walker Little penciled in at left tackle until Van Lanen returned.
Considering Harrison is one of the Jaguars who is next up for a contract extension, he could see his price skyrocket as a result of a potential switch to left tackle. It would be a good thing for Harrison, a college left tackle, to prove in his fourth season, even if we didn't expect it a month ago.
We always expected Travis Hunter to play on both sides of the ball for the Jaguars this season, though I was caught by surprise by two things when it came to Hunter and the first few weeks of camp: how quickly they let it rip with his return, and exactly how he has managed to play both sides. I thought there was a chance the Jaguars would take it slow with Hunter in advance of Week 1, but Hunter has done everything at 100 mph since the first day of camp.
Then there is how he has managed to play on both sides. In last year's camp there would be some days where he played both receiver and cornerback on the same day, but more often than not he spent practices devoted to one side. We have now seen Hunter play both sides of the ball in every practice of camp so far, making it clear where he fits into the Jaguars plans. He is going to make an impact at both wide receiver and cornerback this year, one way or another.
I came into the summer thinking that the Jaguars' No. 3 defensive tackle would be Ruke Orhorhoro and their No. 3 defensive end would be Danny Striggow. While I believe both players still have a chance to win those roles, it does seem like the pecking order has been a bit different through the first several weeks of camp, with two other players seemingly grabbing the top backup spots in Matt Dickerson and B.J. Green.
Dickerson and Green are returning players who made impacts a year ago, and it seems like both have improved since then. Dickerson is getting legit snaps with the top defense in team drills, while Green was the replacement for Josh Hines-Allen in the mock game a week ago. Green then proceeded to completely wreck the practice for the second-team offense, collecting multiple would-be sacks over the course of the practice.
My expectation entering training camp was that the Jaguars would look for different options at both kick and punt returner, since both Bhayshul Tuten and Parker Washington are set to play bigger roles on the offense this year. There is still a chance the Jaguars look to other options like Josh Cameron for either role, but as of right now it sure looks like each player will repeat the duty in 2026, especially Washington.
“I talked to Heath [Associate Head Coach/Special Teams Coordinator Heath Farwell], and he said, ‘shoot, let's go.’ Yeah so, I'm just open to the opportunity, whatever it is," Washington said last week. "Obviously, we'll get some more receiver play, but as I said, I want to come out here and be my best self. If that happens to be on return, shoot. I feel like I've been studying that for a while now. Let's see if we can make some more plays.”
The Jaguars could always change plans depending on the game or the health and state of the roster, but right now I would be surprised if Washington and Tuten are not returners in Week 1. I do not think I would have said that a month ago, but it looks like it is how things are playing out. Perhaps Cameron can make things interesting with live reps in the preseason, however.
No, I do not expect the Jaguars to carry four running backs on the 53-man roster by the end of training camp. But that does not take away from the fact that Ameer Abdullah has provided several explosive plays for the Jaguars' running back room despite entering the summer as mostly an afterthought.
We expected Jaguars undrafted rookie running back J'Mari Taylor to push for the RB4 role behind Tuten, Chris Rodriguez Jr., and LeQuint Allen, but it has instead been Abdullah who has stepped up to the plate as the top backup behind the Jaguars' leading trio. He has geniunely impressed, and it may earn him a spot on the Jaguars' practice squad as a result.

title: 4 Jaguars Who Need to Fare Well in Joint Practices vs. the Saints
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will kick off their first of three joint practices this summer on Thursday against the New Orleans Saints, creating an interesting few days ahead.
With the Jaguars' starters not expected to play in the preseason opener vs. the Saints on Saturday, Thursday's practice is now all the more important. So, which Jaguars need to stand out on Thursday for one reason or another? We break down a few names below.
New Jaguars defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro has certainly flashed at times in training camp, both as a pass-rusher and against the run. With that said, the Jaguars have made it perfectly clear with their actions (practice reps, depth chart) that veteran defensive tackle Matt Dickerson should not be simply assumed to be behind Orhorhoro.
A solid day against an opposing offensive line would certainly help Orhorhoro's stock, especially since the Jaguars have a defensive line that will already have plenty of run and passing down snaps already accounted for with their top-level starters. Orhorhoro has talent to make an impact on the line, and he will need to show this is the case against the Saints.
Jaguars offensive lineman Wyatt Milum has stepped up at a few different spots in camp due to injuries, taking snaps with the first-team offense at both right guard and right tackle. If the Jaguars had a Week 1 kickoff on Sunday, he would be starting somewhere along the offensive line. With that said, simply being present and healthy is one thing, but it is time for Milum to start to stand out.
It remains to be seen whether his best fit is at tackle or guard, so it would make sense for the Jaguars to get a look at him at both spots. The Jaguars are too banged-up to risk getting Milum hurt in the preseason, so this is the time for them to really evaluate how far he has come along, and if he is ready for an elevated role.
B.J. Green has done every single thing the Jaguars have asked out of him since he was drafted, and he has risen up the depth chart in a big way as a result. If the Jaguars had to take the field today, Green would likely be the No. 3 edge defender behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker, an important role that he will have to be ready for. He can help prove that readiness with a good day against the Saints.
Green has stood out this summer due to his motor and explosiveness off the ball, and he has been able to give the Jaguars' offensive line fits as a result. If he can take over a joint practice like he has taken over practices at the Miller Electric Center, then the arrow on his trajectory will be pointing up in a big way.
Another player who has risen up the depth chart as the result of top-notch practice performances is cornerback Jabbar Muhammad. He has stood out in more or less every practice ever since the offseason program in the spring, and he will have another big chance to do so on Thursday since he likely will get at least some run. A lot of snaps will belong to the top cornerbacks, but Jourdan Lewis has been out for the last few days and this would make Muhammad the CB4.
Muhammad has been so impressive against the Jaguars' receivers so far that the last thing he really needs to do is show it against a live opponent. The Saints have a talented receiver room and should offer a solid test for the ascending young cornerback as he continues to make a push for the 53-man roster.

title: It Might Be Time to Temper Expectations for One Top Jaguars Draft Pick
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Top draft picks have always held a special place in Jacksonville. For years the Jaguars and their base would put their hopes in rookies to not just improve the team, but even to carry it.
Times have changed since then, with only one such Jaguars draft pick (Travis Hunter) under the new regime having those kind of early expectations. And even Hunter's expectations have now shifted after the Jaguars finished 13-4 with Hunter missing 10 games as a result of a knee-ending injury.
The Jaguars' roster has grown and matured, and the days of rookie draft picks needing to play superheroes are gone. As a result, there are some Jaguars draft picks who deserve tempered expectations: including third-round defensive tackle Albert Regis.
Selected at No. 81 overall in April's draft, Regis was the second-highest draft pick the Jaguars made this year, behind only rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher. Any top-100 pick is going to be expected to play early as long as they are available, and Regis has had some good days in camp such as on Tuesday when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he showed improvement.
But it is where Regis had to improve from that makes it clear Regis is still very early in his career, and he should not be expected to shoulder the weight of the run defense right off the bat as a rookie. First, he needs reps and consistency, just like any other young defensive lineman.
“I thought today was a better outing. I think maybe the previous few weren't up to his or our standard. Look, it's a work in progress for any of these young guys," Coen said about Regis' performance on Tuesday.
"I think DL, especially IDL, is one of the most difficult positions in the NFL to play young. To play early. I think it's extremely difficult. You're 23 years old playing against a lot of grown men and savvy. O-linemen are typically smart, savvy, tough, strong, those things. And so, you can get exposed a little bit in there, not just because of getting moved, but little details of technique and fundamentals that I think takes time."
In short ... the Jaguars really like Regis, but he still has a ways to go. He will still play as a rookie of course, but it would be fair to say out of the five interior defensive linemen on our latest projected 53-man roster, Regis would be No. 5 in the pecking order and behind Matt Dickerson and Ruke Orhorhoro for total snaps.
But that isn't something that would concern the Jaguars, nor should it concern anyone else. That is the standard developmental track for a Day 2 rookie on a playoff team without many holes. The Jaguars will develop him because they will need him eventually, but they will not need him to be DaVon Hamilton in Week 1, and nobody else should expect it either.
"You look at D-Ham [DT DaVon Hamilton]. How old's D-Ham? 28? 29? Right? And he's what? At this point in his career, he's probably at one of the peaks in terms of the way he played. And so, that does take time, D-Linemen in general, but especially IDL," Coen said.

title: 6 Jaguars With Soaring Stock Who Have Leaped Depth Charts at Training Camp
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have plenty of moving pieces a few weeks into training camp, but things are starting to fall into place.
The Jaguars released their first unofficial depth chart on Tuesday ahead of joint practices and their preseason opener with the New Orleans Saints, and several Jaguars saw their names elevated from where they started in training camp.
So, whose stock is soaring the most ahead of Saints week? We break it down below.
The Jaguars' veteran defensive tackle was a surprise contributor a year ago, going from a spot on the practice squad to eventually becoming a key part of the Jaguars' defensive tackle rotation. Dickerson has been frequently used as an example by the coaching staff of how hard work and effort in practice can lead to a spot on game day, and he made the second-team defensive line on the depth chart ahead of new defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. It is hard to imagine a 53-man roster right now without him on it.
"Matt has done a really good job. I think even in the offseason, in his downtime, he was out working with some guys, getting better," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Wednesday. "He's come in really just physically strong at the point of attack so that shown up, and he's a tough guy. He's really, what you love about our defense in terms of he's always doing his job. It's important to him. He's a great teammate, so I love coaching the guy.”
No player has done more for their overall stock in 2026 so far than Jabbar Muhammad. He flashed as an undrafted rookie a year ago but had to cut his teeth on the practice squad for the season. He then arrived in the spring and seemingly made a big play in every single practice, whether with an interception or a timely pass breakup. This has carried over to training camp, and he was now officially listed as a second-team cornerback. He looks like he will make the roster and even contribute.
“I’d say Jabbar, you go back to the spring, he's probably one of the most improved players on the team. He's doing a heck of a job playing obviously corner and nickel. I’m excited," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Tuesday.
"I want to see him get in the game mix. I remember last year in the first preseason game, he showed up on a play just like running it down from the other side of the field and you're just excited to go see what that could look like. And if he's truly taken that next step that we've seen, ultimately, we do need to see it in a game-like scenario.”
This time last year, Travis Hunter was listed as one of the Jaguars' starting receivers alongside Brian Thomas Jr. and Dyami Brown, but he was also listed as a backup cornerback. His snaps in the season then reflected that, with Hunter playing twice as many snaps on offense as he did on defense during his seven-game rookie season. This time around, though, it has been made even more clear than before just how big of a role Hunter is set to play on defense.
Hunter is now listed as a starting cornerback, yet another signal that he is about to see a significantly larger role at cornerback than he did a year ago. While his offensive snaps will be impacted to some degree as a part of that equation, he has still spent every single day of training camp practicing at both positions, unlike last summer.
I would have said Ameer Abdullah was either the No. 5 or No. 6 running back coming into training camp, and I would not have given much thought about it. But all he has done since camp has begun is make plays with the second-team offense, and as a result he was listed as the Jaguars' No. 4 running back and ahead of DeeJay Dallas and undrafted rookie J'Mari Taylor.
This is more or less how things have played out with the backfield in camp, with Abdullah taking the most second-team reps alongside Nick Mullens in training camp as opposed to Dallas or Taylor. It will still be tough for him to make the roster, but he has made a big jump since he signed with the Jaguars in the offseason.
Both sixth-round rookie wide receivers Josh Cameron and CJ Williams are listed as backup receivers and ahead of a group of veteran wideouts in Austin Trammell and Tim Jones, which paints an acurate picture of what the pecking order has been at training camp thus far. This is not to say that the duo was not expected to be in such a spot, but it is evident on the Jaguars' depth chart that most rookies are simply behind veterans because they haven't played yet.
This is not the case with either rookie wide receiver, though, which could help the Jaguars' duo continue to seperate themselves and even make themselves a part of the passing game's short-term plans moving forward.

title: Jaguars 53-Man Roster Projections 3.0: Saints Trip Brings These Questions to Focus
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are getting into the dog days of training camp, which means the 53-man roster is starting to come more and more into focus.
Some jobs are closer to being won now than they were a week ago, though this week's practice and preseason game against the New Orleans Saints could also tip the scale for head coach Liam Coen and general manager James Gladstone.
"Honestly, we had a personnel meeting the other day, yesterday, and it’s still so early. I think we'll have a better idea after this joint, after this game. That's usually when you try to have a little bit of that in terms of you guys have all seen maybe some of the younger guys in their own way stand out here," Coen said on Tuesday.
"We all kind of know who those people are, but, when you actually have to go play tackle football and play in a game… When we do one-on-ones and stuff, that's not football to me. It's a part of football. It's an aspect of it, but we're not grading that as much. So, I want to go see these guys play football.”
We delivered a 53-man roster last week following the first week of camp practices, and we now turn to an updated version after the team's scrimmage and some heavy-hitting practices like Day 10 on Tuesday.
So, what do we think a current version of the 53-man roster would look like? We break it down below.
Trevor Lawrence has had a solid camp overall, though the offense has had some down days. But then there were days like Tuesday where the lack of a running game made it look like the offense was playing catch-up all day, but you look down and see Lawrence still completing most of his passes. Behind him, it feels like Carter Bradley has had a few nice flashes over the last week for the QB3/Practice Squad spot.
Chris Rodriguez Jr. looks like he will have no issues when it comes to Week 1, with the veteran running back getting more and more looks in team drills since starting training camp only doing positional drill work. He has impressed, too, and he has made a mark since the pads have come on. A split with Bhayshul Tuten, plus third-down work from LeQuint Allen, seems like the most likely outcome here.
“I love C-Rod. He’s going to get downhill and he’s going to run somebody over. In those short yardage situations sometimes last year, not saying anything about anybody, but that's just the type of back we need," Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange said on Wednesday. "You need a back like that and you need somebody that's going to get downhill and get those dirty yards. It's all about the hidden yards. Can you get plus-two on contact? And C-Rod does that. So, he's a special guy and I can't wait to see what he does this year for us.”
My guess is that you see a lot of work this Saturday from Josh Cameron and C.J. Williams. The duo has impressed throughout training camp, and they should be able to get plenty of game reps with the starters set to sit vs. the Saints. If the Jaguars did carry six receivers, Austin Trammell and Tim Jones have both had good camps. But with Travis Hunter getting receiver snaps all camp , this feels unlikely.
The tight end room is absolutely going to feature both rookie tight ends by the time the official 53-man roster comes out, which means the only real question is whether Quintin Morris makes the 53. The Jaguars could carry four tight ends because they believe they will need more bodies due to the increase of multiple-tight end sets, or they could attempt to stash him on the practice squad after a quiet start to camp.
How this actually ends up looking come Week 1 depends entirely on Cole Van Lanen and whether he is on the PUP list. But until that actually happens in terms of the Reserve/PUP list, I am factoring him in. The injuries that have ravaged the Jaguars' offensive line could mean Chuma Edoga earns a spot regardless of what Van lanen's status is, too. The Jaguars need several players in this group to get healthy soon.
The Jaguars have had a number of backup pass-rushers stand out during training camp, but these are the top-four. I hada lot of questions about the Jaguars' pass-rush depth entering camp, but so far this unit has done nothing for the Jaguars but produce. We will need to see if that can carry over to Saints week.
Matt Dickerson was ahead of Ruke Orhorhoro on the first official depth chart, which can either be read into or ignored. What can't just be glossed over though is the fact that he has clearly earned favor with the Jaguars' coaching staff and looks like a secure candidate to make the 53-man roster coming out of camp.
Parker Hughes is clearly going to have to fight for his spot in the preseason, but we are going to slot him here until any games may tell us differently. Jalen McLeod is an interesting player to note because he had a strong start to camp and performance in the scrimmage, but he did not practice on Tuesday. He needs to stay healthy to make the team, and this weekend is a big chance for that to happen.
Perhaps the Jaguars carry six cornerbacks and keep veteran cornerback Christian Braswell, but right now it feels like this is their top-five. The fact that they have a number of safeties who can play in the slot might impact how they build out the cornerback group as well, but it feels like Jabbar Muhammad has earned a spot no matter what.
The Jaguars' safety room looks like it has taken shape, with the top three safeties all due to get plenty of playing time. Rayuan Lane will have a spot on the roster due to his special teams ability, while rookie Jalen Huskey has been impressive over the last week or so of practices. He has clear special teams value, but he has stood out when given a chance on defense as well.
“J-Huskey, he's a dog. He's rangy. He's going to come up, he’s going to hit. I see a lot of myself in him. He is going to be a good player. Yeah, he is going to be a good player," Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson said about Huskey this week.
This one isn't going to change for a long time. The Jaguars have one of the NFL's best special teams groups and it is headlined by this top-tier trio of specialists. Outside of a missed PAT in the mock game last week, the special teams unit has made virtually every other kick in team settings this summer. Cam Little says he thinks he wants to try from 70, and I think he will.

title: Everything We've Learned About the Jaguars' Backup QB Battle So Far
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are hitting the midpoint of training camp, and the preseason opener against the New Orleans Saints is right around the corner.
With the Jaguars set to sit starting quarterback Trevor Lawrence in Saturday's preseason opener due to Thursday's joint practice, it is a good time to take a look at the quarterback room behind him. The Jaguars' backup quarterbacks will be running the show on Saturday against the Saints, and it is worth remembering that there is still a battle for the QB3/practice squad spot between two young passers.
So, what is the state of the backup quarterback situation behind Lawrence? We break it down below.
One thing that has been very clear from the jump is that Nick Mullens is, expectedly, unchallenged as QB2. The Jaguars have never seemed interested in finding another option via a trade or free agency, and it is easy to see why. They have a contract committed to Mullens, a veteran passer who has experience in the system and who successful served as a sounding board last year for Lawrence in his first year in the McVay-family style of offense.
Mullens has taken the vast majority of second-team reps in camp, just like he was always set to as QB2. He has had some solid days, including on Sunday when he was able to find Austin Trammell deep for two different touchdowns against what has been an impressive Jaguars secondary. Mullens is the QB2, and that will remain unchanged moving forward.
Perhaps the more interesting question about the No. 2 spot has to do with 2027 since Mullens is set to be a free agent in March. With that said, it feels like a realistic scenario that the Jaguars would sign Mullens to another similar two-year, $4.5 million deal like he signed with them last March.
When it comes to the QB3 battle between Carter Bradley and undrafted rookie quarterback Joey Aguilar, I think Bradley has the edge right now. Nothing is stopping the Jaguars from keeping two quarterbacks on the practice squad, but there are so few reps to go around in practice after training camp that it is unlikely the Jaguars would make such a move. This means that we will get three preseason games of Bradley and Aguilar dueling, and then we get a decision.
Bradley has made plays during training camp and has even impressed in his few reps with the No. 2 offense at times. Aguilar is a bigger passer with a powerful arm, but Bradley has done a good job of making plays with his feet. Both will likely get reps against the Saints on Sunday, and head coach Liam Coen detailed on Tuesday what he expects from Bradley.
"He's going to get a good amount of play, good amount of burn. I really want to see Carter just go execute the offense at a high level. Eliminate any pre-snaps, the delays or pre-snap motion issues. Like, don't overthink it," Coen said.
"Don't overanalyze it, man. Just go play one play at a time, execute the offense, and then let your playmaking skills take over. You guys saw it all season where, on our scout team, he's out there running around, making plays, making throws, running around, doing some good things. And so, you ultimately want to just see him operate, but also, man, do what also makes you good and how you like to play. I don't want to take that away, but we can't have some of the pre-snaps and things. Want it to be clean.”

title: Chiefs Star Chris Jones on Rookie DT Peter Woods: ‘He’s Strong as an Ox‘
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs wanted to prioritize strengthening their defense in the NFL Draft, and the second defensive player they selected was defensive tackle Peter Woods. The former Clemson standout was taken No. 29 overall in the first round to provide support for Chris Jones on the interior for years to come.
While Woods has been labeled as having "a ways to go" by DC Steve Spagnuolo and HC Andy Reid, his raw talent has stood out during training camp . He has done a solid job of inserting himself into the defensive tackle rotation alongside Jones and Khyiris Tonga. On Thursday, Jones was one of the Kansas City players who spoke to the media after padded practice. The future Hall of Famer sang Woods' praises, particularly when discussing his freakish strength.
"Strong. A young bull," Jones said to describe Woods. "I think for him, just pulling it all together. He has the skill set. He has the power for it, also. He's strong as an ox, and he's willing to learn."
In past years, Jones has dealt with constant double teams and being the center of attention for opposing offensive lines. The hope is that Woods can develop into someone who eases the load off the veteran tackle and eventually becomes a star himself.
Something Jones likes about Woods is his willingness to adapt and learn. He believes the 21-year-old will make a significant impact even as a rookie. "I think a lot of these guys, they're coming from college, and they were one of the top guys in college," Jones continued. "Just being humble in yourself, and being willing to learn and being a sponge. Most importantly, that's what he is, and I think he's going to contribute to this defense a lot this year."
As he continues to improve his technique, Woods will continue to make strides on the defensive line. Even if there are some growing pains during his first year, the future looks bright for Woods.

title: Andy Reid Confirms Status of Patrick Mahomes for Chiefs' Preseason Game vs. Rams
full_text:
As the Kansas City Chiefs gear up for their preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams, many are wondering whether Andy Reid will play his starters. The veteran head coach has lightened up on that workload in years past, but the health of quarterback Patrick Mahomes brings that storyline right back to the forefront in 2026.
By the time Saturday's contest in Kansas City rolls around, Mahomes will be a full eight months removed from suffering a torn ACL and LCL. The superstar signal-caller has participated in everything at training camp , yet that's a far cry from being ready for a game.
With Week 1 of the regular season in mind, Reid is exercising some caution. He says Mahomes won't play this weekend, which was widely expected based on his previous comments.
"The way the rotation will go is Pat won't start or play," Reid said. "So it'll be Justin (Fields) and then (Garrett) Nussmeier, and then Chris (Oladokun) will take it from there. We'll just see how the reps go as we work through that."
This signals a change for Mahomes, who has typically played multiple series each preseason. It remains to be seen whether he'll take the field next weekend in Tampa Bay versus the Buccaneers, although Reid hasn't been too optimistic on that front.
Speaking to the media following a recent practice, Mahomes said that although he's eager to compete , he'd ultimately be game for whatever Reid feels is optimal.
"I'm for whatever coach says," Mahomes said. "Like I said, I'm going to prepare to play. He hasn't told me anything, so I'll prepare to play and prepare to get myself ready. We'll see where we go from there and if not, I'll be as locked in as I am during the game and try to get myself as ready to go [as possible] for the game. It's just a process of trying to make sure you're ready for the season and whatever coach thinks is best, I'll do it."
In relief of No. 15, it'll be Fields getting the nod under center. The newcomer was acquired via trade earlier this year from the New York Jets and went 4-for-9 with 46 passing yards and another 19 yards on the ground last preseason. Oladokun played in all three of the Chiefs' 2025 preseason contests, completing 11 of 23 passes for 120 yards and toting the ball twice for 36 rushing yards.
Fields is the primary backup during the regular season, but there may be some roster math left to do behind him. Despite Oladokun having more experience in the offense and also getting reps in real NFL games, Nussmeier is an intriguing rookie prospect who could force Reid and general manager Brett Veach's hands with a strong preseason. Add in Mahomes' recovery, and there's a world where three quarterbacks are rostered after cutdowns.
Not having Mahomes take away any snaps, at least for the first preseason outing, could help provide some much-needed clarity.

title: How Chiefs’ Preseason Slate Will Determine Kansas City’s QB Depth Chart
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are set to kick off their first preseason game of the year this weekend, giving fans their first chance to see the team in live action since last December. While the result ultimately means nothing, the matchup will finally put all the training camp hype to the test and give Chiefs fans their first real look at this year's squad. Unfortunately, we likely won't see superstar signal-caller Patrick Mahomes until Week 1 against the Broncos. That opens the door for Justin Fields to take reps with the first team while seventh-round pick and former LSU standout Garrett Nussmeier moves into the second-string role.
It also gives Nussmeier a chance to support his case for a spot on the 53-man roster . K.C.'s three preseason games will have major implications on how general manager Brett Veach constructs the quarterback depth chart this season.
Many outlets expect the Chiefs to carry a traditional three-quarterback setup, with Mahomes leading the way, followed by Fields and Nussmeier. However, the preseason could determine whether that ends up being the case.
The fact that Nussmeier will get extended playing time could either boost or hurt his chances of making the 53-man roster. Rookie quarterbacks can struggle when the pressure is on, and one rough preseason showing could quickly change how the Chiefs view his roster prospects.
With so many roster-bubble candidates competing for spots at other positions, the 24-year-old is far from a lock to make the team in September.
Nussmeier also cannot simply be placed on the practice squad. Because he was drafted, he would first have to clear the NFL waiver wire, where another team could potentially claim him — and that's where Chris Oladokun comes into play. Oladokun could serve as the third-string quarterback on the practice squad and be elevated whenever Mahomes or Fields is unavailable for a game. Unlike Nussmeier, there's not much of a risk to let Oladokun pass through waivers knowing that he'll probably end up back with the Chiefs.
The Chiefs showed some confidence in Oladokun by starting him in the final two games of last season, albeit after they had already been eliminated from playoff contention. He finished the campaign with 235 passing yards, one touchdown, no interceptions and 18 rushing yards.
Relying on Mahomes' health after his recent knee surgery could be a risk, and we'd lean heavily toward keeping Nussmeier around to develop as a long-term backup. Regardless, the final decision will come down to how many roster spots the Chiefs have available and whether they believe carrying three quarterbacks is necessary rather than keeping an emergency option on the practice squad. This may seem like a minor decision right now, but it's still worth keeping an eye on during the preseason. The quarterback depth chart could become especially important in the unlikely yet possible event that Mahomes isn't ready to go when the Chiefs open the regular season against Denver.

title: Surprise Camp Standout Andrew Armstrong Excited for First Game With Chiefs
full_text:
Judging by sheer numbers, the Kansas City Chiefs have boatloads of depth in the wide receiver room. The quality of that depth, however, has been questioned at every turn dating back to free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft .
Injuries and a lack of high-end overall contributions from the group have left the door wide open for someone to make a name for themselves at this summer's training camp . Multiple pieces have managed to do so, including second-year man Andrew Armstrong.
With KC's first preseason game of the year on the horizon, the former Arkansas standout believes he's settling into a groove. Speaking to the media on Tuesday, he commented on whether he's built some trust with quarterbacks Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields.
"I mean yeah, I hope so," Armstrong said with a laugh. "I've been out there just doing the best I can be, being the best I can be. Just, like I said, learning. Going into the playbook, and I think that's one of the main goals: being trustworthy for the quarterback. I feel like I'm trying to build that with them."
Head coach Andy Reid echoed that sentiment after a recent camp practice, complimenting the 25-year-old for boasting plus traits in multiple aspects of the receiving game.
“Yeah, I like what Armstrong's doing," Reid said. "Big kid, strong. Looks like the quarterback trusts him, both of them. Top two guys, they trust him on his route running. He's got good speed for a big kid, and good transition. He's not stiff coming out of breaks, and that's important."
In two years with the Razorbacks, Armstrong hauled in 134 passes for 1,904 yards and six touchdowns. After not getting picked in last year's NFL Draft, he latched on with the Miami Dolphins and briefly spent some time with the Detroit Lions later on. Kansas City swept him up on a reserve/futures deal in January, paving the way for him to join a franchise he's long respected.
Armstrong has family in Missouri, which makes the current run he's on even sweeter. It was a no-brainer to sign with the Chiefs and have a chance to compete.
"My family's here," Armstrong said. "This has been my favorite team since I was a little kid. I'm not even worried about the city life and things like that. I'm here to play football and be around the team. Just the seriousness of it all, I really want to be around a serious environment, and this is an extremely serious environment. I love that."
Standing just under 6-foot-4 and weighing in at 202 pounds during the pre-draft process, Armstrong posted one of the best Relative Athletic Scores in his class. He's a truly impressive vertical athlete, but as Reid mentioned, there's a bit more to his game than that. He's surprised the team with a nice blend of fluidity, smarts and timing at the Missouri Western State University campus, thus making him a player to watch this weekend and beyond.
There's no denying that Armstrong has his work cut out for him to make the 53-man roster at the end of the month. Still, he feels right at home and could be a prime practice squad candidate at the very least. Now, he's looking to maximize the opportunity to put on a Chiefs uniform and show what he's made of in front of the home crowd on Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams.
"It's going to feel great," Armstrong said. "Just looking and seeing all the red. It's different playing it on a game than being in real life. I know it's going to feel amazing."

title: Chiefs Make Emmanuel Ogbah Signing Official, Part Ways With UDFA CB
full_text:
As the Kansas City Chiefs close in on their first preseason game of 2026, they're doing so with a familiar face rejoining the fold.
Early on Wednesday evening, the club announced that defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah had officially signed. Ogbah now becomes a Chief for the second time in his career, completing a move that was reported on Tuesday morning pending a physical.
The NFL's afternoon transaction wire and personnel notice originally listed Ogbah as a visit, which coincided with him attending training camp but not wearing pads or working on the field. To make room for Ogbah on the 90-man offseason roster, the Chiefs have released cornerback Bryce Phillips .
Bringing back a Super Bowl champ. Let's get to work, @EmanOgbah 🤝 pic.twitter.com/UsFSzPtHB3
Ogbah, now 32 years old, returns to the place he briefly broke out at during the 2019-20 NFL season. The former second-round pick had 5.5 sacks in 10 games with Kansas City before missing the rest of the season with a pectoral injury, but he was still regarded favorably as a member of the Super Bowl LIV-winning group.
When asked about the imminent Ogbah acquisition on Tuesday, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo expressed plenty of optimism and said he'd kept in contact with Ogbah over the years.
“Yeah, I always had an affection for E," Spagnuolo said. "It was disappointing the one year we had him in 2019. I thought he was really coming on and then he got hurt, and then we didn't have him at the end of the year. But I've always periodically been in touch with him. We've got to get through the physical and all those other things but if he's part of our group, I'll be excited about that.”
Phillips, a former Santa Ana College player, spent his final two collegiate seasons with San Diego State. In two years for the Aztecs, he recorded 74 total tackles (five for loss), 10 passes broken up and a pair of interceptions. He joined Kansas City on an undrafted rookie free agent deal after posting an impressive 8.58 Relative Athletic Score during the pre-draft process.
The Chiefs' offseason roster is down a cornerback, but it gains someone with valuable championship-level experience as the preseason arrives.

title: Chiefs Rookie OT Kahlil Benson Embracing Whatever Role Comes His Way
full_text:
One of the best stories of the Kansas City Chiefs training camp has been offensive tackle Kahlil Benson. The undrafted rookie out of Indiana has turned enough heads at K.C.'s facility to go from a long shot for the 53-man roster to a feasible candidate to start at right tackle in Week 1.
Benson's rapid growth couldn't have been predicted by anyone but himself. The 6-foot-6, 319-pound freak still has a ways to go with his technique and footwork, but possesses exceptional raw physical tools. On Wednesday, Benson met with the media for a four-minute press conference to discuss some of the early rumblings at camp. He was asked how a player like him, who just came off an undefeated national championship season at Indiana, could have gone so under the radar among NFL scouts. Benson chalked it up to the reality of life and the challenges football players have to embrace.
"Realistically, whatever position you get put in, you got to take it on the chin," Benson said. "Being a football player, stuff happens, so just being able to move past one thing and put one foot before the other one and keep going and make sure there's nothing else on the table."
While he was primarily a tackle at the collegiate level, the Chiefs have slid him over to right guard with Trey Smith sidelined by a hip injury in camp. Given that he's a rookie whose roster spot is still up in the air, Benson is willing to do whatever he needs to get on the field and secure a long-term future in Kansas City.
He takes pride in his work as an offensive lineman, specifically his ability to be coachable and willing to learn and adapt. "Showing the humbleness, and the confidence, and the coaches being able to trust you," he said about what he values as a lineman. "Being able to move forward, and when there’s time to be corrected, being able to be corrected, and then being able to just go out to the next play and then do what you got to do the next play."
The Memphis native stressed the importance of staying ready every day and taking advice from his coaches to continue improving. His maturity is already shining through early in his NFL career.
"Being able to take those coaching points from them, as well as from your coaches, you have to be ready when your number is called. Our vets and everybody here have been making sure that all us rookies have been on point."

title: Despite Entering Year 14, Travis Kelce Is Still Focused on Improving for Chiefs
full_text:
At a certain point in the career of an eventual Hall of Fame player, they cross over the threshold of having absolutely nothing left to prove to the outside world. For Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, that moment was likely several years ago.
Despite boasting one of the game's top statistical profiles for his position and putting out some of the best tape in tight end history, Kelce opted to return for a 14th season in KC. Even after marrying iconic singer-songwriter Taylor Swift earlier this year, he still feels the drive to continue his football career. Yet another grueling training camp has him motivated for more than just that.
Coming off a 76-catch, 851-yard, five-touchdown effort in 2025, Kelce believes he can be better for the Chiefs in 2026-27.
"I've still got a lot of love for this game," Kelce said on Wednesday. "I still think I can go out and play at a high level. I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year. I think that's probably the biggest thing for me, making sure that I'm accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I'm out there."
Last season was a trying one for Kelce, as he struggled with drops and also watched Kansas City limp to its worst record (6-11) since he entered the league way back in 2013. It put him to the test in a major way, and he figures to remain a critical component of the offense this coming campaign. Knowing that, he's laser-focused on leveling up and fighting off Father Time once again.
"All aspects of football, man," Kelce said of where he wants to improve. "Being more accountable when the ball's in the air. There were a few games last year that I felt like I put on myself. In the blocking world, being able to get my guys so we can spring guys for bigger gains.
"And then on top of that, just being a better leader. When we get stuck with adversity hitting, who's going to want you in that fox hole with you? That's one of those things: I want to be one of those guys that everybody counts on to be there and get us out of that fox hole."
After a down 2024, Kelce responded with a much more efficient performance a year ago. In addition to his Pro Football Focus overall grade ranking 14th out of 37 qualified tight ends, he was third overall in total EPA for tight ends (71.19, via SumerSports ) and saw his yards after catch per reception spike from 3.5 to 5.6. A tad lighter per-game workload and more short-range work did the trick.
Entering what could be the final season of his illustrious professional career, the aging curve certainly isn't working in Kelce's favor. That's been the case for a while now, however, and he's kept chugging along as one of the sport's better tight ends anyway. He takes training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri very seriously, believing it sets the tone for the team's output in the year ahead.
Kelce didn't admit whether this is his last camp at Missouri Western State University, but he did emphasize wanting to maximize the bonding time he has left.
"I mean year one, I was just trying to make the team, I guess," Kelce said. "So I think this year, not only making the team but trying to figure out how I can bring guys along with me and show them how to play championship football, I think that's a big thing. And be able to just enjoy these moments with the guys I've built this culture with — coach (Andy) Reid and guys like Pat (Patrick Mahomes), Chris Jones, George (Karlaftis) and everybody."

title: Nick Bolton and Jared Wiley Leave Chiefs Training Camp Practice Early, Ride Off in Cart
full_text:
Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton left training camp practice in a cart on Wednesday, but the team later confirmed that Bolton didn't suffer an injury.
Alex Gold of 96.5 The Fan shared the initial update from St. Joseph, Missouri .
"Nick Bolton in the front of the cart. Didn’t see what happened. We’ll have to see after practice."
The team later told reporters that Bolton left with an illness. That sounds unpleasant, but it's much less alarming than any kind of direct injury for the Chiefs' defensive signal-caller.
Third-year tight end Jared Wiley also left practice early on Wednesday, riding in the front of the cart, according to Nate Taylor of ESPN . Wiley was a fourth-round pick in 2024 and has been battling for a chance to be KC's No. 3 tight end throughout camp. The Chiefs announced that Wiley departed with a strained hamstring, per Taylor.
One other young Chief suffered an issue during Wednesday's practice: rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has an ankle injury.
Woods was slow to get up after a play , but Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star noted that Woods wouldn't be subbed off the field.
"Marcus Harris attempted to sub in for Peter Woods after this play, but Woods waved him off and insisted on staying in," McDowell shared on Twitter/X.
A great screen pass from Mahomes to Kenneth Walker for a big gain. 🔥💪🏾 Peter Woods goes down briefly at the bottom of your screen, but he worked the next few plays. 🎥 | @Farzin21 pic.twitter.com/EJuwhPVyDa
The story continues below as originally published.
Gold's detail of Bolton's positioning—sitting in the front of the cart—is a positive sign. Typically, a front-of-cart exit implies a less-serious injury (or perhaps even an equipment issue or an otherwise-planned exit).
Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest noted that Bolton played through an injury on Tuesday .
"Bolton banged up his right knee yesterday and appeared in a lot of pain," Derrick wrote. "He did wave off the athletic trainer and stayed in the practice, however."
Bolton plays a vital role in Kansas City's defense , and his $19.25 million cap hit in 2026 is the highest of his career so far. He played 97% of the team's defensive snaps in 2025.
In addition to Wednesday's early exits, the Chiefs were already missing a usual cast of recent absences.
Right guard Trey Smith (hip), linebacker Drue Tranquill (back), cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (PUP, knee) were all sidelined again on Wednesday, according to Derrick .
It's hard to imagine any of those injured players suiting up for the Chiefs' first preseason game on Saturday . With Bolton also taking an early exit, Saturday's game could bring a major opportunity for linebackers Jeffrey Bassa, Cooper McDonald and Jack Cochrane.

title: Three Biggest Questions the Chiefs Still Face at Training Camp
full_text:
Although final roster cuts don't have to be made until the end of the month, Kansas City Chiefs training camp officially ends approximately one week from now on Aug. 20. There are still a number of lingering questions for this squad that have yet to be answered.
We'd all like to think the expected return of a future Hall of Fame quarterback will solve everything, but that's simply not the case. The Chiefs were already headed toward missing the postseason for the first time in Patrick Mahomes' tenure before he tore his ACL/LCL, and they were severely lacking in several areas that they had to address during the offseason. These three questions will heavily impact the Chiefs' early-season performance. Let's look at the first.
Head coach Andy Reid is making the right decision to sit Mahomes in the preseason this year. For the first time in his decade-long NFL career, he won't appear in a preseason game, but is expected to be ready by Week 1.
While fans should have the utmost confidence in Mahomes figuring things out with his receiving corps, it does raise questions about how much chemistry he'll have with his targets when the season gets underway. Granted, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy have worked with him for multiple years, and Travis Kelce is still available as his security blanket, but the options start to become slim after that. Reid has assured that Mahomes is building "trust" with newcomers like Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong, though the reality is that they won't see any game action together for another month.
It's tough to know how much chemistry a quarterback-receiver duo can build when they're only seeing each other in practice against their own defense.
Since the second day of training camp, the right tackle battle has begun as Kahlil Benson began stealing first-team reps from projected starter Jaylon Moore. That has since changed after Trey Smith's hip injury forced Benson to move to guard, but he's very much still in play to win the job on the outside.
The undrafted rookie out of Indiana boasts exceptional physical tools despite lacking the experience and technique of Moore. He'll need to make plenty of progress before he is seriously considered the favorite, but this competition has lasted nearly two weeks now with no clear frontrunner. This is a question that could be answered by tomorrow or persist until the day before Week 1. Either way, both players are embracing the competition and pushing each other to improve every day, which is a fantastic sign.
The offense has its fair share of injuries in the wide receiver room, not to mention making sure Mahomes' knee is steady. However, the defense is dealing with several ailments that have left the Chiefs shorthanded at certain positions.
Most of the concerns stem from the secondary, where first-round draft selection Mansoor Delane is still donning a non-contact jersey , while Kristian Fulton (hip) and L'Jarius Sneed (lower body) remain limited. Another player to pop up on the Chiefs' injury radar is Drue Tranquill, who is dealing with back spasms that have recently sidelined him.
The defensive line is also becoming a concern. Ashton Gillotte is dealing with a lengthy hamstring strain that could keep him out of the entire preseason, putting Felix Anudike-Uzomah in a starting role . Chiefs fans know it is difficult to rely on FAU, who missed the entirety of the 2025 campaign following a hamstring surgery of his own. To make matters worse, Ethan Downs tore his ACL in camp last month, while 2025 second-round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list with a knee injury.
The Chiefs could be dangerously thin on defense entering the preseason. Not all of these injuries will carry over into Week 1 against the Broncos, but with so much uncertainty less than a month until the opener, it's time to sound the alarm over the defense's health.
