title: Steve Spagnuolo Weighs in on Truth of Chiefs' First Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
There are two things about training camp that can be counted on to fuel chaos on social media. One of them is a nicely framed highlight clip, and the other is a depth chart being released. With a new week of practice in full swing, those in Kansas City Chiefs circles have been exposed to both.
The latter was posted on Monday night, ranking the club's 90-man offseason roster ahead of Saturday's 3:00 p.m. CT outing against the Los Angeles Rams. The preseason opener should feature several depth pieces jockeying for spots on the eventual 53-man group, but many fans are placing considerable stock in the depth chart as a hint at who could be held in higher regard.
Chiefs issue their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 season. I beseech you all once again, please no wagering. pic.twitter.com/E9nXKu7MDt
There's a hangup, though. These preseason depth charts are unofficial in nature and should be viewed more as (somewhat) educated guesses by team public relations staff than a true reflection of coaching assessments. Take the cornerback position for example, where first-round pick Mansoor Delane is listed as a second-stringer but veteran L'Jarius Sneed is a starter.
Is there any validity to the rankings? Speaking to the media on Tuesday, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo weighed in with his thoughts on Sneed, Delane and second-year man Nohl Williams.
"It's really hard," Spagnuolo said. "I mean, it's on there [that] LJ's been in the league for a while. Nohl has, too. That's probably why (vice president of football communications) Brad (Gee) did it that way. You know, neither LJ or Delane has really practiced very much, so we're way down the road on all of that. Health will be a big issue, continuity [and] how many reps they've had going in, and we'll see when we get to the first game."
Spagnuolo's comments serve as a critical reminder that some positional hierarchies have yet to be revealed. It's widely expected that Delane, for instance, will assume a starting role on the boundary once he's cleared from a lingering shoulder injury . When Sneed first reunited with the team, most assumed he was a reserve. Williams' inclusion as a starter ahead of Kristian Fulton might be the only listing worth reading into.
Between his two years with the Tennessee Titans, Sneed managed to play in just 12 of 34 possible regular-season games. Although no one has truly separated from the pack at the nickel spot, that same truth applies to him as well. It remains to be seen whether it'll be him, Kader Kohou, Chris Roland-Wallace or rookie Jadon Canady who claims that spot.
Similarly to the pre-game one depth chart, adjustments entering the following contest don't have to spell doom for one player or another. Preliminary sorting is best taken with a grain of salt on both sides of the ball.
With that said, don't confuse this with dozens of jobs being up for grabs. A majority of the Chiefs' roles and roster spots are fairly defined with Week 1 of the regular season roughly a month out. In competition-heavy rooms like cornerback, however, Spagnuolo is making it clear that there's still a long way to go.

title: Chargers vs. Texans Notes: Trey Lance Unexpected QB Battle, Rookies Shine and More
full_text:

There, the Chargers and head coach Jim Harbaugh let starters like Justin Herbert warm up, not actually play in the contest . He’s doing a “ramp up” that will lead to the bulk of the starters playing at a later preseason game.
Not that there wasn’t excitement to be had from the Chargers, so here are notes to know.
No Tyler Biadasz for the Chargers at center, so fans will have to wait and see what the new big-money center can do.
Until then, the starting line looked like this in Houston:
Yes, that's hyped rookie second-round pick Jake Slaughter at center despite the fact he’s supposed to be taking over a starting guard spot. He later got work at guard.
Branson Taylor, though, has been a revelation for the Chargers and is apparently running away with the left guard job. That played out early on Thursday night.
Hard to miss the Chargers rookies making plays. First-rounder Akheem Mesidor looked the part and physical on the edge. Safety Genesis Smith undercut a pass and picked it off in the endzone, but only had one foot in bounds. And Slaughter looked like he held up well.
There had been some whispers in the week before the game that a quarterback competition could be underway behind Herbert. Trey Lance just doesn’t have a hold on the job over DJ Uiagalelei.
Lance…didn’t do himself any favors on Thursday night. He was mostly average and sometimes terrible, like on an interception right before halftime. To say the door is open would be an understatement.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: Kendall Williamson, Can the 2025 Roster Surprise Do it Again?
full_text:
Kendall Williamson, born on August 24, 2000, in Snellville, Georgia, played his high school ball at his local school, Brookwood, where he would end up earning four-star recruiting status, according to 247Sports . With this status, Williamson could have nearly gone to any school he could have wanted, but ended up choosing Stanford.
Once with Stanford, a school known for its rigorous academics, Williamson made an impact on the field, earning 16 tackles as a cornerback in his first ten games at the college level. 2019, saw Williamson start at the corner spot, recording 47 tackles.
2020 was the COVID-19 pandemic year, cutting everyone's season short. This season saw Williamson play safety, where he seemed to instantly excel in the short season. 2021 was his first full season at the spot, and Williamson had 3.5 tackles for loss, one sack and 67 tackles in 12 games, showing himself to be a well-balanced PAC-12 safety.
In Williamson's final year with the program, he recorded 50 tackles, 2.5 of which were for loss. He also got his first career interception. Williamson's long career at Stanford was a successful one, with him finally entering the 2023 NFL Draft.
NFL Scout Lance Zierlein described Williamson as: "[he] offers good measurables and testing numbers, but he’s lacking in production and consistency. He plays with good route recognition when hovering in off-man coverage, but he might not have the range needed to handle expanded areas of responsibility. He’s willing in run support but overestimates his pursuit speed and misses tackles."
The Chicago Bears drafted the Georgia native in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft, signing him to their practice squad for the entire 2023 season. He was eventually let go after the year, going to the Bills on a reserve contract.
After not making the Bills' roster in 2024, he found his way to the Bolts' practice squad, appearing in two regular-season games, finally getting live NFL action. In 2025, Williamson finally made his first initial 53-man roster, surprising many NFL fans with his inclusion over someone like Tony Jefferson.
During the course of the 2025 season, Williamson was a core special teams ace, proving to the coaching staff that he was a good contributor to keep on the roster. He is now returning for the 2026 season in hopes of making the roster once more.

"Kendall Williamson signed a 1 year, $1,075,000 contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, including an average annual salary of $1,075,000. In 2026, Williamson will earn a base salary of $1,075,000, while carrying a cap hit of $1,075,000." - Spotrac
The Bolts have bolstered the Safety group once again by drafting Genesis Smith in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, making it an uphill battle for Williamson to once again make the Bolts' roster. However, he surprised once, so why could he not surprise once more?
Whether he makes the final 53-man roster, expect him to be a part of this team in some capacity. His traits as both a defender and special teams weapon give him a role on this Chargers team.

title: Chargers Injuries, Akheem Mesidor, Quick Notes and Buzz Before Preseason vs. Texans
full_text:
There are an almost overwhelming number of things to track around the Los Angeles Chargers before they start the preseason in Week 1 against the Houston Texans.
A Rashawn Slater injury watch tops the list, no doubt. But other key Chargers storylines , like rookie breakouts, coaching changes and final 53-man roster outlooks demand attention, too.
Maybe it isn’t so shocking. In addition to the normal training camp stuff, Jim Harbaugh has reset the coordinator spots on both sides of the ball with Mike McDaniel and Chris O’Leary on offense and defense, respectively.
Here’s a quick rundown of notes and buzz before kickoff.
Branson Taylor has gone from the practice squad last year to…leading the battle for the starting left guard job? A 2025 sixth-round pick, Taylor is one of the remaining five or six to get in the mix since camp started. He could steal the spot from new arrival Kayode Awoskia and, more notably, second-round pick Jake Slaughter.
David Njoku has been the big-name signing for the Chargers at tight end this offseason. But according to Gregg Rosenthal after a recent practice, Charlie Kolar has seen major usage. No shocker: Kolar was the first signing at tight end this offseason by McDaniel. And he’s a superb blocker with upside as a receiver. Oronde Gadsden could be getting less work than expected during the regular season.
Rookie fourth-rounder Genesis Smith has always looked like a threat to steal snaps at safety next to Elijah Molden. Exiting a recent practice, Rosenthal confirmed that Smith “could play right away." His elite athleticism and game sense could knock someone like Tony Jefferson out of playing time.
Rashawn Slater took the time to have a media press conference amid his injury woes. So, it must not be that bad, right? The question is whether Slater will get back out there between now and the second preseason game as he’s roughly one year removed from a torn patellar tendon.
There’s a fight brewing at wideout. Big investment from last year Tre Harris could push Quentin Johnston for looks. Rookie Brenen Thompson is attempting to make some noise, which would make life tougher on Derius Davis. Former late finds like Luke Grimm could still put others, such as KeAndre Lambert-Smith, in jeopardy.
First-round pick Akheem Mesidor has looked the part in practice, but it will need to translate to live action in preseason work. They’re counting on the older rookie to produce right away to offset the loss of Odafe Oweh in free agency.
Elsewhere at edge rusher, Nadame Tucker feels like a guy who has locked a roster spot already. The college free agent was productive under O’Leary last season in college and it’s putting a ton of final 53 pressure on still-developing Kyle Kennard and aging veteran Bud Dupree.
Better get to know the name. The undrafted free agent has multiple pass breakups in camp already and is getting shout-outs from coaches. He feels like another breakout cornerback for a franchise that just keeps finding them. His rise puts others like Deane Leonard, Isas Waxter, and Eric Rogers in some danger.
Don’t look now, but DJ Uiagalelei might actually be pushing Trey Lance behind Justin Herbert. Practice reps have shown as much, putting added pressure on deep preseason action. Jim Harbaugh emphasized this point before kickoff this week.
“Both have really acquitted themselves well, and the next piece is in the games and how they play,” Harbaugh said, according to Daniel Popper of The Athletic. “That’s something we’ll all see. I imagine, from what I’ve seen in practice, it’s going to be pretty close. They’re both good.”

title: 2 Chargers Rookie Edge Rushers Making Their Case During Training Camp
full_text:
Training camp is where young players turn potential into opportunity, and the Los Angeles Chargers have two hungry rookies looking to do exactly that. For players trying to earn a spot on the roster and set up long-term careers, every repetition matters. Showing up to the practice facility early and leaving late are what can leave lasting impressions on the coaching staff.
Getting valuable work against elite-level talent in training camp will give them the chance to truly show the Chargers what they can bring to this defense. With that being said, these two rookies in particular are turning heads.
This won't shock most Charger fans, but first-round draft pick Akheem Mesidor is flashing in camp. The Canadian native had a phenomenal season with the Miami Hurricanes and is showing no signs of stopping.
The Chargers knew they were getting a talented player when they drafted Mesidor, but he is wasting no time showing why he belongs at the next level. According to Eric Smith of Chargers.com, Mesidor showed up big on a play splitting a double team and recording what would have been a legit tackle for loss.
On top of that, Chargers Editor Eric Smith also stated  "The 2026 first-round pick used a lethal spin move to get past right tackle Joe Alt, producing one of the cleanest wins we've seen so far in camp". Winning reps against Pro-Bowl caliber tackles is exactly what earns you the attention of the coaches.
With Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu alongside him, he won't have the pressure to carry the Chargers pass rush . He will now have more than enough freedom on that line to make meaningful plays. Mesidor also benefits from their knowledge of the game, getting helpful insights to elevate his talents. Having that at your disposal can be very beneficial in his development as a player.
This undrafted free agent coming out of Western Michigan has been gaining some attention as preseason continues. Nadame Tucker had a very productive year in 2025, recording over 14 sacks and 21 tackles for loss . Tucker is a legit game-wrecker, a player who can make big plays when it matters.
ESPN reporter Kris Rhim mentioned "Nadame Tucker looked great matched up against Taylor". Even rising stars from the offensive side of the ball are having problems with this guy. Tucker seems to be flashing every chance he gets, registering countless wins in team and individual drills.
Nadame Tucker has a real chance to turn this hype into something bigger. He will need a productive training camp and impressive preseason games to stay in the mix. If he can build on his already impressive start to camp, he might force the Chargers into making a tough roster decision.

title: Key Storylines Heading into Chargers' First Preseason Game Against the Texans
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers face off against the Houston Texans on Thursday in their first preseason matchup of the 2026 season. The 2026 season has brought significant changes to the Chargers organization with two new coordinators and entirely new offensive scheme and questions about how that will all look will be answered for the first time against the Texans.
The Chargers have created significant competition across the entire roster and have several fierce position battles that will need to be settled sooner rather than later. Let's dive into several questions and storylines to look forward to as the Chargers take on the Texans.
Chargers new defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary has one year of play-calling under hit belt at Western Michigan University. Thursday night will be the first time he calls plays in an NFL game. Obviously, in the first preseason game and without the regular starters, the call sheet will be fairly vanilla for O'Leary.
How the defensive operation under O'Leary will be worth keeping track of. Is the operation smooth despite new faces and constant rotation? Is there good communication? What is the defensive attitude?
This will be the first time the Chargers defense will face off against an opponent and be tested. It will be worth noting how the players who are in the game are playing and the coaching points that have been implemented. O'Leary has massive shoes to fill in replacing Jesse Minter and this will be the first indication of what style of defense the Chargers will bring to the table in 2026.
The Chargers opted for a battle between at least five players for the starting left guard position. Through OTAs and now into the third week of camp, it appears the job is down to three players but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was adamant that no one has been eliminated from the tournament in his words.
The Texans have a ferocious defensive front, even their backups will bring the fight to the Chargers which will be a blessing in terms of evaluating the offensive line. Will a player separate themselves against the Texans?
The Chargers coaching staff has stated that they want to name their starting offensive line somewhere around the second preseason game.  A standout performance could go a long way to settling this battle.
The back end of the linebacker room will be a tough battle to wrap up training camp. Former Michigan Wolverine and third-round pick Junior Colson has not been able to stay healthy and faces the risk of being left off the roster.
Colson and second-year linebacker Marlowe Wax are both physical linebackers in the run game but Colson needs to make up for lost time. Wax had a phenomenal preseason in 2025 and played at an undeniable level. He also impressed in his lone start of the season in week 18 against the Denver Broncos and should have built in momentum heading into the preseason games.
It is hard for inside linebackers to stand out in passing drills. They need an offensive and defensive line in front of them to read and react to and make plays. Facing the Texans will be the first chance to truly make an impression.
The Chargers' hiring of Mike McDaniel as their new offensive coordinator brought significant excitement to the organization and around the NFL. Questions have been raised at how their personalities would match with the quirky blend of the old school and the new. The two have built a great working relationship throughout the offseason and into training camp.
The first preseason game will be the test run with both of them on the sidelines. How will the dynamic work? How will they handle fourth -down calls and decision-making? Chris O'Leary has worked with Harbaugh before, this will be new for McDaniel and worth watching to see them work through any rough edges.
The Chargers have a rich history in finding gems that fit their team and culture amongst the UDFA class. Running back Austin Ekeler may be the most memorable in terms of playing his way from obscurity to a roster spot with incredible play in the preseason. Last year it was Marlowe Wax. Who will rise to moment and kick the door down?
The special teams units will be the spot for many bubble players to fight and make a name for themselves. Heading into the 2026 season, there are many questions that have yet to be answered and roles that special teams coordinator Ryan Ficken will need to fill.
Beyond Derius Davis as a returner, who else is capable of filling that role? Across from Deane Leonard, who will take the other gunner role? Assuming Tuli Tuipulotu takes a step back from special teams, who fills his role?
The preseason games will play a major factor in how many of the special teams roles are ultimately decided and could settle roster spot battles.

title: 6 Players to Watch During Chargers-Texans Week 1 Preseason Game
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers utilized a travel day on Wednesday and arrived in Houston, Texas, on the eve of their first preseason game. The Chargers and Texans face off at 5 p.m. on Thursday in a game that will not feature the regular starting lineup from the Chargers side.
The game will be the first true NFL action for the 2026 rookie class. There are several rookies with big questions to answer and there are several players locked in position and role battles who will have their first chance at making an impression against an opponent. Let's dive into players that require extra attention in this first matchup.
The Chargers drafted Jake Slaughter out of the University of Florida in the second round. Slaughter was a career center and the Chargers have hoped to transition him to guard and have him compete for the vacant starting left guard job.
As a prospect, Slaughter faced questions over his strength and ability to anchor against NFL-caliber defensive linemen. The Texans may not throw their starting lineup at Slaughter, but they have a deep defensive line and Slaughter will be put to the test.
Slaughter is currently in what appears to be a three-way battle for the starting job with veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year player Branson Taylor. Thursday night will provide a major test for Slaughter to see how he stacks up against the other challengers.
Genesis Smith fell to the fourth round of the draft where the Chargers selected him with their third pick of the round out of the University of Arizona. Smith has excellent instincts and great center field cover skills. He faced a massive question over his tackling in college and it was the reason he fell in the draft.
There will be no hiding from his weakness in his first NFL action. If he can prove his tackling issues were left behind in college, Smith could see a much larger role than originally anticipated for the defensive back room.
Nadame Tucker went undrafted out of Western Michigan despite leading the country in several pass-rushing categories. He is slightly undersized and an older rookie but his pass rush production, play style and connections to the coaching staff have him facing elevated expectations.
Tucker is the only undrafted rookie on the Chargers unofficial depth chart that is not listed last in their position group. He will be in a fierce battle with second-year edge rusher Kyle Kennard for potentially a final roster spot in the edge rusher room. Tucker has been destroying the Chargers backup tackles in practice with his violent and heavy-handed play style. Kennard has been playing well at practice too. Starting with the Texans, the preseason games will be a big factor for this battle and whether Tucker can perform to the expectations.
Junior Colson was once viewed as the top off-ball linebacker prospect in the 2024 draft. The Chargers selected him in the third round and unfortunately, the football gods have been cruel to Colson hitting him with injury after injury.
Colson will be facing a competition for a roster spot with the depth of the Chargers linebacker room leaving no room for error. Colson will need a dominant preseason for a shot at the roster and the physical Houston Texans will provide him the perfect showcase if he can seize the moment.
The Chargers do not have an open quarterback competition behind Justin Herbert, not yet at least. DJ Uiagalelei signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent following the 2025 draft in a return to his roots in Southern California.
Uiagalelei has been grinding and improving since his arrival in Los Angeles. Mike McDaniel's new offense seemed to click with him and he looked great in OTAs and has continued performing well throughout training camp. He got his first run with the second team on Tuesday and a big performance against the Texans could go a long way to inserting himself into a bigger quarterback battle.
Avery Smith was one of the most sought-after undrafted free agents and the Chargers landed him. Smith has long been favored amongst the UDFAs to have a shot to make the 53-man roster and he has lived up to the billing so far in training camp.
He will be in a battle against several other defensive backs for roster spots and his first action against the Texans can set the tone for the battle throughout the last few weeks of camp.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: RJ Mickens, A Sneaky Returning Key Contributor
full_text:
RJ Mickens, born on July 10, 2001, in Irving, Texas, grew up in a football family, being the son of longtime standout NFL DB Ray Mickens. With these roots, Mickens took his talents to Carroll High School in Southlake, Texas, where he played both offense and defense, notching 1,092 yards and 14 touchdowns while also producing 211 tackles with six going for a loss, two sacks, 32 pass deflections, eight interceptions, two fumble recoveries, and eight forced fumbles on defense. These elite career numbers saw Mickens ranked as a four-star prospect, according to 247Sports .
This led Mickens to commit to Clemson, where he played sparingly as a freshman. As a sophomore, he collected two interceptions, proving quickly to the team that he could be a real stalwart in the backend of a defense.
Moving on to 2022, his junior season, he added another three interceptions to his resume while adding 48 tackles, giving the team a reliable deep and box safety. 2023 had Mickens in a statistical slump, recording no interceptions on the season. He returned to school for his final year of eligibility and had his best year, recording two picks and 75 tackles (six of which were for loss).
Mickens would go into the 2025 NFL Draft, where teams viewed him as a Day 3 safety who could instantly compete for playing time, even with his limited athletic traits. His football IQ and instincts made up for his subpar testing numbers, allowing Mickens to be a real prospect in the eyes of NFL teams.
The Los Angeles Chargers were looking to get younger at the Safety position and drafted the Clemson product in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Mickens saw action in 12 games, proving to be a key contributor down the stretch of his first NFL season.
12 Games 29 Tackles 2 Interceptions 2 Pass Deflections
"R.J. Mickens signed a 4 year, $4,374,280 contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, including $174,280 signing bonus, $174,280 guaranteed, and an average annual salary of $1,093,570. In 2026, Mickens will earn a base salary of $1,005,000, while carrying a cap hit of $1,048,570 and a dead cap value of $130,710." - Spotrac
RJ Mickens finds himself in an intriguing spot going into year two of his NFL career. The Bolts drafted Genesis Smith in the fourth round, while still having Derwin James Jr. , Elijah Molden and Tony Jefferson as veteran playmakers.
While the Chargers could keep five safeties on the final 53-man roster, Mickens will be in a tough battle to keep the same role that he had during his rookie season. If he does continue in that role, look for Mickens to once again be a solid contributor for a Bolts defense that relies heavily on its safety talent.

title: Chargers Injury Tracker: Every Injury Update From Training Camp
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have some high-profile injuries to track as training camp continues.
Granted, the Chargers don’t have many injuries. But when one of the guys dealing with an issue is a top-10 player at his spot after missing all of last season due to injury, it becomes a much bigger deal than most training camps around the NFL.
The other guy battling injury , too, happens to be a player who is likely about to reset the entire NFL market at his position with a contract extension.
Tack on the usual wear and tear of training camp for other guys as things progress, and it can be tough to track all of the updates. Here’s a live-updating list of injury items to know for the Chargers.
This is the big one for the Chargers.
Rashawn Slater inked a big contract extension last year and suffered a torn patellar tendon in early August, ending his season before it started. Since, he’s been described loosely as ahead of schedule for most of the offseason before showing up for training camp work.
Last week when the Chargers put on pads in San Diego, though, his surgically repaired knee went through what he called a "minor flare-up" when asked by reporters. He’s been missing practice since.
Chargers fans, understandably, are worried. But considering the team made Slater available for a media session and he was pretty open about the whole thing, it doesn’t seem like a major concern.
That said, Slater’s practice participation is going to be something to closely watch until Week 1.
When Tuli Tuipulotu worked off to the side, if at all, to start camp, it seemed related to the mentioned contract extension talks.
Turns out it might have been something else.
According to Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, Tuipulotu has been “working through” an issue “ramping up” on his way to a return. The star edge rusher himself has said that he won’t comment on the contract and that working on the side away from teammates has been tough.
Like Slater, it’ll be interesting to see how and when Tuipulotu takes part in full practices before the season, but there’s the contract stuff in the background to watch, too.
A possible No. 1 wideout in Mike McDaniel’s scheme, Quentin Johnston has been held out of practice recently while he deals with some minor undisclosed setback.
The steal of a mid-round find for the Chargers defense a few years ago, Tarheeb Still has also been out with a minor undisclosed setback.

title: Jim Harbaugh Brought the Hammer Down after Chargers Practice Skirmish
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers training camp, by most accounts, has been pretty tame.
Granted, there are some important things happening. Rashawn Slater and Tuli Tuipulotu are battling injuries . The offense continues to figure out Mike McDaniel’s new offense while Justin Herbert leads the way, new stance in certain formations included.
But that almost casual nature of it all got broken up this week by, well, a fight.
Let a variety of onlookers tell it, linebacker Daiyan Henley got into it with the likes of edge rusher Bud Dupree and offensive lineman Cole Strange, which led to consequences from head coach Jim Harbaugh himself.
Cole Strange, a newcomer to the Chargers via free agency, was right in the thick of it with two Chargers defensive leaders, it seems.
According to Fernando Ramirez of The Sporting Tribune, the “skirmish” was possibly the first one under Jim Harbaugh at all.
The punishment? All three players going with Executive Director of Player Performance Ben Herbert to a side field for "focus exercises" for the remainder of practice.
And yes, fans at practice apparently captured footage of the dust-up that led to punishments, with Strange removing his helmet at the end of it all:
For those of you asking, here’s the video of the tiny skirmish today. Pretty much nothing but the 3 “involved” still had to go work out, away from the team with Ben Herbert. https://t.co/1ERFHg184O
Kris Rhim of ESPN classified the situation as so: "Daiyan Henley, Bud Dupree and Cole Strange left the team period early and worked off to the side with strength coach Ben Herbert."
This is pretty standard training camp stuff for most NFL teams around the league. But as Ramirez hinted, it’s extremely rare for a Harbaugh team, hence the punishments, even for a veteran like Dupree and one of the core team leaders in Henley.
Is it a bad thing? Probably not. A little fire in training camp during 11-on-11 work is hard to complain about, especially when the rest of camp so far has seemed pretty timid to onlookers.
Obviously, onlookers will want to keep track of whether anything else like this happens during camp. But most Chargers fans probably won’t complain about a new starting offensive lineman like Strange coming over and showing some aggression in front of the star quarterback after how the last few years have gone in the trenches.
They also happen to know what a leader Henley is, so it's not shocking to see a little tone-setting on that front from the heart of the defense.

title: Injury Updates, 1 on 1 Battles and Highlights From Chargers' Last Pregame Practice
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers held their second practice of Week 3 of 2026 training camp. Los Angeles is just two days away from their first preseason game against the Houston Texans and will have an off day for travel on Wednesday. The Chargers started their week on Monday with a light walkthrough but turned up the intensity on Tuesday with pads on.
Overall, the defense was dominant on Tuesday and several players fighting for roles flashed dominant plays. Several bubble players who are battling for roster spots also stood out heading into their first chance to prove themselves in live action. Let's dive into everything noteworthy from Tuesday's practice and press conferences.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh mentioned during his pre-practice press conference on Tuesday that aside from Rashawn Slater, two additional starting players are out of practice "working through something minor." Wide receiver Quentin Johnston and cornerback Tarheeb Still are both out of practice right now.
Rashawn Slater missed his fourth practice in a row and Harbaugh tried to avoid mentioning the specifics of what Slater was dealing with but Slater himself addressed the media and clarified the situation. It was apparent after he had missed his third practice in a row, that Slater had suffered a setback.
Slater did clarify that he felt something around his surgically repaired knee back at the first practice at the University of San Diego last Tuesday. The training staff is holding Slater back to make sure the discomfort he felt doesn't progress to something worse.
"We haven't seen anything that's really concerning. Obviously, it's not always the smoothest process coming back from a big injury," Slater said. "Nothing to be concerned about. Just being smart, being thoughtful with the way we progress.
The Chargers released their first unofficial depth chart following Sunday's practice to wrap u the second week of training camp. The depth chart is not made by the coaching staff and is made by the Chargers media team and PR staff and is therefore not truly indicative of where players stand. However, there were a handful of notable takeaways on the depth chart.
The unofficial depth chart had Tarheeb Still as the starter opposite veteran Donte Jackson or Cam Hart which was a bit of a surprise. Still was sidelined at practice and Jackson and Hart, who may be battling for a top role, put on a show. Jackson walked away with two interceptions on the day and Hart went toe to toe with Ladd McConkey showing off his physicality in press-man coverage.
Undrafted free agent edge rusher Nadame Tucker, who notably was the only UDFA not listed last in his position group on the unofficial depth chart, put on a show in one-on-ones against the offensive line. He even went straight through the chest of veteran offensive tackle Trey Pipkins, as he has been flashing his power.
Tucker is likely in a competition with Kyle Kennard for a role and potentially a roster spot. Meanwhile, Kennard had himself a day as well, showcasing an improved pass rush arsenal. The preseason games will be major for both players.
Defensive linemen Teair Tart, Jamaree Caldwell and Justin Eboigbe continue to be wrecking balls in the middle of the defensive line. Caldwell and Eboigbe both seem to be poised for and embracing the opportunity for larger roles heading into the season.
Wide receiver Keandre Lambert-Smith has stacked together multiple good practices and had a very good winning route in one-on-ones on Tuesday. Wide receiver Tre Harris channeled his inner Mike Williams with a phenomenal adjustment on a back-shoulder throw with Donte Jackson glued to him in coverage to haul in a spectacular catch.
okayyyyyyy tre' 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/jKFqEwO5gH
Edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu has appeared to have fully ended his hold-in and returned to full activities with the team. He spoke to the media for the first time since camp began after practice. Both he and coach Harbaugh danced around the wording of what was going on behind the scenes with the negotiations.
Tuipulotu clearly stated in regards to his contract heading into the final year of his rookie deal, "I'll let my agents and the guys upstairs handle that," Tuipulotu said. "Let the business handle business. I'm a football player. That's all I do. That's all I know."

title: Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua Injuries Becoming Worth Monitoring for Rams
full_text:
For a second consecutive practice, edge rusher Myles Garrett and wide receiver Puka Nacua were unable to participate. The Los Angeles Rams held Garrett out of the joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday due to knee swelling, while Nacua left with some soreness in his groin.
As the team prepared to practice on Thursday ahead of their preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, Garrett and Nacua were both seen working with trainers on the side.
Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett are both working out off to the side with the training staff during practice.
Throughout training camp, the Rams have been overly cautious with injuries . Quarterback Matthew Stafford has practiced every other day as he manages his back and the team tries to keep him as fresh as possible. The Rams have managed veterans such as Alaric Jackson, Byron Young, and Davante Adams as well.
Garrett missed three practices during the middle of training camp before practicing the final two days. McVay said that Garrett felt he was 85 percent on Tuesday, but the team erred on the side of caution. The same was said about Nacua, who left during the joint practice and did not return.
“Puka's doing well. He just had a little soreness in his psoas so we're just being smart with him,” said McVay on Thursday. “We're expecting to be back next week ready to go.”
While McVay was able to provide a timeline for Nacua’s return next week, that wasn’t the case with Garrett. That’s not to say that Garrett’s knee is something serious. However, it may be worth monitoring going forward.
This hasn’t quite reached the point where McVay’s tendency to lack transparency when discussing certain injuries should raise concern. It lines up with how the Rams have managed veterans throughout the offseason. Still, given that Garrett’s knee has been an issue multiple times within the span of a week, it certainly raises an eyebrow.
“He's feeling good. I think it's more along the lines of getting to know him and once he gets back to that return to performance,” said McVay. “He's making really good positive strides. As far as when he'll be back, we want to make sure that that's when it's truly 100%.”
The Rams gave up a lot to get Garrett, which makes the recurring knee swelling somewhat concerning. If the Rams are going to win the Super Bow,l Garrett is going to play a big role in that. It’s why they traded for him.
To be clear, that’s not to say that Garrett has a lingering issue that will affect his play. By all accounts, Garrett has met expectations and been as advertised when he’s been on the field. With that said, it’s fair to wonder if this is something that could linger into the regular season.
There is still plenty of time before the Rams play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. The goal is to be as healthy as possible going into that game. It does the Rams no good to push Garrett now and risk aggravating the injury. The same goes for Nacua. Until then, the Rams are likely to remain cautious, but that doesn’t mean injuries like Garrett’s aren’t worth monitoring closely.

title: Rams RB Jarquez Hunter Has Something to Prove This Preseason
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams released their initial depth chart of the preseason on Wednesday, one thing stood out immediately. After drafting running back Jarquez Hunter in the fourth round last year, he was listed behind Ronnie Rivers and alongside undrafted free agents Dean Connors and Jordan Waters.
If anything, it emphasized just how important this preseason is for Hunter. With a competitive roster, there’s no guarantee that Hunter will make the roster. The Rams have gone into the season with three running backs in the past, and they could do so again. Hunter needs to have a strong preseason to show that he deserves a roster spot.
Still, that doesn’t make it less concerning that Hunter is listed where he is on the depth chart. It wasn’t surprising that Hunter didn’t play much as a rookie. The Rams typically bring their rookies along slowly and Blake Corum got limited action the year before. However, heading into his second year in the offense, it would have been fair to expect Hunter to progress.
Multiple things can be true when it comes to Hunter. It’s very possible that he’s done everything that the coaching staff has asked of him. Just because he’s lower on the depth chart doesn’t mean he hasn’t progressed. At the same time, there was reason to expect Hunter to be ahead of Rivers at this point.
However, Hunter didn’t play a single snap on offense as a rookie , and he also doesn’t provide the same special teams value as Rivers. Hunter played just 22 special teams snaps during the regular season, which all came within the first six weeks. He was inactive from Week 7 to Week 18. It is worth mentioning that Hunter played 13 special teams snaps in the Wild Card round against the Carolina Panthers.
When the Rams drafted Hunter, there was a need for his skill set in the offense. In 2024, the Rams’ running game lacked explosiveness. They had the lowest explosive run rate at just 1.8 percent. It made sense then to draft the player who had the second-highest explosive run rate among FBS running backs with 150 or more carries.
Things have changed since then. At the time of drafting Hunter, Kyren Williams was in the final year of his rookie deal. The Rams hadn’t extended a running back since Todd Gurley following the 2017 season. Given Williams’ value to the run game, the Rams opted to extend him in August.
Additionally, very few would have expected Blake Corum to break out in the way that he did . Corum ranked fifth in the NFL in explosive run rate, bringing the Rams into the top 10 in that stat category. He also finished 10th in missed tackles forced per attempt.
It’s fair to say that the Rams should have had an idea that they were going to try to bring back Williams during April’s draft. However, it’s unlikely that they expected Corum to take a huge step forward. When the Rams drafted Corum, they also saw him as a similar style of running back to Williams with a similar skill set. Instead, he’s turned out to be the perfect complementary piece.
It seems harsh to call Hunter a bust, especially after one year. Simply put, the context within the roster has changed significantly since the Rams drafted Hunter. That doesn’t mean he isn’t a good player, buthis lack of special teams ability also limits his overall value on the roster given the depth at the running back position.
Given the excitement around the Hunter pick last year, it’s certainly disappointing to see him buried on the initial depth chart. However, that doesn’t mean he can’t prove himself during the preseason and earn a spot on the 53. While he may not be the complementary back that many expected when he was drafted, there is still an opportunity for him to find his place on the roster.

title: Rams May Have Underestimated Stetson Bennett Entering 2026
full_text:
Entering the 2026 offseason, there was always some possibility that the Los Angeles Rams could look for their quarterback of the future. That was especially the case after Jimmy Garoppolo announced that he was considering retirement.
With the 13th overall pick, the Rams drafted Ty Simpson to presumably be the heir to quarterback Matthew Stafford. There were certainly some questions around Simpson, especially regarding his lack of college experience. At the same time, it was hard to question his overall fit in the offense.
Still, in a season with Super Bowl expectations, some thought that the Rams would have been better off drafting a player who could contribute immediately. While a player such as Makai Lemon or Monroe Freeling may have just been depth, Lemon would have gotten some playing time as the third wide receiver.Additionally, Freeling or another offensive lineman would have given the Rams depth on the offensive line and could have been needed at some point during the season.
Heading into training camp, there was a battle for the backup quarterback spot between Simpson and Stetson Bennett. It wouldn’t have been at all surprising had Simpson overtaken Bennett by the end of training camp. However, that simply hasn’t been the case.
Bennett hasn’t given the Rams’ coaching staff a reason to turn to Simpson. In fact, Bennett has exceeded expectations and impressed coaches throughout training camp.
“He really has [grown] and I've mentioned it,” said head coach Sean McVay. “He's aggressive. He's a playmaker. He's going to be aggressive but not reckless. He can make some things happen off-schedule. The way that we're able to get in and out of the huddle in terms of his overall command has been significantly improved upon and the way that he works at it…It's cool to be able to see a lot of the work that he's put in pay off with the way that he's playing and the respect he has from his teammates.”
Drafted out of Georgia in the fourth round in 2023, it was always thought that Bennett could be the long-term backup and potentially a bridge quarterback after Stafford retired. Following the 2022 season in which the Rams relied on John Wolford and Bryce Perkins before signing Baker Mayfield, they wanted to find a more permanent solution to the backup quarterback spot.
Through his first two seasons, it didn’t look like that was going to be Bennett . Despite his extensive college experience, Bennett threw one touchdown to three interceptions as a rookie before stepping away from football and leaving the team.
Bennett returned in 2024, but threw two touchdowns to five interceptions during the preseason. When the Rams played their backups in Week 18, they turned to Garoppolo rather than give Bennett experience in a regular season game.
After a full year in the system, Bennett flipped those numbers last year, throwing five touchdowns to two interceptions. His turnover-worthy play rate dropped from 9.1 percent to 5.6 percent. Still, Bennett remained the third-string quarterback behind Garoppolo.
It’s fair to wonder if the Rams underrated Bennett heading into 2026 . McVay made it clear that Simpson would compete with Bennett. The rookie is very clearly on his own development path. At the same time, nobody would have been surprised, and some may have expected Simpson to overtake Bennett by the start of the preseason.
Few would have been surprised had the Rams completely moved on from Bennett during roster cutdowns. Instead, Bennett has gained the respect of the coaching staff and players on the team.
“When you look at Stetson, you can see he carries a certain type of aura and swag when he enters the field,” said running back Blake Corum. “He's not scared to cut it loose. He goes out there with utmost confidence and his form is beautiful…You can hear it in the huddle when he's calling the plays, he's saying it with authority…He's balled out this camp and he's only going to continue to get better.”
Bennett continually impressed during training camp to the point where the Rams seem to feel comfortable with him as the backup. McVay has noted that Bennett may not even play during the preseason. It’s a clear sign that the Rams are confident in him and see him as key depth.
Given Bennett’s experience in the system, there was always going to be some level of catch-up for Simpson entering training camp. With that said, the Rams may not have expected Bennett to hold off Simpson for as long as he has.
This isn’t to say that the Rams made the wrong choice by taking Simpson. Bennett has yet to play a regular season snap outside of a kneel down. It’s difficult to know how he’d fare as a starter, especially considering his smaller frame.
At a minimum, Bennett has shown that he can be an extension of the coaching staff and be a backup in this system. Simpson will still need to beat him out eventually, but the growth of Bennett has been one of the best stories of the offseason. Simpson may still be the quarterback of the future, but Bennett has made it clear that he isn’t ready to simply hand him the job.

title: Rams Add Former Third-Round Pick to Linebacker Room Ahead of Preseason
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams continue to make additions to the roster ahead of their first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. On Thursday, the Rams signed former third-round pick and linebacker Monty Rice.
Rice was drafted in the third round by the Tennessee Titans in 2021 out of Georgia where he earned First-Team All-SEC honors as a senior. Throughout his five-year NFL career, Rice has appeared in 39 games with the Titans, New England Patriots, and Detroit Lions. Rice has started 11 games while totaling 110 tackles, five tackles for loss, and two passes defended.
After being drafted in the third round, the Titans moved on after a Week 13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in 2023. While he had veterans ahead of him on the depth chart during his first two seasons, he was expected to start in his third season However, Rice was outplayed by an undrafted free agent in training camp and remained in a depth role. He was also absent for personal reasons for the majority of the preseason.
Head coach Mike Vrabel said at the time , “It just didn’t work out. I’m sure Monty will go on and have another opportunity. We’ll give other guys opportunities here."
Most of Rice’s impact throughout his career has come on special teams, where he has played 475 total snaps and has 21 special teams tackles. As a rookie, Rice was Pro Football Focus’ 11th-highest-graded special teams player. He also graded highly in 2024 with the Patriots.
Rice did play extensively in 2022 on defense. Among linebackers with at least 350 snaps, Rice ranked 20th in run defense. He also had the 15th-best tackling grade, and his 4.7 percent missed tackle rate was the seventh-best.
While linebacker remains a weakness for the Rams , the top of the depth chart is mostly set. It will remain an uphill battle for Rice to make the roster with Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, and Grant Stuard all above him on the depth chart. With that said, the Rams lack experience at linebacker behind them. Rice could certainly compete for a spot on the team’s practice squad.
It’s clear that the Rams are trying to find some better depth on the practice squad as Elias Neal and Kai Hill-Green were the only options heading into the summer. The Rams also recently signed linebacker Daniel Rickert .
Rice may not be the same player he was when the Titans drafted him in the third round, but it’s a low-risk move for the Rams as they head into the preseason. It’s possible that Rice earns a spot on the practice squad. If he doesn’t, Rice at least gets some tape that he can show other teams during the season.

title: State of the 2026 Rams Offensive Line: Is the Depth Good Enough?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are entering a season in which they will have Super Bowl expectations. However, if the Rams are going to achieve those goals, they will have to stay healthy . When the Rams have struggled over the past four years, it’s been when the offensive line has had injuries.
That would be the case for most teams, but the Rams can’t afford to put themselves in a precarious position this season. For the offense and team overall to hit its potential, the offensive line has to find a way to stay healthy.
Last season, the Rams were able to get by with Justin Dedich when Steve Avila and Kevin Dotson were injured. However, they still went just .500 in those games. In the late-season loss to the Atlanta Falcons, DJ Humphries was exploited at left tackle.
This is something that’s already become problematic as Alaric Jackson awaits the NFL’s ruling on a potential suspension. Justin Dedich has also missed the entirety of training camp with a hand injury that he suffered over the Fourth of July that wasn’t fireworks-related.
This was one of the best offensive lines a year ago, and that should be the expectation heading into 2026. With that said, Brandon Thorn of the Trench Warfare Substack and Bleacher Report ranked them 17th and in Tier 3 . There are still legitimate questions about the unit. Let’s take a look at how the Rams have built their offensive line.
Last offseason, the Rams gave Jackson a contract that made him their franchise left tackle. After Joe Noteboom didn’t work out, Jackson won the starting left tackle spot and never gave it up. While he may not be one of the premier left tackles, he’s provided stability at the position over the last two years.
While Jackson has been reliable, he has missed playing time and gotten himself into off-field situations. Jackson has managed blood clots in his legs, which has forced him to miss a few days of practice as he manages the medication. Additionally, he was arrested this past offseason for felony domestic battery charges that were later dropped . With that said, the NFL could still decide to suspend him, especially given that he’s a multi-time offender.
Brandon Thorn of the Trench Warfare Substack recently graded every offensive lineman in the NFL and ranked them at each position. Thorn ranked Jackson as the 29th-best left tackle.
“Jackson established himself as a functional starter inside the Rams' ultra-friendly offensive structure, which limits true dropback exposure through heavy play-action usage and Matthew Stafford's quick trigger,” said Thorn. “Jackson is a wide, heavy-bodied and sawed-off tackle with below-average movement skills. Still, he has enough play-strength and craft to survive when the rep stays on his terms.”
Alaric Jackson going to work against one of the best pass rushers in the game. Via @BrandonThornNFL pic.twitter.com/DJaXuf2WAF
Giving Jackson a grade of 60 and placing him in the ‘replacement level’ tier seems harsh. When Jackson is on the field, he’s a steady presence at left tackle, even if the Rams’ system benefits him. He may not have the pure talent of other players at the position, but he’s been productive.
Last season, Pro Football Focus graded Jackson as the 11th overall tackle, grading 10th in run-blocking and 22nd in pass-blocking. The Rams could look to move on from him after this season, but he’s been exactly what they’ve needed at the left tackle position. When Jackson is out, the offense suffers, as was evident last year against the Falcons when the Rams had to turn to DJ Humphries.
This is a big season for Steve Avila as he enters a contract season . The Rams drafted Avila with the 36th overall pick in 2023. With Avila and Dotson up for extensions at the end of the season, the Rams may need to make a choice between the two players.
“I try not to think about that stuff too much, but I just want to be who I am and I know all that stuff will work itself out,” said Avila. “All that stuff will work itself out soon, and again, I’m not thinking about it too much. I just want to go out there and do what I can for this team.”
While he hasn’t disappointed, he also hasn’t necessarily played up to expectations . When the Rams tried to move Avila to center in 2024, it was something that didn’t work. Avila has managed injuries throughout his career. When he returned from injured reserve last season, the Rams made him earn his starting role back from Justin Dedich.
Avila received a grade of 71 from Thorn, placing him in the “reliable contributor” tier.
“When available, Avila remained a powerful, physically imposing left guard with the size and play-strength to generate movement in the run game and anchor against power in pass protection,” wrote Thorn. “His pass protection is more strength-based than refined, relying on mass, anchor and body positioning to absorb rushers rather than high-end hand usage or recovery skill. The limitations show up when quicker defenders force him to redirect, mirror late movement or win the hand fight before he can establish control.”
The Lions really struggled defending the Rams' double teams all day. Rams run duo. Steve Avila takes DJ Reader out of the play. Good vision from Blake Corum to cutback and hit the hole. His vision is one of his strengths. pic.twitter.com/Hu87yac2eb
There’s no doubt that Avila has the athleticism and talent to be a Pro Bowl-caliber guard. If he can stay healthy, he could reach those heights. However, the first three years of his career have seen some inconsistencies.
Pro Football Focus graded Avila as the eighth-best guard last season, ranking him ninth in run-blocking and 20th in pass protection. Along with Kevin Dotson, the Rams have one of the strongest and overall best guard duos in the NFL. Avila is a big part of that.
The Rams brought back Coleman Shelton last season after a year away. In 2024, the Rams tried Avila at center and then Jonah Jackson. While Beaux Limmer played admirably, the Rams needed a more experienced player in that spot. Shelton at least provided someone the team could rely on .
“He's pivotal to the whole offensive line. He's literally QB2 in our minds when it comes to play calling and stuff like that,” said right guard Kevin Dotson. “He's put that dedication in, watching the tape, being in there with the quarterbacks to know what the quarterbacks are thinking, what ‘nine’ wants this week. So we trust him with our whole hearts that he's going to get the job done and he's really meticulous in the way he likes to run so we like that.”
That’s quite the endorsement from Dotson early in training camp. While Shelton may not be the most talented center, he’s the glue of the offensive line. He connects the quarterback to the five players in protection.
Longest run of the day for Rams RB Kyren Williams. Well executed blocks by Kevin Dotson and Coleman Shelton to create the hole. Good blocking at the 2nd level by Parkingson and Whittington. pic.twitter.com/pXH8389bwD
In his center rankings, Thorn gave Shelton a grade of 70, placing him at 14th and in the reliable contributor tier.
“Shelton returned to the Rams in 2025 after one season with the Chicago Bears and immediately stabilized the pivot, starting 20 games including the playoffs,” said Thorn. “Shelton is a clear-eyed presence with the awareness to sort line games, pass off stunts and use active hands to play longer than his measurements suggest. His lack of size still shows up against high-end power and length, but his technique, toughness and fit inside the Rams' system make him a rock-solid starting center.”
Shelton has proven to be exactly what the Rams need at the center position on the offensive line. Again, Pro Football Focus only graded him as the 11th-best overall center in the NFL, ranking him seventh in run-blocking and 29th in pass-blocking. Shelton provides so much value with his understanding of the offense and overall football IQ. He very clearly has his strengths and weaknesses, but the Rams are able to game plan around…

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From the Rams’ Initial 2026 Depth Chart
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams released their initial depth chart ahead of the first preseason game. While the initial depth chart doesn't mean a lot, it can still provide some clarity at certain positions. Here are seven takeaways from the Rams’ initial depth chart.
It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that Stetson Bennett is the backup quarterback . Bennett took all of the backup reps throughout training camp and the Rams were very impressed with his overall growth and confidence in the offense. AIt’s not a knock on Ty Simpson, as he remains on his own development path. The Rams seem to be pleased with both guys. Right now, Bennett’s experience in the offense gives him the edge.
It seems harsh to call Jarquez Hunter a bust after one season. However, he didn’t play any offensive snaps as a rookie and is listed behind Ronnie Rivers and alongside Dean Connors and Jordan Waters as he goes into year two. Hunter could certainly be a special teams contributor, but after being drafted in the fourth round, more was expected from him coming out of Auburn.
When the Rams drafted Trost, it was unclear where they would play him. Some projected him inside. However, the Rams seemingly see him as a tackle. To see him behind McClendon as the backup is a positive. Trost should get plenty of work during the preseason, which will be good to see.
Looking at the offensive line, seeing Dylan McMahon at center behind Coleman Shelton was certainly a surprise. Back in 2024, Beaux Limmer started the majority of the season at center with Jonah Jackson injured and played admirably. The Rams played Limmer at guard last year and he struggled. McMahon at center is certainly something to watch going forward.
At the beginning of training camp, Xavier Smith and Kyren Williams were both returning punts and were both returning punts and competing for the job. Smith was listed as the starting punt returner on the team’s depth chart with Konata Mumpfield behind him. That could be a positive sign for Smith when it comes to making the roster.
While it was odd that the Rams listed their top four tight ends as starters , it shouldn’t be too surprising. It’s clear that the Rams see all four as being interchangeable.
“I don't expect anyone in particular to come out on top,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase last week. “I think those guys push each other and challenge each other and are so versatile that you're just excited to see who ends up coming to life based on what the defense wants to do…They all can do so much, both in the run game and the pass game, that you're excited just based on a game plan.”
The Rams may have their internal hierarchy, and some guys will play more than others. However, the Rams see those four players as being able to do similar things. Who starts or plays more will likely depend on the matchup or who’s hot at the time.
Late last season, the Rams moved Desjuan Johnson from the interior defensive line to the edge and had success. The Rams liked what they saw, as that’s where he’s played all offseason and where he’s listed on the depth chart. Johnson was listed as the backup edge to Myles Garrett and could be part of the rotation.

title: 5 Things to Watch When Rams Release Initial Depth Chart
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams get ready for their first preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs, they will release their initial depth chart of the preseason. The Rams likely won’t give up a lot when it comes to the initial depth chart, butit still provides a good look at how the team views certain players. Here are five things to watch for when the Rams release their initial depth chart.
When the Rams release their initial depth chart, it seems almost inevitable that Stetson Bennett will end up ahead of Ty Simpson . Multiple things can be true here. Bennett has certainly earned the backup quarterback role and the Rams appear to trust him there. He has taken all of the backup reps throughout the entirety of the offseason.
At the same time, it shouldn’t be taken as a knock on Simpson. The Rams are bringing him along at his own pace. Additionally, the Rams typically list rookies behind established veterans on the depth chart. In 2023, Puka Nacua was listed behind Tutu Atwell. Terrance Ferguson was listed as the fourth tight end last year behind Davis Allen. The Rams know where each player stands and they aren’t going to reveal a lot on the Week 1 preseason depth chart.
With all of that said, it will be interesting to see where the Rams list CJ Daniels. Daniels has been a standout throughout training camp and the offseason program. The Rams may not have a true WR3, but where Daniels ends up will be something to watch.
Given how the Rams handle rookies, it wouldn’t be surprising, and probably should be expected for Daniels to be behind Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith, and Konata Mumpfield. At the same time, he’s shown a lot throughout training camp to potentially get listed alongside Whittington.
Not a lot has been said about Keagan Trost throughout the offseason. Early in training camp, Kevin Dotson mentioned that Trost had taken some snaps with the ones.
“He has gotten in there and competed, which is what you want,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “You want guys to go look like they belong. He definitely does that.”
When the Rams drafted Trost, it was unclear where they would play him. While he played tackle at Mizzou, he projected better as a guard at the next level. It’ll be eye-opening to see if the Rams list Trost behind Warren McClendon at right tackle or behind one of the guards.
The Rams are set at the top of the cornerback depth chart with Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Behind them is where it gets interesting. Emmanuel Forbes is likely the CB3 behind Watson. However, it’s unclear where the Rams could list Josh Wallace and Cam Lampkin.
Wallace is more of a slot player, but Lampkin has had a strong training camp. Additionally, Quentin Lake is technically a safety, but the Rams played him as their nickel most of last year. With how Chris Shula uses his defensive backs, there are several ways the Rams could structure the depth chart at this position.
Heading into the offseason, a competition at punt returner didn’t seem to be in the cards . However, that’s exactly what’s taken place as Kyren Williams and Xavier Smith split reps as the team’s punt returner during training camp.
It wouldn’t be surprising to see Smith listed as the starter, but how the Rams list it on the depth chart will be very telling. If Williams is listed as the team’s punt returner, it could make for some difficult decisions come roster cutdowns.

title: What Rams’ Joint Practice With Cowboys Revealed About Week 1
Rams Face Interesting Decision With Stetson Bennett in Preseason
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play their first preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs. However, one of the biggest questions heading into that game is how head coach Sean McVay will handle the quarterback position .
There is no doubt that Ty Simpson will play. That has been confirmed by McVay and it’s the correct call given that it is the only live-game experience he’ll get as a rookie. Simpson only had one year of starting experience at Alabama. Playing during the preseason will be key for his overall development.
However, McVay wasn’t sure whether Bennett would play or rest like other key depth. McVay only noted on Tuesday that he had discussions with quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone and that he would have a clearer answer on Thursday.
Over the past few years, the Rams have rested their backup quarterback while Bennett has played the entirety of the game. With that said, the Rams’ backup at the time was Jimmy Garoppolo, who didn’t need preseason reps. This may be Bennett’s fourth preseason, but he still doesn’t have the same experience as Garoppolo.
The preseason could still be beneficial for Bennett. He’s certainly gotten more comfortable in the offense and looked good last year during the preseason. Bennett also had a lot more college experience than Simpson had coming out of Georgia.
Still, unlike Garoppolo, Bennett doesn’t have the experience of starting regular season games. In two years with the team, he hasn’t taken a real regular season snap outside of a kneel-down. The snaps during the preseason are the only live-game reps he’s gotten as well.
That’s not to say that Bennett and Simpson should evenly split the preseason reps with one playing the first half and the other playing the second. However, it would make sense for Bennett to play the first quarter or at least the first drive or two simply to get those live-game reps even if that’s just for the first two preseason games.
While Bennett has shown improvement, he still has things that he needs to work on in games. His interception numbers were down last year, but he has a tendency to overlook coverage in the middle of the field or put the ball in harm’s way. That was seen during the joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys.
3️⃣ INTs Have yourself a day, @justinbarron22 👏 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/Dfv4SLCtmK
The priority for the preseason s hould be to get Simpson as many reps as possible . If the Rams chose to play him the entire game, it would make sense. At the same time, those are reps that are still valuable for Bennett. He’s not the seasoned veteran that Garoppolo was the last two years.
It’s clear that the Rams trust Bennett as he’s taken every backup quarterback rep throughout training camp. However, the live-game reps are still valuable for Bennett given his lack of regular season experience.
McVay has typically prioritized keeping starters and key depth healthy during the preseason. If Bennett is the backup quarterback, he would likely be included in that. However, there wouldn’t be a significant drop-off if something happened to Bennett given that the Rams drafted Simpson. They have two very capable backup options behind Stafford. Getting both players live-game experience during the preseason would benefit the Rams more than keeping Bennett on the sideline.

title: Raiders vs. Cardinals: Winners & Losers; Training Camp Report 17
full_text:
LAS VEGAS, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders kicked off the 2026 NFL preseason a few hours ago by hosting the Arizona Cardinals here at Allegiant Stadium in a 27-14 loss.
There were several significant happenings in the contest relative to players, and we will break that down shortly, but before we dig into the winners and losers from a player standpoint, let’s look at some coaching and organizational issues that stood out.
1. It is a new day in the desert, and as Tom Brady took the field with GM John Spytek , it marked a fresh start. This isn’t a Super Bowl team, but every decision those two men made this offseason has been tactical, deliberate, and made sense.
If this rebuild fails, and the odds are stacked against it, if the decision process continues on the trend in which it is, there won’t be any Monday morning quarterbacking from this reporter.
2. The Metropolitan Police Department here in Las Vegas does a truly magnificent job. Recently, Officer Austin Abdelnabi lost his life in the line of duty. It was classy and warranted that the franchise have a moment of silence to honor our fallen hero.
1. Klint Kubiak called the plays like he was back in the Super Bowl, with ease. The opening drive lasted 10 plays and covered 68 yards, and the team looked polished and poised. Sure, it was a preseason game, but it was his first as a head coach, and he played it like a master.
2. Additionally, for a rookie coach, there are usually numerous logistical issues that come with the first-time head man role. Kubiak was born into the NFL, literally, with his dad as a player, then an assistant coach, then a head coach, and Kubiak followed. The game-day logistics were flawless, and I asked Kubiak about that.
"I thought it was smooth there. I thought our coaches did a good job communicating on the headset. The game itself, we have a lot to improve on. I was very happy with what our defense did in the second half on the third down after the first half. But there's a lot of things that we need to improve on."
3. On the aforementioned first drive, facing an important third-and-one, it was nice after last season to see the team line up in the I formation and actually run for a first down. On Fernando Mendoza’s second drive, the Raiders had a fourth and one that they converted as well. For years, Raider Nation has heard that this franchise will run the football; tonight, Kubiak proved it.
4. Kubiak had a lot of reasons to celebrate if he were still an offensive coordinator. He isn’t, so when asked about his leaders and the game, he quickly brought reality back to the conversation.
"Well, I think we lost by two scores, so we've got to get better there."
5. Mendoza isn’t done yet. When asked how he plans to hand out reps at QB to the rookie in the final two preseason games, he made that point clear.
"We want to get him plenty of reps in the preseason. That was important for us to see him get lots of turns. And as these games go on, we're going to evaluate game-to-game, but he's a young man that needs experience and needs reps and we're going to get them to him."
6. One injury of note, and an explanation from the head coach on Maxx Crosby not playing.
"B-Jack [Brennan Jackson] had a foot, so we'll evaluate him tomorrow. And then, obviously, Maxx [Crosby] did not play, that was my decision. And I'll take your questions."
1. No matter what happened tonight, the young man who had NFL executives raving, Fernando Mendoza, was the story of his first preseason game. He was 10/16 with one touchdown pass (to Jack Bech) and 0 interceptions. His quarterback rating (QBR) was an impressive 100. He was sacked once, and it was a great learning sack.
He isn’t in college anymore, and that one was on him. Not a big deal, or a red flag of any kind. There will be more of those this year. I truly believe that, in his heart, Kubiak was happy, but he wasn’t handing out his rookies' trophies tonight. He was asked afterward about Mendoza’s play.
"Yeah, there'll be some good some good lessons that we look forward to attacking with the tape with him. He knows you can't take a sack and those are things he's going to grow from."
2. Kirk Cousins looked exactly how you expected. He was 5/6 for 50 yards, one touchdown pass, and zero interceptions as well. His QBR was 141. Kubiak was happy with what Captain Kirk gave him and told me so after the game.
“Really happy with what the offense did in that first drive; Kirk [Cousins] leading us down the field.”
3. The first and second team defensive units were both unimpressive. In fairness, I thought the starting linebackers looked good, but the defensive backs and defensive line for both units struggled. I have no issues with rookies struggling, so don’t read too much into it. Kubiak was kind about his defensive backfield tonight, but honest.
"I just think we’ve got a lot of growth to do as a team. As a team, we've got a lot of growth to do, so starts tomorrow."
4. I was very impressed with Mike Washington Jr, the rookie RB from Arkansas, both as a runner, in the passing game, and as a kick returner. He had a special 53-yard run that showed both his speed and power. Someone tell the former Razorback that his new head coach is a fan of his.
"Pleased with what Mike [Washington Jr.]; Mike did some good things just like he practiced. I think he was the same player that we've seen in practice. Had a big run, just got to keep giving him more outs as preseason goes.”
5. Jordan Meredith, whom I projected to be in a battle for his spot on the 53-man roster with Will Putnam, had a penalty that won’t help his cause in a battle for a job. I expect more out of him at this point in his career, vying to back up Tyler Linderbaum.
6. Tommy “Freaking” Eichenberg had a devastating penalty. That was a mistake at this point in his career; he can’t make it. He didn’t play poorly after that, but that mistake, early in the game for a veteran, was big.
7. His fellow “Berg,” Cody Lindenberg, played terrific. He made his reads, flipped his hips, and lent assistance when it wasn’t his play, and showed significant improvement in using his hands to shed blockers.
8. DE Patrick Johnson, the sixth-year player out of Tulane, flashed for the first time tonight on several occasions. He hasn’t had a bad camp, but as a sixth-year player, he has played as I expected. Tonight, he exceeded that.
9. The FAA called and wants to register the leg of AJ Cole.
10. DE Cian Slone had a sack in which he looked like the Incredible Hulk, taking out the Cardinals' QB. My last projection of the 53-man roster had him making it, and he did nothing tonight to move me off that opinion.
11. It was terrific to see WR Jack Bech have his best performance of his NFL career tonight. Game, practice - it doesn’t matter. Tonight was his best, and he got a touchdown from Mendoza out of it. Kubiak was ecstatic about his sophomore wideout.
“He stepped up, had an excellent game. He really has had an impressive camp as far as just being a guy that's continually straining and getting better and hasn't had all the ops in practice and then he came out tonight and was ready to roll. So, I was happy but not surprised with what he did tonight."
