title: Analyzing No. 1 Overall Pick Fernando Mendoza's Raiders Premiere
full_text:
LAS VEGAS, Nev. -- The Las Vegas Raiders followed up the completion of a solid first training camp under head coach Klint Kubiak with another solid day of work on the field. Thursday night's preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals put that on display.
No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was on the field for most of Thursday night's game, showcasing many of the reasons Las Vegas used the top pick of the draft on him. Mendoza had his ups and downs on Thursday, with many more ups than downs.
Below are a few notes from Mendoza's performance during Las Vegas' loss to the Cardinals.
The Raiders have spent the past few weeks practicing against each other in training camp and offseason workouts. Thursday night gave Mendoza and the Raiders a chance to improve by playing another team, providing Las Vegas with a quality measuring stick for the upcoming season.
Mendoza completed 10 of his 16 passes against the Cardinals, registering 97 passing yards. Las Vegas may have lost the exhibition matchup, but the improvement Mendoza and the rest of the team made was well worth a meaningless loss in August.
There are more than a few reasons to be excited about Mendoza's future in the desert.
Against the Cardinals, Mendoza showcased his accuracy, arm, and ability to read defenses quickly. There were several times when Mendoza's willingness to check the ball down helped keep the ball moving and the Raiders' offense on the field.
In just one preseason game, Mendoza looked more competent than any of the quarterbacks Las Vegas featured last season. Furthermore, he did so while playing with largely Las Vegas' reserve offensive line. Arizona had reserves in as well, but the point remains the same.
Las Vegas put Mendoza in during their second offensive drive of the game. Mendoza faced a few Cardinals starters as well. After one preseason game, there is legitimate reason for cautious optimism regarding Mendoza.
Thursday repeatedly confirmed that if Mendoza has a clean pocket, there is a high probability that he will make the right decisions, be on time, and be accurate with the pass. This should encourage Las Vegas' front office to continue revamping their roster, especially on offense.
This may seem simple, but blocking, quarterback decision-making, and execution have eluded the Raiders in recent seasons. Mendoza has a long way to go, but the potential is undoubtedly there. Thursday was more confirmation that Las Vegas is headed in the right direction .
Just as there were positives for Mendoza, there were small areas he will look to improve moving forward. The rookie quarterback took a sack that was a testament to the difference in speed Mendoza experienced in his first game as a professional compared to his college days.
There were also a few passes that Mendoza could have completed had he read the defense a little better. There were also passes he completed that could have yielded greater gains with more time and a better understanding of Kubiak's offense. This will come in time, as Mendoza noted.
“I think it comes from the standard that Coach [Klint] Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko and Coach [Mike] Sullivan demand. Especially in OTAs. There was maybe one or two practices, or two reps, that I thought, ‘Hey, this was a really, really good rep.’ Then when we get in the film room, and maybe it might have slipped past in college, but when we get in the film room, you get torn apart because of a small detail," Mendoza said during training camp.
“Then you end up realizing when you watch the game film and you talk to the veterans, ‘Hey, in the game, the margins are only even smaller.’ In reality, when you thought that was a great ball, it's really a 50/50 ball because you didn't throw in the correct timing."
“Being able to learn from that and have, honestly, frustrations with my own play has helped my growth. It has helped new neurological pathways form because it creates that pressure, and that positive pressure and that positive stress, in order to grow and learn as a quarterback."

title: Biggest Takeaways From Raiders' Preseason Opener vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders faced off against the Arizona Cardinals in their first preseason game of the 2026 season.
Las Vegas fell short on the scoreboard, but had one of their most productive days of work under Klint Kubiak.
In limited action, running back Ashton Jeanty rushed for 16 yards on three carries, and Kirk Cousins completed five of his six passes for 50 yards and a touchdown. It was brief, but Las Vegas' 10-play opening drive, which spanned 68 yards and took over five minutes off the game clock, was refreshing.
The Raiders' first drive was a reminder of just how bad the offense was last season. The opening drive that Las Vegas manufactured against Arizona confirmed that they have a coaching staff that understands how football in today's league works. The Raiders attacked all three levels of Arizona's defense.
Over the past three seasons, it has seemed like Las Vegas' offense needed every little thing to go right just to complete a pass, let alone score a touchdown. On Thursday, the Raiders' coaching staff confirmed that their offensive play-calling will be logical and make sense.
That has definitely not been the case in recent seasons for the Raiders.
Mendoza saw plenty of action on Thursday night against the Cardinals, which is important for several reasons. For the first time, Mendoza was able to get a full dose of life as a signal caller in the National Football League. Overall, the No. 1 overall pick played well, completing multiple solid passes.
Mendoza took a few hits and kept going. He moved the ball down the field with more ease than any of the quarterbacks the Raiders trotted out onto the field last season. Mendoza's potential is there. He needs further development . Las Vegas must add more pieces around him, but he is trending upward.
Entering the offseason, there was competition among Las Vegas' group of wide receivers. Although that competition may still be going on, training camp and the first preseason game confirmed Bech's value and, more importantly, his role in Kubiak's offense moving forward.
Bech's role will be multifaceted, as Las Vegas continues to approach the receiver position by committee. Still, Bech accounted for multiple first-down catches on Thursday. He also did so many times last season. As the Raiders continue to build out their offense, Bech's value is clear.
Las Vegas largely played their reserve players on both offense and defense, with most of their starters only playing a drive or two. Both the Raiders' starters and reserves allowed the Cardinals to convert on third downs at a high rate. It is the first preseason game, so it is far too early to worry.
However, getting off the field is critical for every defense. It will be important for Las Vegas' defense as they continue to gel. The unit was solid on first and second down all game but allowed the Cardinals to convert all four of their third-down attempts in the first half.
The Raiders' first preseason game certainly looked like a team's first preseason game at several points. Both teams committed multiple pre-snap penalties, which is not uncommon for teams at this time of the season. This is especially true for a team with as many new pieces as the Raiders.
Heading into halftime, the Raiders had seven penalties for over 70 yards, most of them false starts on offense or untimely penalties on defense. If the Raiders can clean up the penalties, it is hard not to like what they showed on Thursday night.
Over the past few seasons, the Raiders have been inconsistent at best. Whether it was positive plays, which Las Vegas had several of on Thursday night, or negative plays, what Las Vegas showed on Thursday was consistent with what they have shown in training camp.
There were no surprises that took place for the Raiders on Thursday. After years of inconsistency and instability, Thursday night's exhibition game against the Cardinals was confirmation that what the Raiders have shown in camp is an accurate glimpse of what they will be in 2026. That in itself is a win.

title: Raider Nation Erupts Following Fernando Mendoza's Preseason Debut
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have produced a ton of hype throughout training camp, and Thursday night was the first test to see that in live action against an opposing NFL team.
It's officially football season, and fans of the Silver and Black have been waiting patiently to watch their team. That being said, we all know who the fans really wanted to see: No. 1 overall pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza . Here is how social media reacted to the rookie quarterback's Raiders debut against the Arizona Cardinals on Thursday night.
No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza makes his NFL debut with the Raiders 🏴‍☠️ pic.twitter.com/Q57JybQZp9
After Kirk Cousins led the starting offense on a 10-play, 68-yard drive, which concluded with a 13-yard touchdown pass to tight end Michael Mayer, Mendoza had plenty to live up to on his first drive and the Raiders' second offensive drive of the game.
Mendoza went 1-of-3, and Las Vegas' offense stalled after seven plays, but the rookie quarterback executed a third-down conversion with a nine-yard pass to Jack Bech.
Fernando Mendoza ➡️ Jack Bech 🔥 The 1st completion of Mendoza’s pre-season career. pic.twitter.com/MPpSFkvKfI
Overall, not the cleanest drive by the Raiders, but it was good to see Mendoza convert a long third down. His first pass attempt was a throwaway, as the pocket instantly collapsed at his feet, forcing him to throw the ball to the sidelines off his back foot.
Fernando Mendoza off to a rough start on his first drive (1/3 for 9 yards). https://t.co/XXTEWNt248 pic.twitter.com/WNd3Mby0ng
It didn't take long for Mendoza's connection with Malik Benson to shine through, as the future franchise quarterback ripped a 19-yard pass to the rookie receiver down the seam off play-action.
Fernando Mendoza is going to be ELITE pic.twitter.com/A8Qy33U9ut
(guys, i think fernando mendoza is going to be good. as a rookie.)
Following a 53-yard run by rookie running back Mike Washington Jr., Mendoza showed his mobility, picking up seven yards on a carry after being flushed out of the pocket.
Im sure the raiders dont want to see Fernando Mendoza running down the middle of the red zone in preseason pic.twitter.com/6x42v3zX6D
If Mendoza proved anything early on in his debut, it is that he can withstand adversity and bounce back when circumstances aren't ideal. The No. 1 overall pick took a sack after Washington Jr. converted on fourth down with a two-yard carry. Mendoza steadied the ship, completing a six-yard pass to the former Arkansas running back before finding Jack Bech for a six-yard touchdown.
Fernando mendoza is #good Nice touchdown
I fully realize it’s preseason, but Fernando Mendoza looks GOOD
Through Mendoza's first two drives, the rookie signal-caller completed 5-of-9 passes for 47 yards and one touchdown, while averaging 5.2 yards per attempt. It's clear that operating from under center is still a work in progress, but overall, it was a steady start for Mendoza.
Fernando Mendoza looks pretty good so far.  You can definitely tell he needs more time under center to be comfortable. He's obvious much better and quicker with his decisions when he's in the shotgun. Good day for Bech. Maybe Bech won't be a bust.
Fernando Mendoza is my quarterback for life.
As mentioned, Mendoza capped off his second drive as an NFL quarterback with a six-yard touchdown to Bech. It was a quick, decisive throw from the rookie, who didn't allow the defense to react. Once Bech found a pocket between two linebackers, Mendoza fired a low laser to protect the second-year receiver, which was an underrated component of this play.
As we said a week ago - If Fernando Mendoza aces his three tests (pre-season games), he'll start Week 1. Consider tonight "aced." Two to go.
The Future of the Las Vegas Raiders is bright. Fernando Mendoza is gonna be special. pic.twitter.com/gKMiYevMIF
It was unknown if Mendoza would take the field in the second half, but he was on the field when the offense returned after Arizona produced three points. The end of the first half was much sharper, as Mendoza went 1-of-2 for six yards and the Raiders went three-and-out. Mendoza held onto the ball too long on third down, taking an unnecessary hit in the process.
Fernando Mendoza is taking a lot of hits
Earlier this week, head coach Klint Kubiak said that Mendoza would get plenty of opportunities in his first preseason game, and he wasn't kidding. Mendoza went out for a fourth drive, and he was masterful, completing multiple impressive passes in the intermediate area of the field.

title: Malik Benson Continuing To Stand Out During Raiders' Training Camp
full_text:
So far, the Las Vegas Raiders have given their fans a lot to be excited about heading into the 2026 NFL season.
There have been several standout performances, but rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has been one of the most consistent players throughout training camp. While speaking with the media on Tuesday, Benson discussed his experiences with Kirk Cousins and his involvement with the first-team offense.
If there was one area on this roster that is a question mark heading into the upcoming season, it would be the wide receiver position. Jalen Nailor was the Raiders' top receiver acquisition this offseason and was the WR3 for the Minnesota Vikings over the last few seasons. Nailor joined a group of Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, and Dont'e Thornton Jr., who have all been in Las Vegas for one season.
Following free agency, the Raiders still had a glaring need at wide receiver, and while they didn't invest a top pick at the position, general manager John Spytek and the front office selected Benson in the sixth round of this year's draft.
At that point in the draft, most prospects are viewed as wild cards, but Benson has proven that he could be a consistent contributor in this offense. Las Vegas needs one or two wide receivers to step up alongside Brock Bowers, and Benson could be one of those guys.
The six-foot, 194-pound receiver has been utilized at all three levels of the field, and while he has been operating with the starting offense, Benson has also established chemistry with Fernando Mendoza.
Overall, Benson is making a significant impact every time he's on the field, and that consistency is why he is being featured with the starters. Don't be surprised if Benson makes plays throughout the season and establishes himself as a pivotal piece in the offense moving forward.

title: 5 Raiders I’m Excited To Watch Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders will kick off their preseason on Thursday night, hosting the Arizona Cardinals in the first action of a new era for the franchise.
First-year head coach Klint Kubiak said the starters will play this week , as the team will get a chance to evaluate the entire roster and see how several of their players do in live action for the first time since January. This is an intriguing group of players who have a chance to show their growth as the team continues through a rebuild under general manager John Spytek. With that in mind, here are five players I'm excited to watch this week.
My apologies for being cliché about this, but the "unofficial" debut of the Raiders' No. 1 overall draft pick is one of the most highly anticipated moments in recent franchise history. Mendoza has had a great camp, impressing coaches and observers with good ball security. Now, he'll face a different NFL defense than his own team's for the first time, as he'll likely work in with some of the starters, per Kubiak.
"He's [Mendoza] going to get plenty of experience in the game," Kubiak said. "Look forward to seeing him out there with his teammates. A lot of guys that we need to evaluate, but he'll get plenty of reps."
No matter how good or bad Mendoza plays this week, it will be fun to see just how much growth he has made since joining Las Vegas.
A rookie who has continued to stand out during camp, Masses has been wildly impressive for the growth he has made in training camp. Coverage versatility has always stood out, especially from his college days. The ball production was elite at Cal, and the Raiders hope to have more of the same flash during the preseason.
Technique and general consistency have always been an issue for Masses. I want to see what discipline and new techniques he has added to his skill set once he begins to trickle into the game.
There is a legitimate competition for the right-guard spot in Las Vegas, no matter who gets the nod for the slot on Thursday night. Caleb Rogers has begun to showcase the tools that made him an interesting middle-round draft selection, but Powers-Johnson is the one facing the most pressure heading into the preseason. He must showcase what made him a touted offensive lineman from Oregon to prove he is worthy of being the Week 1 starter.
A piece of news every Raiders fan had been waiting for all summer came true on Tuesday when Kubiak said the rookie fourth-round selection, McCoy, would play this week against the Cardinals, marking the first snaps for the former Tennessee Volunteer since the 2024 opening playoff round against Ohio State.
"I think Jermod [McCoy] has been practicing almost every day we've been out there, so we expect him to play," Kubiak said. "We expect him to compete and look forward to watching him play."
McCoy was arguably one of the top talents in the NFL Draft this spring, but concerns about a potential issue with a knee plug signaled red flags, causing him to tumble to the start of the fourth round. If he can stay healthy, this could be a major steal, making McCoy a future top team defender.
Hemingway is a player I'm buying the hype on early in camp. He has made major improvements from last season and enters his second year looking to be a better contributor in the trenches as a core depth talent in the middle of the defensive line. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard values Hemingway's inside-out versatility, so his deployment on Thursday could give us a glimpse of just how much he has grown this summer.

title: One Raiders’ Position Battle Isn’t As Close as Some Think
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders made wholesale roster changes across the board this offseason. Those changes led to increased competition at training camp, which will continue into the preseason and the 2026 season. Las Vegas' coaching staff has insisted that competition has taken place at every position.
The Raiders' front office added talent to essentially every position group on the roster, except tight end and punter, where they have two of the best players in the league at both positions. The roster additions have improved the Raiders, but there is still plenty to figure out.
Las Vegas recently released its depth chart ahead of its first preseason game. Thursday's exhibition matchup against the Arizona Cardinals will be the best look at Klint Kubiak's Raiders . They have a long way to go. They hope a new approach will lead to even more improvement.
Las Vegas plans to handle their wide receiver position by committee. The position will be handled largely by Jalen Nailor, Tre Tucker, and Jack Bech. Kubiak noted earlier this offseason that Bech is in competition with Dont'e Thornton and others, but Bech appears to be solidified on the depth chart.
Despite Kubiak's words, there is a decent gap between Bech and Thornton that was not there last season. While there is increased competition at the position, that competition comes from the group as a whole, more than from Thornton specifically.
Rookie wide receiver Malik Benson was drafted in the seventh round of this year's NFL Draft. He has already begun making more of an impact at receiver than many expected on draft night. He is also making that impact sooner than most would have expected.
Many players have had a strong training camp, only to fall by the wayside during the regular season, but Las Vegas' need at receiver and more productive practices will lead to more opportunities for Benson. Raiders wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni recently gave insight into Benson's development.
"Malik’s doing a good job. I'm pleased with his improvement, his progress. Long way to go. He's still a rookie, makes those rookie mistakes. But I'm pleased with his effort, his attitude. He's extremely coachable,” Azzanni said following training camp.
“He's tough. You do that, you got a chance. And he's improving every day, which is what I want to see. Slight improvement, steady, a little bit every day, and he's been doing that. So, I'm pleased with where he's currently at."
Las Vegas' group of wide receivers features several players who could push for playing time at some point this season. The Raiders will handle the position by committee, giving any and every receiver on the roster a chance to secure a roster spot and playing time.
If Benson can shoot up the depth chart, any of the other wide receivers can too. This should encourage and motivate the likes of Thornton and any other receiver moving forward. Azzanni believes Thornton has responded well to his ups and downs on the field.
"Same thing with Dont'e. I always tell our room that the tape is our resume, let the tape be our guide. So, all of those guys, if they have a down day, they got to come back and have a better day. We just press play. We evaluate it every day. He's had a couple rough days and he's bounced back and had some good plays here and there,” Azzanni said.
"And that's what we're looking for in training camp, we're installing all this stuff. Everything's not going to be perfect, but I am pleased he's got a great attitude. He's working his tail off. I saw some improvement today, which was good. We go day by day in training camp, so he's coming along like the rest of them."
With the Raiders aiming to supply their offense with as many capable pass catchers as possible, they will likely hold on to as many receivers as make sense. This should buy time for Thornton and others who hope to progress to develop further.
However, Las Vegas is sure to continue revamping the position group over the next few seasons. Time will tell how patient the front office and coaching staff will be with a group of receivers that is largely replaceable. The receivers currently on the roster must make the most of their opportunity.

title: Raiders Training Camp Report 16: Evolving Expectations Emerge
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—Today marks Day 16 of the Las Vegas Raiders' full-team training camp, and expectations are high as the team prepares for its first preseason game of the year tomorrow night at Allegiant Stadium.
Klint Kubiak, while a rookie head coach, has shown none of the rookie head coaching mistakes so far by running a considerably efficient and tight camp, with enormous credit going to his staff, young and old, and the fact that he has been born into the NFL and it has been the totality of his life.
Today will be my final update before the preseason game, and I want to do a deep dive into what is setting this camp apart and what you can really learn from the first preseason game.
On a team with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, with NFL executives swooning over Fernando Mendoza, you would not have expected so much attention to go to so many other rookies.
Perception would be wrong. While Mendoza has looked terrific, credit John Spytek and his staff of Brian Stark, Brandon Hunt, and Brandon Yeargan, and their respective staffs, for assembling a fantastic rookie class.
The youngster Hezekiah Masses, CB, appears to be a fifth-round steal as he makes plays every single day all over the field. The biggest criticism of his game coming into the NFL was his lack of physicality on tape. It was a fair criticism, but it didn’t mean he couldn’t do it. He wasn’t asked to. He is now making those criticisms look foolish. I asked him about his impressive physical nature and that criticism.
"Oh, yeah, I'm trying to take their head off. Yeah, that was a big issue, they said I can't tackle, so I'm going to show them. I'm going to show them very physical. I can do everything."
Once, while interviewing Michael Jordan, I asked him about when he performed at his highest level, about being in the zone, and what that was like. He told me, “Like the rim is 10 feet around, not high.” I have never forgotten that, and right now, Masses is playing in that proverbial zone, in my perception. I asked him.
“I'm in that zone for sure, just 100%. I'm just out there just making plays and just being myself. They calling great calls, and I'm just out there executing."
Masses has been terrific and will clearly have an impact on the Raiders' 2026 season. But don’t say that too loud; he still thinks he is on the bubble and said he has his focus on making the 53-man roster. Hey, Hezekiah, you have.
“A goal for me is just make the 53-man roster, and then just be the best version of myself, be the best teammate I could be, and then just whatever I can do to contribute to help us win. That's what I'm going to do."
When Hezekiah speaks, the appreciation of being an NFL player exudes from him. You can see it every moment, every rep; he wants more, he will do more, and he loves the moments. While fans and many veterans even bemoan preseason games, Masses isn’t one of them.
He knows that it is special to play in the NFL, and since he was little, being in this league has been his dream. When you listen to him talk about Thursday night’s preseason tilt with Arizona, he makes it sound like a Super Bowl. It most certainly is for the young man who dreamed of being an NFL player. It was refreshing.
"Yeah, I'm just super excited, man. It feels so unreal, man. My first preseason game. I'm just happy for the opportunity. I'm just ready to play on Thursday."
Coming into the 2026 NFL Draft, Jermod McCoy was considered by most as the best CB in the draft. Concerns about a potential issue with a knee plug saw him plunge to the top of the fourth round. That plunge conceivably cost him $40 million. But he isn’t bitter; he is motivated, and credits the Raiders staff for having him in tip-top shape.
“I think it's been a great process with them. From the day I came in to now, the way I feel is so much better. AG [Alex Guerrero], all the guys in there, I feel like they just really been pouring into me. I mean, they got me right."
Malik Benson, the WR the Raiders somehow managed to snare in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has not been good; he has been sensational in his first NFL training camp. The coaches love him, and McCoy loves the chance to compete with him.
"Oh, it's been good. Me and Malik [Benson], man, every time I'm up against Malik, I love it because they love throwing to Malik. So, I know when I'm against Malik, the ball's probably coming there. So, I'm going to try to make a play."
The Raiders have been terrible on defense, creating and getting turnovers. But in adding new players, they have brought in ball hawks. Men who see the ball and get it. Something Jermod McCoy is known for, and he thinks he and the “Leonard Doctrine” are tailor-made for each other.
"I'm always trying to get the ball back, make plays on the ball. I mean, we want the offense on the field as much as possible to put points on the board. So, whatever we can do to get the ball back and help the team do that, that's what we're going to do."
McCoy missed his entire 2025 season after his preseason knee injury. While incredibly gifted, he doesn’t take the game for granted. This is a game he loves. Like Masses earlier, getting back on the field Thursday night is going to be emotional for him. Not only achieving his dream of playing in the NFL, but also being back on the football field for a game, something he loves.
"For sure, there's definitely going to be some emotions."
McCoy has seen the success of fellow rookie CB Masses and thinks the two are helping each other, which is exactly what Spytek wanted in selecting four DBs in the 2026 NFL Draft. A decision that appears to be paying off, per McCoy.
“Me and Zeke [Hezekiah Masses], we talk a lot about stuff that we see, try to coach each other up on things. I feel like we're really similar with our mindsets. We both want to be the best. So, I mean, I think two rookies coming in and doing that, it's something. It's hard to find that for real, I think."
No matter who you talk to on this team, the appreciation for Klint Kubiak’s commitment to detail has them raving about the Silver and Black first-year head coach. Something rookie Trey Zuhn III echoes.
"I love working with him. He's extremely detailed. He expects the most out of us every single day, day in, day out. So, he's definitely taking this team where it needs to go."
Zuhn, the top OL in the SEC last year, dug into the adjustment from the country's second-best conference (SEC) to the NFL and why he loves the challenge.
"Yeah, it's just more detailed. The competition's so much better; it's the best of the best. So, you can't be half a step wrong. You have to know the playbook like the back of your hand, and you have to study your teammates like they're an opponent every single day so you have a step on them. So, I've enjoyed it."
In the MLB, a five-tool player has mastery-level ability in the five core critical skills of playing baseball. Zuhn can play all five offensive line positions in the NFL, and does so seamlessly from one rep to the next. His football IQ is enormous, and when he does get a break, I often see him talking to Tyler Linderbaum, the Raiders' C and a generational talent, and Kolton Miller, one of the top-five LTs in the NFL. So what is it like as a young rookie having those two resources to draw from? I asked him.
"Right, those are amazing resources. So, I want to talk to them all I can. I just want to learn from them because they've been in the league, they know how it goes, they know football. So, whatever I can learn from them to help the team, I want to learn."
Switching from one play to another, or one series to another at a different position, wouldn’t be easy for anyone. Zuhn’s football acumen is off the charts, and he let us into his mental process for dealing with and playing so many different spots.
"Whenever I'm going in for a series and I'm at a certain position, I just have to lock in and be at that position. Because I've learned the playbook from a whole, so I know what everybody's…

title: Spytek, Raiders Add Offensive Lineman: What It Means
full_text:
With their first preseason game of the season quickly approaching on Thursday, the Las Vegas Raiders made another addition to their offensive line Wednesday. The Raiders made the addition while they are still in the process of solidifying the depth chart along their offensive line.
Las Vegas completed training camp on Tuesday evening at Allegiant Stadium, then signed offensive lineman Braeden Daniels. The fourth-year offensive lineman has spent time with several practice squads around the league, including the Dallas Cowboys and, most recently, the Miami Dolphins.
Daniels will be a depth piece on Las Vegas' offensive line, as their front office continues to make changes to the unit. The Raiders will take the next few weeks of preseason practices and games to sort things out.
In a corresponding move, the Raiders waived/injured offensive guard Justin Pickett. The Raiders' front office continues to make moves they believe will improve the roster overall, regardless of how big or small those moves may be.
The addition of Daniels to a position group that Las Vegas is still figuring out shows they are serious about revamping every level of their depth chart. Daniels' addition is likely not a big move, but it should send somewhat of a message to the players that the front office notices everything.
The addition of Daniels should also be a reminder that it will take longer than just this offseason to truly fix Las Vegas' most pressing issue. When healthy, the Raiders' offensive line is better than it was last season, but the starters need further development in a new system, and the unit still needs depth.
Raiders offensive line coach Rick Dennison recently explained where the Raiders' offensive line stands, noting that although some positions have been solidified, players on each level of the offensive line's depth chart are still competing.
“They're all trying to be the best they can be for the team, whatever role they are. I think that's the big thing. It's a big 'we' in our meeting room,” Dennison said following training camp.
“They all talk about we watch individual, we watch team, I correct them, they talk to each other, and the leaders like Kolton [Miller], he'll say, 'This is what I would have done. You should think about this.' So, those guys have shared information. I think they're just trying to get the best team out there."
After an offseason filled with big swings that added much-needed talent, there is not much more the Raiders' front office can do to improve the roster this offseason. Still, they continue to look for ways to improve at every turn, as they look to establish a firm offensive identity under Klint Kubiak.
The Raiders have improved the coaching along their offensive line and look to continue adding talent when possible this offseason and beyond. Dennison elaborated, noting that he and the coaching staff are doing all they can to help build a cohesive offensive line.
“I don't think we have anybody in the room that doesn't want to be pushed. That's why they're here. If they were that way, they probably wouldn't be here, right? So I don't know if I'm tough or not, I'm just me. I tell them all the time, I'm going to be mad at you if you make a mistake. If you make it twice, I'm really going to be mad,” Dennison said.
“But it's important that they know that their jobs are essential for all 11 to do right. It's not just one guy. All 11 got to do something right. So, we can't just say we're successful because one guy did it right. We've all got to work together, that's why the five of them have got to work hard."

title: Raiders Round Out Training Camp, Prepare To Move Forward
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders held their final training camp practice of the 2026 season at Allegiant Stadium on Tuesday night. The Raiders opened the stadium to fans to showcase the progress made on the field after a number of solid roster moves.
The Raiders hope to be consistently competitive sooner rather than later. Below are a few notes from Las Vegas' 11th and final training camp practice of the season. The Raiders are two days away from their first exhibition game under head coach Klint Kubiak.
The Raiders took the field at Allegiant Tuesday evening in front of Raiders fans. It was an affordable opportunity for fans to connect with a largely new-look roster that the Raiders will debut this season. Tuesday was another step closer to a season that has begun garnering cautious optimism.
It was an unpadded practice for Las Vegas, yet they showed enough to give an idea of what to expect moving forward. It also gave the Raiders a chance to get some work done on their home field, which differs from the practice fields at the team's headquarters.
“Tonight's really important. Really excited about going and being in front of our fans, being on the grass that we're going to play on. Coaches communicating with the headsets; really important for the whole operation,” Kubiak said earlier on Tuesday before practice.
“Obviously, it's my first game in there. Played a few games on the other side of the stadium, but it'll be really important for players and coaches to get familiar with our surroundings so that we can play our best football on Thursday night."
With Tuesday's practice out of the way, Las Vegas will take Wednesday off before returning to Allegiant Stadium for their first preseason game on Thursday to face the Arizona Cardinals.
Las Vegas is implementing a whole new offensive and defensive scheme, with a new head coach, coordinators, and players at critical positions. They have practiced against each other enough. They need additional work against a different team to truly improve. Kubiak explained his plan for Thursday.
"We do have a plan for those guys and how many snaps or series we'd like to see them go. No need for everyone else to know it, but we're going to have a lot of guys playing this game. We need to evaluate the whole roster,” Kubiak said ahead of Tuesday night's open practice.
"I think it's really important that our guys have the same attitude we've asked them to have all camp – have a team-first attitude and have shocking effort. That's what we're looking for, looking for competitive guys. And one thing that we've really stressed is, especially for our young guys, of using special teams as their avenue to make the team. So, we're going to be evaluating those reps very critically."
Kubiak has made it clear that Las Vegas' starters will play against the Cardinals. Regardless of how much they do or do not play, it is fair to assume that progress will be made. The Raiders have about another month's worth of practices and preseason games before the first regular-season game.
The Raiders will now enter the preseason looking to take the next step in their progression under Kubiak ahead of his first regular season as a head coach. Progress has been made, but even Kubiak would agree that much more must be done in the next few weeks before they face the Miami Dolphins.
It must be remembered that much of the progress the Raiders and other teams hope to make cannot be made until everything is going at full speed. That means it will likely take a few weeks into the regular season to get an idea of what the Raiders will be this season.
Based on what they showed during training camp, it is fair to expect they will be better than in the past two seasons. That is, assuming they stay relatively healthy. Kubiak's coaching staff has begun changing the culture in Las Vegas. They hope additional wins will follow.

title: Another Reason to Push Back Against Dolphins Doom and Gloom Predictions
full_text:
In case you haven't heard by now, the Miami Dolphins aren't expecting to be very good in 2026.
That's the consensus from power rankings, over/under totals, position group rankings and commentary from around the nation. Even Troy Aikman, who remains a consultant with the Dolphins, said as much this week during a Dallas radio interview when he pointed out he won't be calling any Miami games on Monday Night Football this year because "The Dolphins are not expected to be very good this year."
The major reasons the Dolphins are expected to suffer in 2026 include all that dead cap space, the loss of so many high-profile players, and the unusually large number of rookies expected to either start or play a considerable role.
It's clearly a rebuilding project not unlike that of 2019 in Brian Flores' first year as head coach.
The Dolphins used a lot of rookies that season, and they're expected to do the same in 2026, but there's a big difference.
Not every rookie is created equal.
The 2019 Dolphins wound up having 13 rookies start at least one game that season, with a combined total of 76 starts.
Three rookies started at least half the games: defensive tackle Christian Wilkins, guard Michael Deiter and cornerback Nick Needham.
The Dolphins had five rookies listed on the first team on the team's first depth chart of 2026 if we include linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who was part of an either/or listing with Tyrel Dodson at one of the linebacker spots.
The others were Kadyn Proctor, Caleb Douglas, Trey Moore and Chris Johnson.
Other Dolphins rookies who very well might end up starting a game or two (or three or more) at some point in 2026 would have to include tight end Will Kacmarek, wide receiver Chris Bell, maybe linebacker Kyle Louis, maybe wide receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. and maybe safety Michael Taaffe.
The likelihood that the number of rookie starts in 2026 exceeds that 76 mark is pretty good, and those starts have a good chance of being a lot more impactful.
Here's the stat that really stands out:
Of the 13 rookies who made starts for the Dolphins in 2019, only four of them were draft picks and only two were selected before the fifth rounds (Christian Wilkins and Michael Deiter).
The 2026 Dolphins, meanwhile, had eight draft picks in the first four rounds — Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez, Caleb Douglas, Will Kacmarek, Chris Bell, Trey Moore and Kyle Louis.
The likelihood is those players have greater future potential than the nine rookie free agents who started games seven years ago and also likely will perform better as rookies.
Also don't forget that the 2019 Dolphins went 5-4 in their final nine games after gaining some footing under Flores with a team that was so heavy on unheralded rookies.
The 2026 Dolphins are much more likely to be able to begin the season as a cohesive unit because of all the high draft picks and a much clearer quarterback situation, where Malik Willis is the guy this season while the Dolphins bounced between Ryan Fitzpatrick and Josh Rosen early in 2019 before Flores decided he had seen enough of Rosen.
We're not suggesting with this analysis that the Dolphins are ready for a 10-win season because there are still too many holes on the roster and the depth is borderline nonexistent, but their season also might not be the unmitigated disaster so many are projecting.

title: What to Know About and How to Watch the Miami Dolphins Preseason
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' 2026 preseason schedule kicks off Friday night against the Washington Commanders before coming back to South Florida for the rest of the preseason.
The game against Washington will be televised live in the South Florida and Washington markets, and replayed on NFL Network on Tuesday at noon ET.
The Dolphins will have one live national television preseason, that one scheduled for Saturday, August 22 against the New York Giants at Hard Rock Stadium at 4 p.m. ET. That game will come two days after the teams conduct a joint practice.
The preseason finale will be Friday, August 28 against the Atlanta Falcons at Hard Rock Stadium at 7 p.m. ET. That game will be replayed on NFL Network.
By comparison, the Dolphins had two preseason games on live national TV last year, against the Chicago Bears and the Jacksonville Jaguars.
The Dolphins finished 2-0-1 in the preseason last year, tying with the Bears before defeating the Lions and Jaguars.
The Dolphins are 10-5 all time against the Commanders in the preseason and will be meeting for the second time in three years. Miami won 13-6 in 2024 after the teams conducted a joint practice before, just like the teams did this year. Washington is looking to rebound from a 5-12 season that followed their surprising run to the NFC Championship Game in that 2024 season, and feature some noteworthy newcomers, including former Dolphins cornerback Rasul Douglas.
The Dolphins have a perfect 7-0 preseason record against the Giants, though the teams haven't faced each other since 2016. The big story with New York in 2026 was the start of a new era under head coach John Harbaugh, who was hired after his long tenure with the Baltimore Ravens came to an end. The newcomer to watch just might be first-round pick Francis Mauigoa, the guard from the University of Miami who was considered a potential Dolphins target before he was selected 10th overall.
The matchup with the Falcons will be the teams' 22nd in the preseason, making Atlanta the second-most common opponent behind only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (which obviously makes geographical sense).
The Dolphins are 12-9 against Atlanta in the preseason, including a 20-13 victory at Hard Rock Stadium in the last meeting in 2024.
The big story in this matchup revolves around quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and whether he will play at the stadium he called home the past six years. Tagovailoa is battling for the starting quarterback position with incument Michael Penix Jr., who has yet to receive full medical clearance coming back from a knee injury.
Along with Tagovailoa, former Dolphins players currently on the Atlanta roster include punter Jake Bailey, defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand and linebacker Channing Tindall.

title: Willis (Yes) Headlines 10 Players to Watch in 2026 Dolphins Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will open their preseason schedule against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on Friday night in new head coach Jeff Hafley's first game, and as always the final score won't be nearly as significant as the individual performances we'll witness.
While Hafley hasn't said definitively his starters will play in the game, the feeling remains that anybody not dealing with some sort of an injury likely will some see action against the Commanders, even if it's only a matter of single-digit snaps.
Those who will get extensive action either will be trying to offer more evidence they should be on the 2026 team or at the very least get a bigger role on offense or defense.
With that in mind, here is our list of 10 players to watch in that preseason opener against the Commanders:
Yes, we have to start with Malik Willis, who we strongly suspect will get a series or two depending on how many plays that first drive lasts. Willis has looked the part during training camp, even if the results haven't always been there for the first-team offense. This will be simply another step toward getting Willis ready for his all-important first season as a full-time starter.
While Willis has been solid in camp, Ewers quite frankly has had a disappointing summer. And Hafley and the Dolphins would feel a whole lot better about their backup quarterback situation with a strong outing here. If Ewers struggled, we might be looking sooner rather than later at the Dolphins starting to consider other backup options.
There are a lot of reasons to be excited about Douglas' performances in training camp and the next step is carrying that kind of work into preseason games. Douglas already looks like the lead wide receiver in a questionable group, and another good outing here would make his stock soar even more.
If Douglas has stood out at wide receiver, it's partly because the rest of the group has been pretty nondescript or even disappointing. In his homecoming, the former Miami high school star has yet to make much of an impact, to the point where his spot on the 53-man roster shouldn't be taken for granted at this time. Atwell can change pretty quickly with a strong preseason outing.
It would be tempting to go with the easy choice here of first-round pick Kadyn Proctor, but the biggest question mark on the starting offensive line isn't Proctor, it's Savaiinaea. His teammates have sung his praises consistently since the start of training camp, but now it's time to show the desired improvement in game settings.
Yes, this is where we've got to start on defense because the Dolphins need their 2025 first-round pick to step up in his second season, and Zach Sieler's injury absence makes that even more important. Grant hasn't really stood out so far in training camp; this would be a good time to start making that happen.
Robinson has been borderline dominant throughout training camp and by all accounts had another strong showing in the joint practice in Virginia, and a good preseason opener could be the final step in setting the stage for a breakout season.
Our second rookie draft pick on this list, Rodriguez really has come on since the early days of training camp, showing the same knack for being around the ball he showed during his days at Texas Tech. Preseason games is the next step.
While he came up with a great play toward the end of the joint practice, Taaffe has had a pretty low-key training camp, but he has a chance to play himself into a bigger role with the injuries to fellow safeties Dante Trader Jr. and Lonnie Johnson Jr.
While he was listed first on the depth chart and appears to have the inside track on a starting job at safety, Anderson's career resume is as a special-teamer and reports indicate the safety play was less than ideal in the joint practice Wednesday. Anderson needs to be trending up over the couple of weeks if he wants to cement that starting job instead of the Dolphins scouring the waiver wire for another safety option.

title: How Miami Dolphins Rookie Trey Moore Climbed on the Depth Chart (And What Are Fair Expectations for 2026)
full_text:
On the first depth chart of the 2026 season for the Miami Dolphins, one name stands out on defense: Trey Moore. Miami's 130th overall pick in the fourth round out of Texas is listed as a first-string inside linebacker.
Aside from Moore, Jordyn Brooks unsurprisingly gets the nod, with the final linebacker spot being designated to either Tyrel Dodson or Jacob Rodriguez. Yes, three separate inside linebackers are being listed in an official depth chart.
Never take a preseason depth chart too seriously when it comes to determining who's starting in Week 1. However, Moore has come a long way during training camp to prove to Jeff Hafley and Miami's coaching staff that he's earned a starting spot.
Moore has had a standout camp, putting in a lot of work with the first unit. Hafley believes there's a lot of potential with Moore right away, being the Swiss Army Knife of the linebacker unit. For a Hafley-led hybrid defense that likes to use the nickel, that's a very important trait to have.
"He's done a really good job setting the edge," Hafley said. "He can play inside linebacker, he can play outside linebacker at Sam (strong side), and then he's got the ability to rush. He gives you a linebacker who can play all three downs. He can play in zones. He's good against the run, and he's got rush value. So we'll see where he's at. But I like the way he's practiced."
Hafley noted his play at inside linebacker, but Moore's bread and butter in college was setting the edge. His best highlights with UTSA and Texas positioned him on the far left and right sides of the line, where he showcased his athleticism, spinning past linemen with excellent footwork and a deep bag of moves to pull from.
However, Hafley has looked to Moore's versatility as a linebacker as his best trait during training camp. With Texas, he expanded what he can do on the field aside from just pass rush. He had success countering the running game in the middle of the field. He wasn't afraid to spy on the offense and could handle man coverage pretty well.
Getting to the quarterback was his best attribute, and Miami will want him to replicate his success in college. Moore recorded 30.5 sacks for the Roadrunners and Longhorns, the fifth-most of any player in FBS this decade. This was against competition at both the Group of Five and power conference level.
Moore's draft profile highlights his instincts and reliability as key traits, with 46 starts at college. His overall speed and 6-1, 243-pound frame were knocks, though Moore is listed at 6-2 on the Dolphins' website.
The Dolphins have been all in on his skill set since the moment they drafted him. This preseason can determine where Miami will want to primarily keep him on the field, likely between Sam and Will, but his versatility will be put to the test against NFL-caliber offenses ahead of the regular season.
If Moore does well enough in the preseason to remain a starter on defense, then the possibilities are intriguing when it comes to what he could do in the regular season. Assuming he stays healthy (he never suffered a serious injury in college), he can make double-digit starts this season, likely around the 10-12 area.
Sack-wise, it'll depend on whether the Dolphins mainly keep him on the edge. If that's the case, around three to four sacks are possible for him against some of the weaker offensive lines Miami will face, including Las Vegas, Green Bay, and the New York Jets.
Don't expect interceptions from Moore, as that wasn't his specialty in college. If the Dolphins play him at the Will (weakside linebacker) sporadically, he likely won't get many opportunities. What's more possible are forced fumbles, which he occasionally caused via strip sacks or ripping the ball away from running backs. If he gets one or two of those, that should be considered a massive success.

title: Examining Minkah's Miami Comments ... and Other Former Dolphins Updates
full_text:
Minkah Fitzpatrick got into the Dolphins record books this offseason when he tied the franchise mark in being traded away for a second time, but the circumstances were much different this time.
The four-time Pro Bowl safety and 2018 Dolphins draft pick acknowledged the well-accepted idea that he wanted out the first time around, though he specified the real reason during an appearance on The Pivot podcast with Channing Crowder, Ryan Clark and Fred Taylor.
And while previous speculation was that Fitzpatrick wanted out in 2019 because he didn't like then-head coach Brian Flores or the way he was going to be utilized, Fitzpatrick said the reason was much simpler.
"I saw what they were doing that season, and that's why I wanted out, you know what I'm saying?" Firtzpatrick said with a smirk. "Yeah, I knew what was going on. That's why I left that first time."
What the Dolphins did in 2019 was flush out most of their high-profile veterans and clear out cap space in a full rebuilding project that many analysts instead have referred to as a "tanking job."
Of course, this is where many would point out that the Dolphins are doing a lot of the same things in 2026 by jettisoning Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle, Bradley Chubb and, yes, Fitzpatrick, but there's one significant difference.
That difference is the Dolphins signing Malik Willis as a potential franchise quarterback, whereas in 2019 they brought in veteran Ryan Fitzpatrick at the end of his career and traded for Josh Rosen one year after he was the 10th overall selection and flopped as a rookie.
The 2026 Dolphins also have 13 rookie draft picks, to go along with an eight-player class from just a year ago, compared to only six picks in the 2019 draft.
The ironic part about Fitzpatrick's comment regarding his trade request is that Flores so vehemently rejected the notion of the Dolphins tanking in 2019 whenever the notion was brought up — and his not playing the clearly ill-equipped Rosen the whole season instead of Fitzpatrick certainly suggests he indeed was trying to win games.
This season, as in 2019, the Dolphins could use Fitzpatrick in the secondary but instead traded him away. In doing so, they made him the second player the team traded twice, along with long-ago quarterback John Stofa, traded to the Cincinnati Bengals and Denver Broncos sandwiched around signing with Miami as a free agent.
Fitzpatrick, now a member of the New York Jets, is one trade away from tying the NFL record currently held by wide receiver Brandin Cooks and Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson.
When they re-acquired him from the Pittsburgh Steelers last summer, the Dolphins adjusted his contract to lower his cap number with everyone fully aware he'd want a new contract this year.
The Dolphins weren't willing to pay him big money, which made sense considering where the organization is at this time, so they put him on the trade market and ultimately the best they could was land a seventh-round pick for him.
Keeping up with former members of the organization:
-- The Detroit Lions finally officially announced the hiring of former GM Chris Grier as a personnel advisor. Grier often was the target of fan displeasure during his tenure in Miami, which spanned from 2000 until he was fired on Halloween of last year, including nine years as general manager.
-- Former Dolphins backup QB Skylar Thompson's run of bad luck continues. The Baltimore Ravens placed him on injured reserve Wednesday, essentially ending his season or at least his time with Baltimore. This comes after Thompson spent the entire 2025 season on IR with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who he joined after leaving the Dolphins.

title: With DT Zach Sieler Set to Miss Time, Time to Step Up for Former Dolphins First-Round Pick
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins’ defense is trying to build itself from the ground up. Head coach Jeff Hafley has talked a lot this offseason about wanting players to take steps forward, and what he needs from each player as they try to identify their core players for the foreseeable future.
Unfortunately, in the NFL injuries are the rule not the exception. Now defensive tackle Zach Sieler is going to miss some time with an injury that is undisclosed as of this point.
Sieler will miss the Dolphins’ preseason opener against the Washington Commanders on Friday night. The hope is that Sieler will be ready for the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders, but it’s not clear whether Sieler will be ready after Hafley called his status "week to week."
In the meantime, however, the popular phrase whenever a player is injured is next man up. Sieler’s shoes are not easy to fill. He’s been very productive during his career in Miami with 25.5 sacks coming in his last three seasons with the club.
With Sieler out of the lineup, there’s a big man who needs to make a big jump into a productive role.
The NFL draft is the lifeblood of almost every franchise in the NFL. Teams are often at their best when they draft guys, develop them under their rookie contracts, and sign them to extensions.
That’s the approach that GM Jon-Eric Sullivan has been used to during his time in Green Bay, and is hoping to have it carry over as he takes over as the head man in Miami. This offseason alone he’s handed out contract extensions to core players like Aaron Brewer, De’Von Achane and Jordyn Brooks.
Sullivan only has one draft class under his belt, but he and the coaching staff still have to work with what was given to them by their predecessors.
One of those picks was 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant. Grant was picked to be one of the anchors of Miami’s defensive line after a productive career at Michigan that saw him paired with fellow first-round pick Mason Graham.
Grant was part of a defensive line that spearheaded the Wolverines defense into a national championship-winning unit.
Grant was picked 13th overall over players like Emeka Egbuka, Tyler Warren, and Jaxson Dart.
Fair or not, that’s how any drafted player ends up being looked at. If a player does not turn into a consistent contributor, they’re going to be compared to players who are.
In fairness to Grant, he is now a second-year player, and defensive tackles typically take a year to develop as they try and get acclimated to the NFL game.
Grant’s first season saw him sack the quarterback twice with 29 pressures, which ranked 40th out of 134 defensive linemen. In addition he had 23 hurries and 20 run stops according to PFF.
That’s not a terrible rookie season by any measure, but the Dolphins are going to need more from a top-15 pick.
That was true regardless of whether Sieler was in the lineup or not. Now that he is set to miss some time, there is a big red circle around Grant. That’s true of both the Dolphins’ coaching staff and those who are set to face off against them.
To Grant’s credit, he’s done his part this season. He told Miami reporters in July that his goal for his playing weight will be 325 pounds, which is down from the 337 he played at a season ago.
The goal would be to become more explosive so he can make more plays in the passing game like Sieler did in 2023 and 2024.
When a player like Sieler is set to miss time, the onus is going to be on everyone to step up. Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips will likely need to take on bigger roles as well.
With all due respect to those guys, however, they were not drafted in the first round.
Fictional character Ben Parker once said with great power comes great responsibility. The great power, in this case, is Grant’s draft status.
Now, comes the responsibility to live up to the billing while Sieler is out of the lineup, and maintain that momentum once he returns.

title: Projecting Dolphins RB De'Von Achane's Touches in Light of Coach's Comments
full_text:
Miami Dolphins Head Coach Jeff Hafley made a joking statement about one of the team’s best players, but what does it mean for his potential workload?
In an interview Monday with Rich Eisen, Hafley laughingly said that he told star running back De’Von Achane that he could see an unheard-of workload next season.
"I just gave Achane a heads-up this morning and I told him, 'You better be in good shape... After you touch the ball 40, 45 times, I might have to pick you up, and I'll carry you back into the locker room.’”
Quite frankly, 40 touches is an absurd number. Achane’s career high in touches per game is only 29, and dating back to his college career, his personal record is still just 38, which he tallied in his final game at Texas A&M.
To find the last 40-touch game in the NFL, you have to go back to 2021, where Derrick Henry, a listed 57 pounds heavier than Achane, received 41 with the Titans.
So, knowing that 40 touches is a pipe dream, while also understanding that Achane’s workload likely will increase in the post-Tyreek Hill era after receiving a new contract extension, what’s the magic number?
De’Von Achane averaged 19.1 touches per game last season, a career high for the three-year pro. Meanwhile, the NFL’s leader, Christian McCaffrey, averaged 24.3. McCaffrey is an outlier in recent NFL history, however, as he’s the only player in the last eight seasons to record 400 or more touches in a single season (he’s done it twice in that span). Second-place Jonathan Taylor had 369 in 2025, while Achane had 305.
A more realistic target for Achane (assuming an increase) is somewhere between 20 and 22 touches per game. The league leader in yards per carry in 2025, Achane finished only 14th in total carries, with 238 — 14 more (about one more carry per game) would have gotten him into the top 10, and 32 more (two per game since he played 16 last season) would have tied him for sixth.
As for Achane’s receiving workload, it seems that a change would be in the quality of targets, rather than the quantity. He finished tied for fifth in running back targets, but had a negative air yards per target, per NFL Pro. With a young and unproven receiving group, it wouldn’t be surprising to see more opportunities out wide and farther down the field.
A projection for Achane, given this information, would be somewhere in the 320 to 340 touch range, which would have placed him between fifth and seventh among the NFL in 2025.
Achane certainly will be the focal point of the Dolphins' offense in 2026. However, a healthy workload, more than anything, will be the key to keeping the 195-pound back upright throughout his extension. Jeff Hafley will be looking to get him the ball often, but finding the sweet spot will be crucial.

title: How Tolbert Can Turn the Back the Clock In Miami ... And Earn a Big Role in the Process
full_text:
After signing with the Miami Dolphins on March 16, Jalen Tolbert finds himself in uncharted territory in his NFL career.
After spending four seasons in Dallas, Tolbert will want (and, for Miami's sake, need) to double as a leader for a young, inexperienced wide receiver corps, alongside providing production that harkens back to his 2024 season.
Where there's a new system, there's a new opportunity. Tolbert spoke about this and plenty more to media after practice on Monday, highlighting the challenges and expectations he has for the 2026 season.
Tolbert is staying positive despite the circumstances. Two seasons ago, he was the right-hand man to CeeDee Lamb, starting in 15 games while racking up 49 receptions for 610 yards and seven touchdowns, all of which were career highs.
Tolbert still believes he can reach those heights once more in Miami, with an added task of being a natural leader for the receiver corps.
"I know what I'm capable of," Tolbert said. "I know what I can do to help this team, and I know what I can do in this league. I'm earning my opportunities, some points of attack on the menu, and helping take this team to another level, being a leader for those guys in the room. Obviously, we're a young team, young room. I think that's one of my goals for this year."
It's a young room, and to Tolbert's point, he stands out age-wise. He's tied for the oldest receiver on the team at 27 years old, alongside fellow offseason acquisition Jalen Reagor. The unit features four rookies alongside multiple pass-catchers looking for their first breakout season.
Tolbert's skill set was not entirely why he had a down year in 2025. What killed his playing time was the Cowboys' acquisition of George Pickens, alongside breakout seasons for Jake Ferguson and Ryan Flournoy, which moved Tolbert down the depth chart. He started only eight games in 2025 and did not play in four of the last six games of the season.
Now, Tolbert will look to solidify himself as a day one starter for Miami. Drafted just two picks after Malik Willis in the third round of the 2022 draft (86th overall to 88th overall), Tolbert has made it a priority to build chemistry with his former teammate in the Senior Bowl.
"It's important to build that trust from your quarterback," Tolbert said. "So he trusts that you're going to be where you need to be, when you need to be there, and what he's looking for in certain routes. To talk through the tiny parts of the game means a lot, and the second part that I think is overlooked is just being able to understand each other."
Being on the same page when it comes to routes might be key for Tolbert to silence doubts about his route-running ability. Changing direction mid-play might be his biggest weakness as a receiver, as building separation from defenders has been difficult for him at times.
This con, however, has highlighted one of his best pros: contested catching. Standing at 6-1 with a 36-inch vertical jump, Tolbert can excel at making plays happen in a crowd. In addition to his speed, this made him a reliable option when running go routes or out routes, and an occasional deep threat when he can fly past the secondary.
Going back to 2024 isn't enough for Tolbert. He wants to replicate his success when he was the Sun Belt Offensive Player Of The Year in 2021 with South Alabama.
"Another goal I have, as I said a long time ago, is to get back to the version of myself I was in college,"  Tolbert said. "I want to get back to that player. I know that that player is in me. I know that it's possible. I know that it's there and I know what I can do."
In his final two seasons with the Jaguars, he recorded over 1,000 receiving yards and 16 touchdowns, breaking school records in the process. There was no CeeDee Lamb to worry about; he was the main weapon. Before discrediting his numbers due to playing in the Sun Belt, keep in mind he dropped 143 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions against the SEC's Tennessee in 2021.
He had a strong draft profile, highlighting his frame, speed, and, interestingly enough, route-running. His main weakness also happened to be catch adversity. So far in the NFL, route-running and catch adversity seem to have flipped in those regards.
Tolbert puts his time at South Alabama in high regard, even going so far as to stay with a long-standing tradition dating back to his freshman year of college.
He had surgery done on his left leg in his freshman year at USA after suffering a knee injury in preseason training camp. Since then, he has worn a sleeve on his left leg for the rest of his college career and then during practices in the NFL, since the look is outlawed during regular-season games.
"I had surgery when I was in my freshman year of college," Tolbert said. "That mental block when I first was coming back made me think that, even though this little sleeve does nothing, my leg was straight. You trick your mind; whatever it is you gotta do to make it work, you make it work. I took it and ran with it, and I've stuck with it, and so it's gonna stick with me as long as I play."

title: Examining the Under-the-Radar (But Very Significant) Dolphins Injury Concern
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins have the makings of a solid offensive line in place if Kadyn Proctor lives up to expectations and Jonah Savaiinaea can take the anticipated jump in his second season, but there is a clear problem with the group.
That problem is an alarming lack of depth, and it's a concern that's only growing with each passing day.
To help find a potential solution, the Dolphins swung the trade for New England Patriots 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace and an ideal world he can live up to his draft status in Miami and provide help either at guard or tackle.
But Wallace has become just one of the many unproven young players in the offensive line room, which continues to be missing the one veteran who projects as the top backup on the unit.
That would free agent acquisition Jamaree Salyer, who has not practiced since the third of training camp back on July 31.
Head coach Jeff Hafley hasn't been asked about Salyer recently, but it's not just that he hasn't practiced, he also hasn't been spotted at practice at all in August — unlike just about everybody else who is dealing with an injury, whether it be Dante Trader Jr., Kevin Coleman Jr., rookie Chris Bell or PUP cornerbacks Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr.
This makes it a bit concerning as to Salyer's availability at the start of the regular season. Yes, we're still a month away, but remember that Salyer was carted off the field during minicamp and missed the final week of OTAs.
And the reality is that the Dolphins really can't afford, as presently constituted, to be without Salyer for a long period of time.
Salyer joined the Dolphins as a free agent after spending four seasons with the L.A. Chargers, for whom he played both guard and tackle — and he was very durable there, played all 17 games in 2022-24 before playing 13 last year.
In light of fellow free agent pick-up Charlie Heck's well-publicized struggles in training camp — though he has practiced better the past few days — Salyer looks like he might be the one reliable backup right now at guard or at center.
Andrew Meyer is somebody who showed some promise as a rookie free agent, but the fact remains he's still an unproven commodity.
And the same applies to everybody at tackle outside of Heck.
The newest addition, Wallace, has only 10 games of NFL experience, but that's more than Marques Cox, Kevin Cline and Gottlieb Ayedze combined.
The thought coming out of the spring was that if something were to happen to Austin Jackson — and we don't need to go over his injury history — then Heck simply would fill in, but training camp has provided reason for concern.
Salyer has played right tackle before and right now he would look like a better option. He also would be the top backup at guard, even an option to start if it turned out that Savaiinaea wasn't able to take that step forward after his rough rookie season.
But Salyer has to be healthy and on the field to be able to contribute.
Right now he's not and he hasn't been for more than 10 days, with no clear picture as to when he'll be back.
So, yes, his injury is a clear concern. A major concern.

title: Dissecting the First Dolphins Depth Chart of 2026: Rookies at the Forefront
full_text:
With the Miami Dolphins set to open their preseason schedule Friday night against the Washington Commanders, we have our first depth chart of the 2026 season.
As we tell everyone every year, coaches produce a depth chart for official consumption only because it's a league requirement at this time of year and also because nothing is etched in stone.
With that in mind, here is what stood out from the Dolphins' first depth chart:
-- The first name at the top of the offensive depth is attention-grabbing because it's Caleb Douglas, and he's one of five rookies listed on the first team — including Jacob Rodriguez who listed as "or" at one of the inside linebacker spots. This isn't surprising, mind you, considering the reps Douglas has gotten in training camp.
-- Former UFL Gottlieb Ayedze is listed as the second-team left tackle and we'll honestly say here it would be a surprise if he were to take a regular season snap for Miami. But somebody has to be listed here, right?
-- Very interesting to note that new offensive lineman Caedan Wallace is listed as a backup at both right guard and right tackle, and we'd suggest that would seem to indicate he's got a pretty good chance at making the 53-man roster. Particularly noteworthy is Wallace being listed as one of top second-team right tackles along with free agent pick-up Charlie Heck. This speaks a bit to the depth concern along the offensive line.
-- Ben Sims being listed as first-team fullback/tight end tells us the Dolphins will be using a fullback in 2026, even if not in name. This matches what we've seen in camp with the usage of Sims as an H-back.
-- Jaylen Wright being listed ahead of Ollie Gordon II as the second-team running back suggests he's in the lead to be De'Von Achane's top backup, though that spot could be very fluid.
-- Rookie sixth-round pick D.J. Campbell being listed third team at right guard — and with an either/or at that — behind 2025 practice squad member Josh Priebe doesn't seem bode well for his chances of making the 53 as a rookie.
-- As with the offense, the defense lists 12 positions to account for the various personnel groupings the Dolphins will employ.
-- On the defensive line, Kenneth Grant or Jordan Philips being listed first team next to Zach Sieler makes sense because the opening defensive lineup figures to depend on whether the Dolphins are expecting a more run-happy or pass-happy opponent, Phillips being the choice to stop the run and Grant more so to rush the passer.
-- Two things that stand out at edge are rookie seventh-round pick Max Llewellyn listed ahead of veteran Cameron Goode at one spot and Robert Beal Jr. listed ahead of David Ojabo at the other. Goode flat out has outperformed Llewellyn so far in camp, while Ojabo brought better credentials to Miami than Beal when both arrived as free agents.
-- Rodriguez being listed as first-teamer alongside Tyrel Dodson with the "or" designation is eye-opening to a degree, though it's been well earned with Rodriguez really coming on in the last several days of camp.
-- Veteran Ronnie Harrison Jr. has had a very solid camp, which is why he's listed as second team along with Kyle Louis behind Jordyn Brooks when the rookie fourth-round pick otherwise normally would get the nod. It's entirely possible the Dolphins will wind up keeping Harrison along with Louis on the 53-man roster.
-- Rookie fourth-round pick Trey Moore has gotten a lot of work with the first unit in training camp, so it's not surprising to see him listed ahead of Willie Gay Jr. Gay, who left practice early with an injury Monday, remains one of the most confusing players on the roster.
-- There is nothing surprising at all in the secondary, where the only question is whether it should be taken as an automatic that starting nickel corner Chris Johnson will move outside when the Dolphins are using only four DBs. In that scenario, it likely would be Johnson and Brents as the starters.
-- On special teams, we shouldn't be surprised to see Malik Washington listed as the first-team punt and kickoff returner after the success he enjoyed last year.

title: Offensive Lineman Joe Huber on the Rise at Vikings Training Camp
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are serious about protecting their quarterback and opening holes in the run game during the 2026 NFL season. They proved this by using a first-round pick on left guard Donovan Jackson last year and extending right tackle Brian O'Neill this offseason.
An undrafted free agent out of Wisconsin in 2025, Joe Huber is entering his second NFL season. He played in 12 games for the Vikings as a rookie, starting in the team's Week 3 victory over the Cleveland Browns.
After that big game, Huber's involvement in the purple and gold offense dwindled, and he only played two snaps on the offensive line for the remainder of the season since Jackson returned to the starting lineup at left guard, although he continued to get snaps on special teams.
However, this preseason is a chance for Huber to again get on the team's radar. And he's already making the most of whatever opportunities pop up.
During Minnesota Vikings training camp on Tuesday, starting right guard Will Fries was out of action. To work with the first team, head coach Kevin O'Connell chose Joe Huber. They could have picked Henry Byrd, Michael Jurgens, or one of the rookies on the roster, but instead went with the six-foot-five, 314-pound Huber.
Huber's play gained praise according to the official Vikings website. His ability to step in at center if needed was noted, and the quality of creating holes in the run game was listed as one of the big positives from practice.
On Wednesday, the first unofficial depth chart of the season was released, and Huber was listed as the first backup under Jackson as left guard. This is proof that the 24-year-old Ohio native is someone the team trusts and wants to see more from.
It would be amazing if Huber could carve out a role for himself similar to another versatile offensive lineman, former Minnesota guard and center Joe Berger. His value on the roster for being able to play any of the interior positions on the line while having experience at right tackle in college could make him a player whom O'Connell puts a huge amount of faith in to continue developing and stepping in when needed.
Huber is a player to watch as he continues to build on his solid rookie season with the Vikings. Seeing what his role will be when he steps on the field for the first preseason game against the New York Giants will be something to keep an eye on.
