title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy Sees Bigger Role for One Wide Receiver This Season
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers’ preseason is now in full swing, giving non-key veterans valuable opportunities to earn more snaps and carve out bigger roles.
The 53-man roster deadline is on Sunday, August 30, at 3 pm PT. So the 49ers have three preseason games to think about as they play the Tennessee Titans , the Los Angeles Chargers and the Las Vegas Raiders.
One of the biggest position-group battles is at wide receiver. The 49ers have some difficult decisions to make, but this competition has been watched closely throughout the preseason.
Heading into training camp, Demarcus Robinson was widely expected to not make the cut . At 31 and entering the second year of his contract in San Francisco, his future with the 49ers looked slightly uncertain.
That said, Robinson has stayed healthy throughout training camp, which has been especially important for a 49ers team once again dealing with a long list of injuries
Ricky Pearsall will miss the entire season as he continues to recover from PCL surgery, while Christian Kirk and Mike Evans remain questionable and day-to-day, respectively.
But with injuries continuing to thin out the wide receiver room, the 49ers may have little choice but to rely on Robinson. His ability to stay on the field could ultimately secure his place on the roster.
Brock Purdy has advocated for a larger role for Robinson, telling reporters: “Yeah. I think he’s just one of the best receivers that I’ve played with in terms of the one-on-one matchup and his feel for the game.
"We’ll have something drawn up like, ‘Hey, the receiver needs to get this many steps and be here on time,’ but sometimes there’s situations where you cut it off short or you push up into a guy a little bit longer and then get out of the cut.
"Like, he has a good feel for the game when it comes to that. He’s played for a while. He’s got a lot of savviness to him. And obviously in the red zone, he’s got length, he’s got just the ability to go up and get the ball.
"So, obviously I learned a lot about him last year, but this offseason, watching film on him, it’s like, all right, we can give this guy more ops and have him be a huge part of our offense.
"He’s had a great camp. He’s been out there every day showing up, making plays and catches. Today [Tuesday] against the Titans too. Same thing. So, I’m really excited for him.”

title: 3 Things to Watch With De'Zhaun Stribling in 49ers Preseason Opener
full_text:
The first preseason game of 2026 has arrived for the San Francisco 49ers. It's always an exciting time when teams get to don their uniforms in a game again, despite it being an exhibition.
And while there won't be many starters playing for the 49ers today against the Tennessee Titans, there are still intriguing players to monitor , like rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling .
How well he performs is what everyone will pay attention to, but there are three more important things to watch with Stribling in the preseason opener. I break those three things down below.
One issue with Stribling coming out of college was his limited route tree. He didn't display a ton of variety in the routes he ran at Ole Miss.
The 49ers have surely been trying to expand the routes in Stribling's arsenal. Look for Stribling to run several different routes against the Titans.
They might not even be ones he runs much of in the regular season. This is the time for the 49ers to see how he looks running routes that aren't simply go-balls or in-breaking routes.
Everything has to be experimental to see what works and what doesn't. It'll reveal to everyone which routes he can immediately execute in Week 1 and which routes he needs more work on.
Stribling has the capability to line up all over the formation, minus the backfield. Seeing how the 49ers line him up will be very intriguing.
There's also the element of motion, which will be curious to see if Stribling will be used a lot for that. I imagine he will. Kyle Shanahan is sure to be creative with how Stribling is used pre-snap.
He can be aligned close to the tight end since he's an aggressive blocker. He can be in the slot or lined up on the outside and be used on a motion. Everything is on the table for Stribling.
Last but not least is the main reason the 49ers drafted Stribling. It's for his playmaking ability when he has the ball in his hands.
His yards after the catch are one of, if not his biggest strengths. Watching how he performs in that aspect will be a sight to see. It will help add context as to why the 49ers wanted him.
Stribling can also provide home run capability with his speed on vertical routes. He was brought in to help generate explosives. That is where the 49ers significantly lacked last year.
Even if he can't connect on one, if the potential is there, it's enough. It won't be difficult to tell if he's capable of boosting the 49ers in that category after a few opportunities.

title: 10 49ers With Everything to Gain in Preseason Opener Tonight
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers preseason opener is the first chance to get a real look at some of the players and how they fit into the roster. Kyle Shanahan does not expect many starters to get snaps in the first preseason game. Still, there are plenty of players to watch. What do fans need to know?
Stribling got healthy just in time to suit up for the preseason opener. He has flashed a lot in training camp. Now, the question is how he translates to game speed. Also, does he play more outside or in the slot? The slot is his best path to the roster.
The running back room is thin with the number of injuries they have. It appears none of the players expected to make the 53-man roster can suit up. Herbert is the best of the bubble running backs.
Rourke did not get to participate in the preseason during his rookie year. Now, he is fully healthy and ready to show that he can be the 49ers' backup quarterback by the start of next season .
The left guard position is wide open. So, aside from Jones, the question is whether Connor Colby plays left guard, and where in the rotation he stands. He was listed as a right guard, with Carver Willis behind Jones at left guard on the depth chart .
With Kittle out, the 49ers have Jake Tonges and Luke Farrell. Then, there is a wide-open competition. Deguara signed last week but can push to make the team.
Martin has reportedly been getting work starting next to Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw. Do they keep him in that role without those two starting, and how does he look?
This also includes his fellow UDFA James Thompson, who has flashed in training camp on the defensive line as well.
Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, and Keion White are unlikely to play, so Height should get on the field early and often. How does he look against the run, and does he have the pass-rush juice expected?
Has Sigle progressed in his second NFL season? Does he fit in the Raheem Morris defense as he did with Robert Saleh?
Hobbs has been quiet this offseason. Does he work in the slot, play outside, or mix in at both?

title: Four 49ers Who Need a Strong Performance Against the Titans
full_text:
Well, kind of. The first preseason game for the San Francisco 49ers kicks off today at Levi's Stadium against the Tennessee Titans.
A win or a loss doesn't matter, but it's still a meaningful game. Some players need to perform well to improve their current standing on the roster.
With that said, here are four 49ers who need a strong performance against the Titans.
No other player on the 49ers needs an impressive performance in the first preseason game more than Connor Colby . The starting left guard spot was there for the taking.
Now, he's staring at being a backup to Dominick Puni at right guard. The 49ers have been trying Colby out at right guard while giving Robert Jones the starting reps at left guard in the last week.
That signals Colby hasn't been able to cement himself during the first two weeks of training camp. If he gets reps at left guard in this game, he has to play incredibly well.
Where things stand now for him, they seem ready to abandon any idea of him starting completely. Colby has to make the 49ers rethink their chances of him as the starting left guard.
The same logic applies to Jones. He has a prime opportunity ahead of him. He's been receiving first-team reps in practice, which means the 49ers are intrigued by him.
They want to find out if he's better than Colby, if they don't already think that now. Against the Titans, Jones will need to prove the 49ers right for trying him out as the starter in the last week.
If he falters considerably in this game, it will put the 49ers in a pickle. They will start to pull away from him and look at either Colby at left guard again or give rookie Carver Willis a shot.
Knocking off Renardo Green as the starter is challenging, but Jack Jones has been making a strong case for that. In almost every practice, Jones has been cited for making a few sweet plays.
He's been playing great since the start of training camp. Now, he has to translate that from the practice field into a preseason game.
A strong performance against the Titans won't allow him to supplant Green as the starter. But it will make the 49ers continue to think about it, especially if Green goes through a rough patch.
One player who hasn't been cited for the plays they're making is Jordan Watkins . He's not doing a whole lot to stand out, even though he is playing with second- and third-stringers.
Maybe he's better suited to flash when it feels like a game, which makes tonight the perfect opportunity for him. He needs to impress the coaches.
Watkins is buried on the depth chart, but if he goes out there and balls out, the coaches will nod in approval. It will give him momentum for the next week of practice, which he desperately needs.
Otherwise, he will continue as a forgotten player . His roster spot likely isn't on the line, but it will be easier to consider the more he goes unnoticed.

title: 5 49ers Players to Follow in First Preseason Game Against the Titans
full_text:
The first preseason game for the San Francisco 49ers is finally here.
No longer will they be confined to the practice field . They get to unleash their players at Levi’s Stadium in front of a crowd against the Tennessee Titans. However, the majority of the starters will not play .
That’s typical for a preseason game, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t players to be intrigued by. With that said, here are five 49ers to follow closely against the Titans.
One of the most hyped players of training camp has been De’Zhaun Stribling . His skills have only been on display to reporters and some fans in the last two weeks.
Now, everyone gets to see what all the fuss is about. This is Stribling’s first step in cementing himself as a key role player in the 49ers’ offense. He needs a sound showing after the time he missed due to a hamstring injury.
Another rookie who has been receiving praise in camp lately is Jaden Dugger. He’s slowly been seeing an increase in reps with the first team, which is indicative of what the coaches think of him.
Dugger has shown enough to them that he’s ready to be a role player on the starting defense. This preseason game will showcase exactly what his role could look like and how sweet he’s looked in camp.
There hasn’t been much noise from Nick Martin in training camp. It’s probably been tough for him to stand out more with Dugger flashing in the last week or so.
He needs a solid performance against the Titans. Last year, he had a mediocre performance against the Denver Broncos. He couldn’t execute a tackle to save his life.
And with Dugger leapfrogging him on the depth chart, Martin could find himself buried or on another roster after final cuts. The Titans have been a team I’ve cited as one that could want Martin, since Robert Saleh was the one who wanted him.
The only noteworthy move the 49ers made at defensive end this offseason was drafting Romello Height. He’s their only real option at edge rusher outside of Nick Bosa .
His performance against the Titans will reveal what he’s been looking like in camp. The 49ers will hope he can stand out, as they need him to pan out, especially with Bosa’s knee tendinitis causing issues.
For the last week, the 49ers have stopped giving Connor Colby reps at left guard with the starters. They’ve been allocating them to Robert Jones, which the 49ers say is part of the plan.
However, whoever gets the nod to start the game will indicate where each player stands for the starting job. Plus, it’ll be intriguing to see how Colby looks.

title: Deebo Samuel Reveals Exactly Why He Rejoined the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers and Deebo Samuel are back working together after one year away.
Is Samuel's return a surprise? Not really. The 49ers front office signed him as soon as they knew Ricky Pearsall was going to undergo season-ending surgery on his PCL injury.
But both parties agreed to a very favorable one-year contract worth up to $7 million. It's since come to light that a fair whack of that money is incentive-based.
Samuel entered free agency after just one year with the Washington Commanders, and there were no reports of him being close to signing with another team.
But given the circumstances surrounding San Francisco right now, a reunion with the 49ers suddenly makes plenty of sense. As always, injuries dominate the headlines.
Samuel admitted that the culture was a key reason for coming back, the same reasoning as Dre Greenlaw .
"This is where I got drafted at, and the culture that John [Lynch] and Kyle [Shanahan] and those guys have built with the players that they have bought in, and the mentality that they have instilled in all the players, it's just a standard," Samuel shared on the NFL Network .
"And you can go back to last year—I was still keeping tabs on the guys. And with all the injuries and this, that, and the third that they was dealt, they still had a great season. And that's just the standard of next-man-up mentality. Everybody practices the same, everybody lives under one standard."
Samuel reacquainted himself with Brock Purdy after the pair previously helped take the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game and Super Bowl in 2022 and 2023. He also explained what he likes most about Purdy's game.
"I think Brock has been the most consistent, persistent, really good in decision-making, not making too many mistakes," Samuel said. "I think that's what he's really, really good at—getting the ball out on time, and giving receivers opportunities to step back to the ball even when you're covered. Let's see [if you can] make this play to build that trust, and also challenging the defense as well."
Samuel's return to the City by the Bay has been welcomed all around by staff and players alike, but it's best to temper expectations based on his first stint. He's older now and likely isn't operating at the same level he was during the prime years of his career.

title: Why the Buccaneers' Offensive Line is Poised to Dominate This Season
full_text:
Most football experts tend to agree that building a high-quality offense in the NFL starts and ends with the offensive line.
Based on his track record of prioritizing the trenches through the draft and free agency over the course of his time in Tampa Bay , it's safe to say that Buccaneers GM Jason Licht is one who abides by this philosophy.
Over the years, Licht has done a tremendous job of building strong units up front to ensure that his quarterbacks, whether it was Tom Brady in the early 2020s or Baker Mayfield now, have the protection they need to run the offensive game plans with limited interruptions.
Unfortunately, Licht was unable to properly evaluate the quality of his group in 2025 because the Bucs' o-line was completely ravaged by injury. The most troublesome implication of that, of course, was that the entire offense struggled as a result.
Because of the revolving door up front, receivers had less time to get open, Mayfield had less time to operate and the running backs didn't have the same amount of daylight they were accustomed to the year prior.
Fast forward a year, and aside from some precautionary rest for All-Pro LT Tristan Wirfs, the Buccaneers' offensive line is finally healthy and eager to re-establish itself as one of the league's best.
The Buccaneers' OL has more than just health working in their favor, though.
Even if Wirfs, Luke Goedeke, Cody Mauch and Ben Bredeson weren't in the lineup for significant chunks of time last season, they were still in the building. They understand the protection scheme, they understand each other's playstyle and they know how to communicate with one another when things get muddy. This is a massive benefit for a group that is looking to re-establish itself as one of the league's elite OL units in 2026.
Adding even more optimism to this group's outlook for this season and beyond is the fact that all of the Bucs' starting offensive linemen have youth on their side. Ben Bredeson is the oldest starting offensive lineman, and he is still just 28 years old.
There's no question that both Graham Barton (24) and Cody Mauch (27) have plenty of room to grow as players. Each has just two full NFL seasons under their belt, and it would be shocking if either one of them didn't take a significant step forward this year.
Wirfs and Goedeke are both 27 years old, and despite being elite players at their respective positions, there's no reason to believe that they couldn't both continue to improve as they have in each season so far in their respective careers.
At 28, Bredeson is the oldest of the bunch, but he's got plenty of experience, positional versatility and, even if he's coming off an injury, he seems to have really hit his stride since joining the Kevin Carberry and the Bucs' offensive line room a few seasons ago.
When it comes to evaluating offensive line play, at least from a media perspective, there is no one better than Brandon Thorn . Recently, Thorn unveiled his rankings for the top offensive linemen in the NFL heading into 2026 at each position.
Thorn clearly recognizes the talent that Licht has assembled along the offensive line in Tampa Bay.
In Thorn's opinion, Wirfs is the best LT in the NFL. Goedeke, meanwhile, was ranked as the fifth-best RT in the league. Bredeson, the lowest positional score of the Bucs' starters, was ranked the 21st best LG. Despite undertaking a steep learning curve after switching positions from college, Thorn already considers Barton to be the 11th-best center in the NFL. And lastly, Mauch, despite missing almost the entire 2025 season, is considered to be the seventh-best RG in football.
Thorn isn't the only one who recognizes the talent that the Bucs have up front, though. Pro Football Focus just published its team OL rankings this week, and the Buccaneers were graded as the third-best OL unit in the NFL heading into 2026.
"Injuries hurt the Buccaneers’ offensive line at points in 2025, but this is a really strong unit heading into the new season," they said. "Left tackle Tristan Wirfs set a career-high with a 92.7 PFF grade in 2025 and has yet to earn a PFF pass-blocking grade below 80.0 in a season. Opposite him, Luke Goedeke has improved throughout his career and didn’t allow a sack or hit on 416 pass-blocking snaps last year, while the return of Cody Mauch and the continued emergence of center Graham Barton give them the chance to be the best offensive line in football this season."
Top 10 Offensive Lines Ahead of the 2026 NFL Season💪 Save 33% on PFF+ Subscription: https://t.co/iondZ9gEDI pic.twitter.com/MEK1LbHDHL
There are many question marks surrounding the Buccaneers right now, who have a disgruntled defensive star and a quarterback who isn't happy with his contract situation. That being said, one of the best things the Bucs have going for them right now is the age, talent and continuity of their starting offensive line group.
If Wirfs, Bredeson, Barton, Mauch and Goedeke are all able to stay relatively healthy this season, not only could the Bucs have the best offensive line in football, but they would have a clear runway for a potentially prolific offensive season, which — in conjunction with what is expected to be a much improved defense — could very well catapult the Buccaneers into Super Bowl contention as early as this season.

title: Vita Vea Reminds Buccaneers Why He’s Worth A New Contract
full_text:
Vita Vea has been present throughout Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp, but he has yet to step foot on the field as he deals with a "tweaked" back (more so a hold-in) as he searches for a contract extension after publicly announcing a request for a trade.
The Buccaneers have said they have no intention of trading their All-Pro nose tackle, and instead will look to add to his current contract or find middle ground on an extension.
The defensive tackle market has exploded this offseason with the likes of Jeffery Simmons, Jalen Carter and Quinnen Williams all receiving major paydays, and Vea believes that he is worth being paid like one of the top guys in the league at his position.
With NFL Network on the ground for the Bucs' joint practice with the New York Jets, NFL analyst Mike Garafolo brought up numbers that reflect why Vea should get paid.
And Vea, who rarely comes out to voice anything, replied to the tweet with a simple emoji agreeing.
🤷🏽‍♂️ https://t.co/wzyn0thSnq
Vea has been one of the top performers at his position, consistently taking on double teams in the trenches while getting into the backfield for sacks, tackles for loss and anchoring the defense against the run.
Vea has been one of the most important pieces on the Bucs' defense, and while he is set to make $17 million in 2026, none of the money is guaranteed.
On top of that, his productivity as one of the top players at his position isn't reflected by his current contract, ranking 21st amongst all interior defensive linemen.
The Bucs have been adamant that they have no intentions of trading Vea, but if they aren't able to come to an agreement on either an extension or getting him more guaranteed money for this season, they might not have any other option.
Vea likely won't want to sacrifice any of his money, so he will have to return to the field eventually.
If Vea is traded, however, it drastically changes the outlook of a Bucs defense that is looking to turn things around after a few years of average play.

title: Buccaneers Players Who Could Surprise Against The Jets
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play their first preseason game on Friday when they face the New York Jets in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
The Bucs have already been conducting joint practices with the Jets this week, and things have gotten chippy as both squads test their mettle. Those joint practices are valuable, but head coach Todd Bowles and the rest of his coaching staff will get a good first look at some rookies in game-time situations under the lights on Friday.
There are a few players we're curious to see, and they could introduce themselves to a wider audience if they play well on Friday. Here are four Bucs players who could surprise in their preseason debut:
The Bucs drafted Bauer Sharp in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft as a raw move tight end prospect, and so far, he's impressed throughout camp. His athleticism has been on display and he's made plenty of plays during training camp so far, including a grab he made against the Jets in joint practice.
Sharp will be competing with TE Devin Culp for his spot on the roster, so he'll really have to impress to solidify himself there. He's flown a bit under the radar among NFL fans outside of Tampa Bay, though, so if he has a great game in New York, he could surprise plenty on the national stage.
Garnes came to Tampa Bay as an undrafted free agent out of Arizona, and since then, he's put himself at the forefront in training camp,
Garnes has made numerous pass breakups across all of camp, and he even had two during the second day of joint practice against the Jets. He's mainly been competing with Pepe Williams, who the Bucs signed last year, but his increasing production in conjunction with CB Benjamin Morrison's absence has allowed him ample time to prove himself — and prove himself he has.
Some great coverage plays on Friday, or even an interception, would go along way for a UDFA like Garnes to establish himself. Nothing can be more surprising than a player who went undrafted showing out, and Garnes has the chance to do just that.
Walker has been the talk of training camp. The Bucs drafted him in the fifth round last year, but after he tore his ACL in training camp, he's making his official debut this year.
If he lives up to the hype he's had already, he could be in line to shock the NFL world in 2026. Walker has been dominant throughout camp and won plenty of pass-rushing reps, and his get-off and skill moves look polished for a second-year player. He can't sack the quarterback in practices, but in a preseason game, he's free to hit the quarterback and show off his acumen.
Walker has the chance to surprise the entire league in 2026, and the road to doing that starts on Friday.
The Buccaneers brought on Patterson as a tryout player in rookie minicamp and liked him enough to sign him. And based on how he's played in training camp, the team probably feels better and better about that every day.
Patterson has stepped up in a big way in training camp with multiple other wideouts like Tez Johnson and David Sills injured. He's caught plenty of touchdowns in team periods and has shown he can make grabs through tight windows, and this is all despite him catching just eight passes last year with Georgia Tech.
As always, though, camp studs have to prove they can do it in a game. If Patterson shows out on Friday, he could have a place on this roster against all odds.

title: Buccaneers Dealing With QB Injury Ahead of Jets Preseason Game
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been in New Jersey this week for their joint practice sessions with the New York Jets ahead of their first preseason game of 2026.
Things have been chippy between the two sides over the two practices, but both sides will now get the opportunity to show what they have when the lights come on Friday night.
However, the Bucs might be down their starting quarterback for the matchup, as backup quarterback Jake Browning is dealing with an injury.
Browning, who was signed this offseason to back up Baker Mayfield, was slated to start against the Jets with Todd Bowles ruling Mayfield out.
However, that is now uncertain after Browning was rolled up on during the teams' first joint practice.
The injury doesn't seem to be too severe, with Bowles not quite ruling out the veteran backup yet, but did iterate that if Browning is not able to go, then second-year QB Connor Bazelak would get the nod to start with rookie undrafted QB Jalon Daniels also getting his first NFL action.
It would be wise of the Buccaneers to hold Browning out of the matchup given their backup quarterback problems of the past and to avoid further injury that could cause him to miss more time.
If the Bucs do withhold him from the game against the Jets, expect heavy doses of both Bazelak and Daniels, who are vying for the team's third QB roster spot.
Browning went undrafted out of Washington a few years back before being signed by the Minnesota Vikings.
His stint with the Vikings didn't last long, as he was eventually picked up by the Cincinnati Bengals, which is where he became a household name after filling in for the often-injured Joe Burrow.
Over the past three seasons with the Bengals, Browning has started 10 games, going 4-6 with a 68.5% completion percentage, 2,707 yards passing, 18 touchdowns and 15 interceptions.
The numbers won't wow anyone, but having a backup that is young with plenty of starting experience at the NFL level should give the Buccaneers confidence after years of having the likes of Kyle Trask and Teddy Bridgewater as backups.
The Buccaneers and Jets will face each other Friday night on WFLA locally in Tampa Bay at 7:00 PM EST.

title: Emeka Egbuka's Injury Status Revealed With New Update After Buccaneers-Jets Practice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a stacked wide receivers room heading into 2026. That being said, any injury to that room would be tough for the Bucs' offense this upcoming season.
The Bucs are already dealing with some injuries among their wide receivers, as wideouts Tez Johnson (groin) and David Sills (knee), among others, have been banged up during camp. The Buccaneers potentially looked to take a serious hit to the room, though, when wideout Emeka Egbuka went down during Wednesday's practice and was attended to by trainers.
Egbuka got rolled up on during an end around and was on the trainer's table for quite a bit, and it left many wondering what his status was after trainers got a more in-depth look after practice.
As it turns out, Tampa Bay may have avoided a close call, and Egbuka looks to be mostly fine after the incident.
NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Wednesday that Egbuka suffered a toe injury that the team considers to be "minor", paving the way for him to return to action sooner rather than later.
#Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka’s injury that cut his practice today is a toe issue that’s considered minor, source says. That jibes with RB Bucky Irving telling @MJD earlier during our interview, “I think he’s pretty good. He just got rolled over on.” Thumbs up 👍 on Egbuka’s toe. pic.twitter.com/P8355zqSms
While the injury appears minor and Egbuka will likely miss a little bit of practice time before the regular season, toe injuries can be a bit tricky. Hopefully for Tampa Bay, Egbuka's injury doesn't take too long to heal and he can factor into the lineup for Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals on the road.
In the meantime, the Bucs will continue to rely on Jalen McMillan and veteran Chris Godwin in the wide receivers room. With Egbuka likely missing time, though, Tampa Bay's wideouts room remains thin — Tez Johnson, Kameron Johnson, Sills and now Egbuka are banged up, so wideout Ted Hurst will have a lot of reps to take over in the latter part of camp.
The Bucs face the New York Jets on Friday at 7 p.m. for their first preseason game of the year.

title: Fans May Have to Wait to See Buccaneers' Top Draft Pick Play in Preseason
full_text:
Fans in Tampa Bay collectively rejoiced the moment that Roger Goodell announced Rueben Bain Jr. would be the selection when the Buccaneers made their first pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Draft picks can be very contentious.
There are so many different players, positions and levels of competition to evaluate when considering which player will be the best fit for a given roster. Not only do these debates happen between NFL scouts and decision-makers, but also among fans as well.
However, when the Bucs selected Bain 15th overall this past April, it was pretty well unanimous amongst the fanbase that Tampa Bay had just hit a home run.
Not only was Bain a born-and-raised Floridian, but he played his college ball at Miami, where his dominating style of play off the edge helped the Hurricanes reach the National Championship game for the first time in almost a quarter of a century.
The Bucs have been in desperate need of an impact edge rusher for many years now. Bain's selection provides at least the potential for that dream to become a reality.
Bain's explosive power, relentless style of play, and versatility to both rush the passer and defend the run at a high level made for what could easily be considered the easiest decision in Jason Licht 's tenure as GM of the Bucs.
Although we've yet to see Bain make his NFL debut, the early returns have been extremely positive. Throughout minicamp, training camp and joint practices, Bain has earned the respect of his teammates, coaches, and the fans who have gotten the opportunity to watch him practice.
"I can't wait to see what he does this season." Even Reuben Bain Jr's teammates are excited to see what the rookie can do on the field this season after an impressive start to training camp. #WeAreTheKrewe #NFL #NFLNews | @FOX13News pic.twitter.com/Q5QH5Vlw8T
Everyone who has been impressed by what they've seen from Bain so far, though, is going to have to wait a little longer to see the dynamic defender in live game action.
On Tuesday, following the second day of Buccaneers' joint training camp practices with the New York Jets ahead of their preseason game on Friday, Todd Bowles informed the media that he doesn't see Bain playing much, if at all, in the game, per Jeff Dubrof.
Bowles doesn’t foresee Rueben Bain playing much if at all on Friday night #bucs
Although many fans who have been eagerly awaiting Bain's NFL debut may find themselves disappointed, this is a positive sign regarding the role that Bain has already carved out for himself on this football team.
Not only was Bain listed as a starter on the team's first unofficial depth chart which was recently released, but the fact that the team is likely to rest him in their first preseason game further cements his status as a likely starter on this football team.
Chances are, we will see Bain suit up for the Buccaneers this preseason. Just not yet.
This decision represents a logical big-picture approach to managing the explosive rookie's workload in his first offseason while ultimately limiting the injury risk he is exposed to. The positive takeaway from this particular decision is that fans can expect Rueben Bain Jr. to play a big role in Bowles' defense right away as a rookie.
If the talent, commitment and work ethic he's shown so far in his first few months as a pro are any indication of the NFL player he will become, then this is the right move.

title: One Buccaneers Player Who Missed Last Season Has Jason Licht Fired Up
full_text:
Buccaneers 2025 fourth-round pick David Walker has been very impressive throughout training camp to this point. Walker has been able to make a great number of plays in practice, having plenty of would-be sacks against backups and starters alike.
One person who is very excited to see what Walker can do this 2026 season is general manager Jason Licht.  According to Jason Licht, when speaking to WDAE, the excitement for Walker is "on an even plane" with that of rookie Rueben Bain Jr.
Now that is a pretty bold comparison for Licht to make, as Bain was the fifteenth overall pick in the most recent NFL Draft and Walker was a fourth-round selection last year. However, both players have looked very impressive in training camp so far and should be a very bright spot in a hopefully new and improved pass rush for the Bucs' defense this season.
Licht is not the only person in the Buccaneers organization to give praise to Walker. Speaking to the media on August sixth after practice, here is what head coach Todd Bowles had to say about what he's been impressed with regarding Walker.
"Just his energy and his athleticism [have] showed up," Bowles said. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves. He moves like an inside [linebacker], but he plays outside [linebacker] and he [has] great power. To see him out there playing fast and not worried about his knee is great."
Another player who had a very good impression of Walker was veteran pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad.
"He has a motor. The good ones, as far as [defensive] linemen and pass rushers, and all that good stuff, they play with a motor, and he plays with a motor. For his size, he knows who he is and the things that he [does], he [does] well. He's been having a [great] camp, so it's impressive."
Time will tell how much of an impact Walker will have this upcoming season. He's still competing for reps with a lot of players, including Muhammad, Bain Jr, and other veterans like Yaya Diaby, Anthony Nelson and even Chris Braswell if he does make the final roster. However, the organization certainly has a lot of high hopes for the young second-year player.

title: Will Baker Mayfield Play in Buccaneers' First Preseason Game vs. Jets?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gone through 10 days of training camp, including their joint practice with the New York Jets on Tuesday. After all of that, it's almost time for the team's first preseason game of the year.
The Bucs are set to face the Jets Friday, and when they do so, they'll be looking to evaluate many of their rookies for the first time under the lights. These games can be very important for that evaluation, and as a result, it's also important to make sure other players on the squad can play well enough around them to properly evaluate them.
With that in mind, head coach Todd Bowles has the decision on whether or not to play his starting quarterback in Baker Mayfield. The option is also worth considering in the wake of a potential injury to backup quarterback Jake Browning on Tuesday.
So will the Buccaneers play Mayfield in their first preseason outing this season?
Mayfield is not set to play during Tampa Bay's preseason game on Friday against the Jets. Initially, quarterback Jake Browning was set to start that game, but he injured his back during the first day of joint training camp, so his status on Friday is in jeopardy, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud.
Bucs No. 2 QB Jake Browning appeared to injure his back. Todd Bowles had no update but Browning was expected to start Friday vs Jets. He said Baker Mayfield will not play.
That makes sense. Mayfield is the team's starting quarterback, and it would be unusual to play him in the first preseason game of the year unless he specifically requested it as some quarterbacks do.
That being said, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield plays during the preseason at all. Last year, he skipped out on preseason entirely — he was slated to play during the team's second week of preseason against the Pittsburgh Steelers last year, but Bowles decided against it at the last minute and did not play him at all during the preseason.
There's a chance that a similar scenario could happen this preseason, too. For now, though, the Bucs will have to figure out what they plan to do on Friday if Browning isn't able to go — reps will be split between QBs Jalon Daniels and Connor Bazelak, if that's the case.
The Bucs play the Jets at 7 p.m. on Friday.

title: Baker Mayfield Wants His 'Lick Back' in Buccaneers 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers started out 6-2 in 2025, and things were looking up for quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield was an MVP candidate, and vibes were great in Tampa Bay.
Those vibes didn't end up continuing throughout the season, though. The Bucs went 2-7 over their last nine games and, presumably due to injuries, Mayfield's play deteriorated. Some thought that head coach Todd Bowles' job was in danger, but he kept his job and plans to coach the Bucs in 2026.
Mayfield and the rest of Tampa Bay's squad, who were there for the 2025 season, weren't happy about how it ended. Mayfield recently had a contract saga this offseason, where he placed a training camp deadline for an extension that he and the team did not meet, but he's stressed that he's all ball from here on out after that saga has come to a close.
Mayfield may be unhappy about his contract situation, but in a recent appearance on the 4th & South podcast with Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette, he seems far unhappier about what happened last season — and he's solely focused on fixing it.
Mayfield was very vocal about his disappointment after he couldn't get an extension done with the Bucs. He told Fournette and Landry that if some people are unhappy with that, it's too bad — but he promised to rectify the team's mistakes from last season this year.
"I've always worn my emotions and thoughts on my sleeve. If you like that, that's great. If you don't, that's too bad — I'm not gonna change for you," Mayfield said. "There's the business side of football. Yes, we all play this for a job, but they know that when it comes to gamedays, I'm ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026 — we didn't play well enough in 2025, so it's on go."
Baker Mayfield on contract negotiations not distracting him from how he’ll come to play in 2026 for Bucs. “They [team] knows when it comes to gamedays, I’m ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026. We didn’t play well in ‘25. It’s on go.” (via @4thAndSouthPod ) pic.twitter.com/zeGjg5V9rG
Tampa Bay and Mayfield could be in the position to do just that this season. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson could be a better option at offensive coordinator than Josh Grizzard, and new offensive weapons like running back Kenny Gainwell and wideout Ted Hurst could improve the offense in a big way.
There's still quite a bit of time until Mayfield can try and get that lick back. For now, though, the Bucs will continue joint training camp passes vs. the New York Jets this week before a preseason game on Friday.

title: Multiple Fights Occur at Buccaneers Joint Practice vs. Jets
full_text:
Today was the first day of joint practices between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New York Jets, and to say that things got heated in practice is a bit of an understatement.
Multiple fights occurred during practice today between the two teams, with defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson being involved in one, per Jeff Dubrof, and offensive guard Luke Goedeke being involved in two, per Ralph Vacchiano .
The first fight that Goedeke was involved in included rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who wanted to go against Goedeke in one-on-one drills, which then resulted in said fight. This is what Goedeke had to say on the incident, per Pewter Report:
︀︀“Well, [David Bailey] called me out in one-on-ones and wanted to go against me and lost, and then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare], I believe, came from the side and just cheapshotted me."
Bucs RT Luke Goedeke on the practice fights with the Jets on Tuesday: “Well, [David Bailey] called me out in 1-on-1’s and wanted to go against me and lost. And then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare] I believe came from the side and just cheapshotted me." pic.twitter.com/AIP6fG7nw2
The Bucs were already dealing with some pushing and shoving matches occurring in their own training camp practices before making the jump to New Jersey to practice with the Jets. This is usually the time of year when teams get very antsy and are typically ready for live game reps and the regular season.
It is also important to remember that these two teams do have a bit of recent history. They played each other in a close matchup last season, where the Bucs would win 29-27. The Jets, however, came very close to winning said matchup on a blocked field goal that gave them the lead late. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would then be seen dancing down the sidelines as the Jets took the lead over the Bucs.
Also, the Bucs have spent a good amount of effort this off-season improving their mentality and grit when it comes to the roster. Players like A'Shawn Robinson were added to players like Luke Goedeke to give the team more of an edge and to help change some of the more laid-back attitude the team had in the past couple of seasons.
Overall, fights during practices are not ideal, but not surprising. Football is a very physical sport, and these things happen all the time. The Bucs and Jets face off on August 14th in the Bucs' first preseason matchup and should have another joint practice on the schedule soon. We'll see if more fighting occurs.

title: 3 Biggest Winners and Losers From Titans Preseason Victory Over 49ers
full_text:
After waiting through the entirety of what may have been the most eventful Tennessee Titans offseason of the last decade, fans would've likely taken any respectable level of football in the preseason opener. Brian Callahan not calling the shots goes a long way already.
However, it helps that Robert Saleh picked up a win in his sideline debut as Tennessee topped the San Francisco 49ers, 19-13. That's technically a 1-0 start.
With a full game with the new-look Titans on the books, we've compiled the three biggest winners and losers from the opening matchup. There's plenty for fans to celebrate here in spite a handful of big names dropping the ball.
The Titans have a running back room full of studs, and the group proved it together against San Francisco.
Combining for 167 yards on the ground (compared to the 49ers' 84 yards), Tennessee's backfield was one of the only clear bright spots on offense. Tony Pollard punched in a red zone touchdown in the first quarter, although Julius Chestnut actually led the battalion with 47 yards on just six carries.
Rookie Nick Singleton also had a notable night, adding 31 yards of his own on eight attempts, alongside Tyjae Spears' 35 yards on four rushes. The whole crew went to work.
Even in limited minutes (three drives), Tennessee's starting quarterback appeared out of rhythm. Finishing 5/12 passing with just 57 yards, Ward simply couldn't get to his spots.
No turnovers from Ward avoided his showing being outright disastrous, but it'd have been difficult to drum up a more underwhelming sophomore debut from the Titans' franchise player, even in the preseason. He missed a number of open throws and was tagged with an intentional grounding penalty.
JC Latham, for as much heat as he's taken this offseason as a questionable piece of staying power as the Titans rebuilt, had himself a strong night to kick things off this preseason.
Like every great offensive tackle, his efficiency is proven by the "0" in Ward's sack statline. Scattered pressure aside, Latham stood his ground and kept the 49ers at bay on Pollard's scoring drive. The OT appears to be stepping up right when the Titans need him most.
After struggling to contain the 49ers' offense in joint practice earlier this week, Tennessee's secondary continued to struggle in live action. On the night, the Titans' pass defense stood out in all the wrong ways.
San Francisco's Kurtis Rourke threw a near-perfect 12/14 for 101 yards as the starter, dicing up the Titans every chance he got. De'Zhaun Stribling went for 63 yards receiving, making him one of three Niners to eclipse 20 receiving yards. No Titan achieved the same metric.
It was death by a thousand cuts for the secondary specifically, even if the unit managed to avoid allowing any scores through the air. San Francisco ended up with 238 passing yards.
Hey, a win is a win. By all means, Joey Slye showed up and played his part to a tee in the Titans' preseason opener.
Slye went a perfect 4/4 (1/1) kicking for Tennessee, including a long shot from 58 yards out that went down as the final nail in the match. Did we want to see more from Brian Daboll's offense? Yes.
Is this just the first preseason game, and Slye was made all the better by picking up the slack? Also yes.
Carnell Tate's struggles can be partially lumped with Ward's, although not entirely. Tennessee's rookie receiver was both outplayed by the aforementioned Stribling, the 49ers' own rookie, and his fellow pass-catchers.
Ending up with zero catches on three targets, Titans fans expected more of Tate given all the noise he's been making in training camp. He's got the most room (and time) to improve of anyone on this list, but Tate going totally quiet was something nobody could've expected.
Tennessee will head back home to regroup before hosting the Seattle Seahawks in 10 days. Ward, Tate, and the Titans' secondary will look to recover, whereas the game-one winners can continue to build on their early momentum.

title: Titans' Will Levis Has Golden Opportunity to Save NFL Career in Preseason Opener Against 49ers
full_text:
After a few weeks of grueling training camp practices, the Tennessee Titans will finally take the field for a preseason contest. Robert Saleh's group will square off against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on Thursday, and though many players have a lot at stake , nobody has more pressure on them than quarterback Will Levis.
Levis has had a rough camp, as he has struggled to keep the ball out of harm's way and is firmly stuck as the No. 3 quarterback behind Cam Ward and Mitchell Trubisky. Levis threw another interception during joint practice on Tuesday to 49ers defensive back Jakob Robinson.
During Thursday night's game, Levis should play a good number of snaps with Tennessee's second- and third-team offenses, and it'll be an opportunity for the Kentucky product to salvage his NFL career.
At this point, Levis would have to tally a near-perfect preseason, one without any turnovers and with consistent, efficient play to beat out Trubisky for the backup job. Trubisky is more experienced and has spent time with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll before with the Buffalo Bills.
Based on what we've seen from Levis over the last couple of weeks and when he started 12 games in 2024, it's clear he isn't capable of going multiple games without turning the ball over or making a head-scratching blunder. However, if Levis can put together a solid preseason in which he shows improvement in his decision-making and leads sustainable scoring drives, the 27-year-old could find a new home fairly quickly if the Titans let him go during final cuts, which is expected. For Levis, this must start Thursday night in San Francisco.
Levis can't afford to be inconsistent over the next few weeks and post a good game here and a bad one there. The 2023 second-round pick needs to be a steady performer throughout the preseason, and that should lead to another opportunity elsewhere once his tumultuous Titans tenure comes to an end.
With Levis set to go up against the 49ers' backups and third-stringers, he will have a golden opportunity to kick the preseason off on a high note. Though it never worked out in Tennessee, Levis still has talent and could extend his career somewhere else if he takes advantage of his chances for the rest of August, like what Malik Willis did a few years ago .

title: Nick Singleton Could Earn His Spot in Titans Rotation With Preseason Debut vs. 49ers
full_text:
You could pick any one of the Tennessee Titans' rookies or sophomores as breakout candidates this preseason, and you'd likely have a case to make. Receivers Carnell Tate and Xavier Restrepo both stand out for different reasons, and linebacker James Williams (a third-year) is also seen as someone primed for a leap. However, Nick Singleton has become an underrated name in the fray.
Singleton, a former Penn State Nittany Lion, was taken by the Titans in the fifth round of the NFL Draft this year. After an impressive turn in Tennessee's joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers, the rookie back is facing down the perfect opportunity to earn a spot in the backfield rotation.
In time, he may even have the ability to take it over entirely, and it all starts in tonight's preseason opener.
Jim Wyatt reported a touchdown from Singleton in the aforementioned joined practice, as well as "several other impressive carries." The rookie is making an impact early, dubbed "a great teammate" and "real explosive" by Cam Ward as well.
Having already familiarized himself with that 49ers defense, Singleton should have no problem making the most of his clock against San Francisco.
As is the nature with preseason competition, Singleton's status as a backup (for now) means he's on deck to get plenty of opportunities. Even given Robert Saleh's claim that Tennessee will play their starters for more than one series, it's fair to expect time from Singleton in the second half.
If he does get out there and make a splash, his competition in the backfield isn't as steep as it may seem on the surface.
Of course, Tony Pollard is a bonafide veteran who has temporarily earned his spot as the Titans' RB1. Even throughout the franchise's turmoil last season, Pollard broke the 1,000-yard mark and scored five touchdowns. But he's also in the last year of his contract and is about to turn 30.
Who's up to bat from there? Tyjae Spears would have Tennessee's claim to the top spot beyond Pollard, and has already seen extensive work in the passing game this offseason. He should be expected to continue to rise into a primary role.
There's no reason to think that Singleton can't rise with him, though. Julius Chestnut and Michael Carter both fell behind Singleton in touches at Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage. So long as he continues to climb and make an impact, Singleton will remain a serious riser for the Titans.
After all, he scored double-digit touchdowns in three of his four seasons with the Nittany Lions. He's had what it takes from the jump, and Tennessee taking a chance on him was all it took for that to emerge in the NFL.

title: Where to Watch and What to Expect: Titans Preseason Opener vs. 49ers
full_text:
We've finally made it, Titans fans. After one of the most action-packed summers in recent franchise memory, the entirely rebuilt Tennessee Titans play football today. Robert Saleh's coaching debut with the baby blue and white will come in his former home out west tonight against the San Francisco 49ers, and it does so on the heels of a heated joint practice between the two teams.
Between some thrown punches and plenty of words exchanged, the energy is already at a boiling point between the Titans and 49ers. Tonight, in live competition, we'll get to watch that fuel turn into fire. When the bout kicks off, there are more than a few key factors to keep an eye on.
But to keep an eye on anything in tonight's matchup, you'll have to tune in and watch it first.
Tennessee's debut matchup on Thursday, Aug. 13, will air from the jump on WKRN Channel 2 in Nashville, at 8 p.m. CT. NFL Network will then join the game in progress an hour later, at 9 p.m.
The matchup taking place in California is bad luck for the average viewer's sleep schedule, but what else are we to do at the very beginning of the season? Any way you can watch, tune in for the technical first game of an entirely new era.
As for what to look out for specifically:
Robert Saleh confirmed that he'll play the Titans starters for more than a series against the 49ers, which means we'll get complete looks at the team's primary unit going forward, on both sides of the ball.
On the whole, this is an opportunity to see what Tennessee is made of in their current state. Much can change as the year goes on, but even a prolonged stint in a preseason game like this one can serve as a solid litmus test as to where this group's potential stands.
Within the starting squad more specifically, everyone will have a thumb on the connection between Cam Ward and Carnell Tate. This duo is positioned as the future of Titans football, and the flashes they showed in Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage was enough to send Titans fans into a frenzy online.
Being their first chance to compete together in an actual game, the tether between Ward and Tate will be properly tested under the spotlight against San Francisco.
Finally, once the starters give way to some of the guys vying for bigger roles (or even a roster spot), we'll get to see Tennessee's bastion of backup receivers battle it out for expanded touches.
In addition to the obviously anticipated Xavier Restrepo, both KJ Osborn and Bryce Oliver should get the opportunity to prove themselves worthy of a rotation spot in the preseason opener. Who comes in behind Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike?
Maybe we'll find out tonight. Either way, we'll have you covered here as the whole thing goes down.

title: 4 Titans Players With the Most to Gain in Preseason Opener Against 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans will play a football game for the first time in more than seven months on Thursday, as the team is set to open the preseason against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Tennessee had a joint practice with San Francisco on Tuesday and will now conclude its trip in Santa Clara with a preseason contest.
Head coach Robert Saleh said after practice on Tuesday that the Titans' starters will play Thursday night and even get more than one drive. It's critical for the starters to see the field a bit to prepare for the regular season, but still, this game isn't about them.
The main focus of Thursday's game is for players on the bubble to bolster their claims for a roster spot and raise their stock. With that in mind, let's take a look at four Titans who have the most to gain with a standout performance against the 49ers.
Entering camp, Williams was in danger of getting cut. However, he's been fantastic so far in camp, as Williams has significantly improved in pass coverage and is still playing with tenacity and power.
Saleh also commended Williams earlier in camp for losing 20 pounds this offseason , which explains why the Miami product is playing faster and fits well in the new-look defense.
If Williams carries his impressive play from practice into the first preseason game, he should secure a roster spot and make the Titans rethink the linebacker depth chart. Williams has outplayed Cody Barton and Mohamoud Diabate in camp, and if that continues, we could see the position group look a lot different than initially expected come Week 1.
Restrepo was the biggest winner of Tuesday's joint practice, as the 2025 undrafted free-agent receiver hauled in two touchdowns and led the team in catches with five. Restrepo has been making plays all camp and is pushing for a roster spot for the second straight year.
With Tennessee already having at least five roster locks at receiver in Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike, Restrepo is fighting for one of the final spots. Bryce Oliver will also likely make the roster due to his special teams ability.
However, if Restrepo posts a productive outing on Thursday, the Titans may consider keeping seven receivers and retaining the 24-year-old playmaker. Restrepo's connection with quarterback Cam Ward should also help him in roster arguments, but an exceptional preseason would go a long way for the young receiver's case.
Harrell has generated some pressure this camp, but overall, it's been a quiet last few weeks for the 2024 seventh-round pick.
Though Harrell hasn't made much noise in camp, the Michigan product ended the 2025 campaign on a high note , tallying 4.5 sacks in the final five games of the year and establishing himself as a key piece of the pass rush. However, he's fighting for a roster spot in Tennessee's deep edge rusher group.
Harrell must turn in a dominant preseason to ensure his future in Nashville for another year. The young pass rusher has proven that he can be an impact player in spurts, but Harrell must put it all together.
At this point, Levis would have to post a historic preseason to save his future with the Titans . The 2023 second-round pick likely won't be on the roster by September, but what Levis can do in the preseason, starting Thursday, is audition for his next team.
An efficient preseason where he takes care of the ball and leads the second-team and third-team offense on sustainable scoring drives could entice a team to give Levis another chance. The Kentucky product still possesses solid arm talent and mobility, but his decision-making and confidence are holding him back.
A team that wants to upgrade its backup quarterback situation or add a developmental signal-caller could take a flier on Levis and give the Titans a late-round pick in return. It would be a win-win for all parties involved.

title: Pro-Bowl LB Fred Warner Praises Cam Ward's Fearless Attitude for Titans
full_text:
Cam Ward isn't afraid to get his hands dirty. The Tennessee Titans quarterback has already garnered a reputation in the NFL for his brutal honesty, and according to San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner, that was on full display in the teams' recent joint practice.
In a clip from 95.7 The Game, the four-time Pro-Bowl defender praised Ward's fearless mindset, even as he stands across from one of the meanest defenses in the league. "I think Cam is one of the unique quarterbacks where he's not afraid to sit there and play that game with you," Warner said of Ward.
"I love joint practices, though. It's the best." Warner, after chirping with Ward all practice, was all smiles following the encounter. Ward also spoke on the matter, sharing a similarly positive outlook on their bickering.
“I think Cam (Ward) is one of the unique quarterbacks where he’s not afraid to sit there and play that game with you… I love joint practices, though. It’s the best (smirks).” 😈 Fred Warner on chirpin with Titans QB Cam Ward at joint practice pic.twitter.com/wgKJCtcjxJ
"That's what I want to see, because I want him to be at his best. So, when I'm at my best, I know what I can and can't do in a game," said Ward. "He helped me out a lot today, he's a great player."
Not every Titans player can share that optimism, as both Austin Deculus and Dan Moore Jr. got booted from practice due to their own altercations. But for Ward, it's healthy to get mixed up with an experienced defender this early in his career, especially if he doesn't take the beef to heart.
Ward embracing the trash talk also aligns well with Carnell Tate's "fast and violent" quote after the practice. Tennessee's rookie receiver saw the intensity as a benefit for the Titans more than anything else. The battle was a chance for Tennessee, in Tate's words, to prove "who we are."
Heading into Thursday's preseason opener against San Francisco, we'll be looking out for a Titans team playing with that tenacity on the whole.
After all, it'll be the same 49ers team that just attempted to bully the Titans all practice facing off against them again. Only this time, they'll have the benefit of a home field and a bastion of fans looking to witness their first win of the year.
On the opposite end of the spectrum, Ward and the Titans are trying to make an early statement to the NFL under their new head coach. That sets the stage for an unusually tense preseason matchup.
We'll have the coverage of tomorrow night's game here. Hopefully Ward's talkative tendencies carry over into that duel, as they seem to translate to similarly bold play on the field.

title: Carnell Tate Reaffirms Titans 'Fast and Violent' Mentality Ahead of Preseason Brawl With 49ers
full_text:
If the Tennessee Titans' joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers was any indication of what their preseason matchup is going to be like, we could be in for a real heater. Punches were thrown and two players were ejected (both from Tennessee's camp). After the intense run, Carnell Tate was asked if the clash served as a "reality check" for Tennessee.
"It didn't feel like a reality check at all," Tate responded quickly. "We went out there and proved to them who we are... We're the Titans, we came here to play fast and violent." Tennessee's X account took the quote and ran with it and, voila, we have our table dressing for Thursday night's opener.
Beyond the entertaining optics, however, lies a mindset that seems to have permeated the entirety of this Titans team. Keen fans will remember Robert Saleh using "fast and violent" to describe his hopes for Tennessee, all the way back in January.
Let ‘em know, Carnell! pic.twitter.com/b6vMO6DiD8
The phrasing has been used a few times since, but with the beginning of the season so near, it seems like Tennessee is actually beginning to implement it. Those words were present on the field yesterday, no doubt.
Tate repeating them once again confirms that this Tennessee team is prepared to bring the fire.
Given the Titans' struggles in yesterday's practice, this may seem like a moot point at first. Who cares how you think you're playing if you're actively being outplayed?
Yet, there may be some merit yet in Tennessee taking on such an aggressive mindset. Titans fans aren't all that far removed from Brian Callahan's most recent team; one that was criticized again and again for their distinct lack of fight and grit.
Tennessee's shutout loss to the Houston Texans in week four, 26-0, epitomized those failures. The entire point of bringing in a new leader was to do away with Callahan's failures on the sideline. It may not be such a bad thing to embrace this squad's self-imposed identity, even if they're not yet out of the rebuilding phase.
Assuming yesterday's practice reports were as telling as they seemed, the 49ers will have the upper hand in the preseason opener. But this is the first Titans team in a while that may benefit from having a hill to climb. In fact, they may even prefer it that way.

title: 4 Major Takeaways from Titans' Heated Joint Practice with 49ers: Day 3 Rookie Continues to Shine
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans and San Francisco 49ers held a heated joint practice on Tuesday. Both teams will square off again on Thursday night in a preseason contest at Levi's Stadium.
Tuesday's practice between the Titans and 49ers was incredibly physical, as there were multiple fights and it seemed like there was extracurricular activity after nearly every play. San Francisco clearly wanted to set the tone and get under Tennessee's skin.
Though tempers flaring was the main storyline of the day, there is still a lot to discuss from practice on Tuesday. Let's take a look at the key takeaways for the Titans.
After a quiet start to camp, Carmona has been making a ton of noise in recent practices , and Tuesday was no different. According to ESPN's Turron Davenport, the fifth-round rookie received early first-team reps at right guard during the scrimmage period against the 49ers. In practice, Carmona contributed a key block on a Cam Ward touchdown pass, though the rookie also committed a costly false start during an end-of-practice two-minute drill.
Tuesday marked the second straight practice Carmona worked with the starting offense, and head coach Robert Saleh praised the Arkansas product for earning his opportunities . However, Saleh also confirmed that right guard is still an open competition.
"You gotta earn it to get in there [with the first-team], but he's been doing a nice job," Saleh said about Carmona. "But like I said, with that right guard spot, we're gonna keep working to find the best player for it."
Carmona is definitely in the running for the starting right guard gig with Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater. We can now officially call this position battle a three-player race entering the preseason opener.
It was an up-and-down for quarterback Cam Ward and the offense. According to Davenport and Buck Reising of A to Z Sports, the passing game was in sync early , as Ward started with a few completions to wide receivers Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate. Rookie running back Nicholas Singleton also had a few nice runs .
However, it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. Will Levis threw an interception , Mitchell Trubisky struggled to evade pressure, and Ward also had his missteps. The Titans' QB1 tossed a pick-six to 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown and failed to lead Tennessee to a score on the aforementioned two-minute drill to end the day. Ward went 16-of-23 on the day , with a touchdown to Ridley and running back Tony Pollard, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com.
One guy who had a splendid day was wide receiver Xavier Restrepo, who led the team with five catches, including two touchdowns, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com. Restrepo is continuing to showcase his playmaking ability and is building a compelling roster case.
It's clear Brian Daboll's offense has a lot to work on, but it wasn't all bad at the same time either. The group should learn from Tuesday and use it to bolster their attack.
The Titans' secondary has had its struggles in camp containing Tate and Elic Ayomanor, but there hasn't been much panic. However, facing a new opponent on Tuesday, the unit didn't look much better.
ESPN 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner reported strong days for San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy and wide receivers Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling. Reising also noticed Robinson beating Titans safety Amani Hooker for a touchdown.
Additionally, Bonta Hill of NBC Sports Bay Area & California said that Purdy hit on a lot of downfield strikes on Tuesday, and David Lombardi of The San Francisco Standard jotted down multiple touchdowns for 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel during red-zone drills.
Though we're still early in the camp and the preseason, the Titans can't afford to be prone to allowing explosive plays in 2026, especially with the amount of money they committed to starting corners Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott. The secondary needs to step up sooner rather than later.
This was one of the most intense joint practices we've seen in a while. The benches cleared early in practice when 49ers cornerback Renardo Green shoved Wan'Dale Robinson out of bounds. Coaches were able to break things up, but that was a sign of things to come.
There were too many skirmishes and back-and-forths to include, but the major takeaway was offensive tackles Austin Deculus and Dan Moore Jr. getting ejected from practice. According to Nick Suss of The Tennessean, Deculus threw a punch at a 49ers defender within the first 10 minutes and was kicked out. About an hour later, Moore was also thrown out for getting into a fight with 49ers defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa.
San Francisco brought the heat, and though Tennessee responded, it's clear Saleh's squad was flustered at times. We should see growth from the Titans in this area, as the team is still pretty young and just needs more experience.
Saleh confirmed after practice that the Titans starters will play in the preseason contest on Thursday. Saleh added that he'll also leave the starters out there for more than a series, so they should get some good work in.
Overall, it wasn't an awful joint practice from the Titans, but it's evident that they have some stuff to clean up before Week 1. The 49ers have been a consistent playoff contender for nearly a decade, so Tuesday was a fantastic opportunity for the Titans to see where they stand with a few weeks to go in camp.

title: Tempers Flare in Titans Practice With 49ers as Tennessee's QBs Seriously Struggle
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans prepared for their preseason debut against the San Francisco 49ers this week by taking part in a joint practice out west. If today's unofficial meeting between the two teams is any indication, we could be in for a real mess on Thursday, and for more reasons than one.
Not only did tempers flare to an extreme degree in the practice, with both Austin Deculus and Dan Moore being outright ejected, but the Titans quarterbacks reportedly struggled to find their footing overall. Per Turron Davenport, Will Levis threw an interception to Jakob Robinson. Tennessee's long-time depth piece under center has had a rough offseason thus far.
Elsewhere, Cam Ward gave up a pick six to San Francisco's Upton Stout, missing a wide open Carnell Tate, according to Cesar Bass. The cherry on top was Mitch Trubisky being swarmed by the 49ers defense as, in Davenport's words, "No one stopped the pass rush."
Ward would ultimately end up escaping with two touchdowns, but to say that it sounds like a long day for Tennessee's offense overall would be an understatement. It's not quite fair to forge any real worries out of reported practice struggles, but you couldn't be blamed for suspecting that Thursday's game could pan out poorly for the Titans as a result.
Of course, Robert Saleh is fresh off of his latest stint serving as the 49ers' defensive coordinator. That means this practice, and more importantly Thursday's game, each serve as a bit of a homecoming for the head coach.
Having one of his offensive lineman be thrown out of a practice for throwing a punch probably wasn't Saleh's ideal start, but he and Tennessee have time to turn things around before their actual matchup with San Francisco.
Besides, on their home (practice) field facing off against a coach that just ditched their unit, it isn't a huge surprise that the 49ers defense came out and bared their teeth. After all, that bunch has been consistently known as one of the best in the entire NFL. Try not to take this news to heart, Titans fans.
However, everyone will be looking for a little more composure when Tennessee actually takes the field... to say the least. Preseason or not, throwing punches and picks won't cut it for a team expected to take a major leap this season.
Regardless of the eventual outcome, improvement from the personnel under center would go a long way to quiet the hearts of folks reading the practice reports from today. Levis, if he ends up with playing time, could use a leap following his shortcomings at Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage last week.
None of this is worth panicking over. At the same time, however, the team's optics were far from pretty coming out of this practice. All eyes are on Thursday's game.

title: Washington Preseason Opener Puts Roster Battles Under the Lights — Commanders Daily
full_text:
We have finally reached the point of training camp where we can break away from building roster evaluations primarily based on practice sessions and shift to real-time game situations. For the Washington Commanders , that means playing host to the Miami Dolphins Friday night at Northwest Stadium . Washington already had the opportunity to test their new schemes on both sides of the ball at joint practice on Wednesday , a morning the Commanders spent dominating the Dolphins . Now the test will shift to situational football mode, where the team can learn more about how well this group does under pressure. This particular game means more for the players involved in Washington’s unresolved roster and depth-chart battles that have been going on for the past couple of weeks. The team has serious competition at running back, receiver, and tight end, just to name a few offensive spots. They need the work to get through the difficult task of getting down to a 53-man roster in a few weeks. Standing out in practice gets you the shot on gameday; this Friday will be their opportunity to show that those flashes translate into their coach's vision once the game is at full speed. While nobody is winning or losing a roster spot solely because of one preseason opener, bubble players can certainly change the direction of their camp with a strong or poor showing. Friday's game will also begin a compressed evaluation period, during which the team will have to reduce the roster size from 91 to 53, leaving them with only two more games after Miami to figure things out. Now it's time to see if the camp storylines survive the lights.
long ball to Burks ✊ @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Hlb14ySbYg
Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley was asked Wednesday whether he intended to play starting quarterback Malik Willis on Friday; he was direct with his response. "I am, yeah. But like you said, things can change." Willis already witnessed Washington’s pressure firsthand during Wednesday’s joint practice session , when the Commanders repeatedly disrupted Miami’s offense. Friday could create different matchups, as players fighting for roster positions and situational roles take center stage, while many veterans look on. With Miami playing its starting quarterback, Washington's hungrier section of the roster will get an opportunity to make its case against legitimate NFL competition.

title: Commanders' Jayden Daniels Responds to Ongoing NIL Controversy
full_text:
Jayden Daniels has caught the ire of the football masses for the first time in his burgeoning professional career, and it isn't for a reason anyone would have first assumed, with training camp coming to a head and the NFL preseason approaching.
The Washington Commanders' star quarterback finds himself embroiled in an NIL controversy with LSU, the school with which he won the distinguished Heisman Memorial Trophy, as his camp is reportedly " deeply disappointed" and feels "profoundly disrespected " at the university's choice to hand his hallowed No. 5 to a recruit.
The Tigers weren't slow in fighting back against Daniels' cease-and-desist letter , a demand that the school stop using his name, image and likeness. New LSU head coach Lane Kiffin stood by a promise evidently made to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett regarding the number, but Daniels, attempting to save face amidst the brewing legal dispute, took to Instagram to personally address his priorities.
Jayden Daniels on the recent controversy via IG: #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Z99a3VHrlB
"Obviously, there are issues to be worked out between my team and LSU, and my hope is that it will get done privately," he said . "My sole personal focus is on Commanders football. I realize the business of football is unique, and I trust this can all be resolved."
The letter from Jayden Daniels’ attorney Adam Kenner to LSU football stating the program “must immediately cease and desist from any further use, display, publication, distribution, promotion, commercialization, or other exploitation of Mr. Daniels’ NIL in any manner or medium.” pic.twitter.com/QdX6Tl1evG
This, of course, arrives within hours of news surfacing that Daniels' side is reportedly requesting that LSU return the Heisman that he won for the SEC juggernaut.
BREAKING Source: Jayden Daniels has NOT asked #LSU to return the Heisman Trophy and the cease and desist letter was not filed in response to DJ Pickett wearing the number 5, but rather in an attempt to be compensated for use of his name, image and likeness, per sources. Full… pic.twitter.com/uTghfuhr8q
The LSU-Jayden Daniel saga takes another strange turn. Sources confirm Daniels’ camp wants LSU to return its copy of the Heisman Trophy—something LSU has no intention of doing. Daniels contacted LSU leadership before fall camp. Lane Kiffin has personally spoken to Daniels.…
Whatever's going on, Daniels sounds eager to keep the dialogue from leaking into in-season drama.
Daniels' attempt to keep the university from profiting off of the number he took to new heights makes sense if the school has no plans to respect what he was able to do as an upperclassman, but the tension is admittedly untimely.
He's been at the center of the Commanders' August training camp, to little surprise, looking smooth enough in a revamped offense to revive the hype he'd squandered over an unfortunate sophomore campaign. He's reading and reacting to defensive coverages with as much poise as ever, creating enough highlight throws and dashes to inflate the belief that he can tap back into the greatness he recently demonstrated as an Offensive Rookie of the Year-winning revelation.
The Commanders are set to take the field Friday in their preseason debut against the Miami Dolphins, where Daniels likely intends to open the 2026 season on his own terms as the healthy wielder of Washington's revitalized weapon assortment. He already spent Wednesday morning putting on a show in Ashburn .
But now, with some fans revising the history that Daniels made as a Tiger while providing their two cents on NIL residuals, there's little wonder as to why the Commanders' frontman is angling to sweep the can't-miss theatrics away from the public eye.
